title: fix(mp): reject transfer mode mismatches at registration
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4929/files) against `dev`.

## Summary

- install explicit registration guards only for transfer modes disabled by the server
- return requested and supported mode names instead of falling through to an unregistered request
- keep `auto` accepting both transfer paths and expose the configured mode in server status

## Broken invariant

A client/server transfer-mode mismatch should fail during KV-cache registration with an actionable error. Previously the server had no handler for the disabled registration request, so the client could only observe a generic missing-handler failure (or, before remote error frames, wait until timeout).

This preserves the existing wire request types and is compatible with older clients.

## Dependency

This is a stacked Draft on #4919, which carries the bounded remote handler-error frame. The implementation unique to this PR is commit `36229a5b`; its prerequisite commit is patch-equivalent to #4919. Once #4919 lands, the shared changes disappear from this diff.

## Test-first reproduction

The new suite initially failed at collection because the transfer-mode guard did not exist. The end-to-end ZMQ case then exposed and fixed the exact handler signature/return annotations required by the protocol registry.

The first full Buildkite run found a repository-wide architecture guard violation because this regression test constructed the raw ZMQ implementation directly. The test now constructs its client through `RequestClientFactory`, matching the public transport contract; the guard and the end-to-end mismatch case pass together.

## Validation

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/multiprocess/test_futures.py \
  tests/v1/multiprocess/test_mq.py \
  tests/v1/multiprocess/test_transfer_mode_guard.py \
  tests/v1/multiprocess/test_client.py
```

```text

```

```text
pre-commit run --all-files: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

A throughput benchmark is not applicable: this adds only a registration failure path and no successful store/retrieve hot-path work. The ZMQ regression asserts that the mismatch reaches the client within a 1-second bound.

Relates to #4759.

Validated from an isolated worktree at exact commit `36229a5b9c5b3d538df3499cb93cc880046c42d1` on macOS arm64 / Python 3.12.13 with the locally built LMCache native extensions.

title: fix(mp): return handler failures to clients
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4919/files) against `dev`.

## Summary

- add an exception terminal state to `MessagingFuture`
- return a versioned, bounded error frame when sync or blocking handlers fail
- return the same terminal error for unregistered request types
- keep full tracebacks server-side while sending only exception type and a message capped at 4096 characters

## Broken invariant

Every accepted MQ request must eventually complete its client future with either a response or an error. Previously, sync exceptions, blocking exceptions, and missing handlers were only logged by the server. The requester remained pending until its local timeout, obscuring the original failure and contributing to the silent registration/failure behavior described in #4759.

Healthy response frames are unchanged; the new marker is emitted only on failure.

## Test-first reproduction

title: fix(mp): isolate outbound request failures in shared polling loop
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4910/files) against `dev`.

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

ClientPollingLoop is shared by every MessageQueueClient in a process. Previously, a payload/version mismatch, encoding failure, or send_multipart exception could escape process_outbound_task, terminate that shared thread, leak a pending future, and strand unrelated clients.

This change:

- completes the affected MessagingFuture with the original exception;
- validates and encodes before publishing a request in pending_futures;
- rolls pending state back when socket send fails;
- keeps draining later requests after a per-request failure;
- guards the shared polling loop so an unexpected client exception cannot terminate it.

**Validation**:

- Linux Python 3.12, CPU-only: pytest -q tests/v1/multiprocess/test_mq.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_futures.py — **42 passed, 14 skipped** in 51.75s. Skips are device-dependent cases when no GPU is exposed.
- Focused regressions and existing loop lifecycle/dispatch coverage — **8 passed**.
- pre-commit for both changed Python files — SPDX, device rules, timeout rule, isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell, and mypy all passed (Rust hooks skipped because this PR changes no Rust files).
- In-memory outbound-path microbenchmark, 7 runs on Python 3.12:
  - 20,000 valid NOOP requests: median **13.965 ms** (**1.43M requests/s**).
  - 5,000 rejected malformed requests: median **7.719 ms** (**647.8k requests/s**).
  - The benchmark excludes queue construction and network I/O and is intended only as a reproducible control-path sanity check.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

The Linux run builds LMCache with NO_GPU_EXT=1; this is a message-queue control-plane correctness change and does not require GPU kernels.

title: fix(mp): bound per-client outbound polling
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4930/files) against `dev`.

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The process-wide client polling loop currently drains each client's outbound queue until it is empty. A producer that replenishes one queue faster than it is drained can monopolize the shared thread, delaying later clients and inbound responses indefinitely.

This change:

- limits each client to 64 outbound requests per polling turn;
- preserves FIFO order within each client;
- re-notifies the polling loop while queued work remains, so progress continues without waiting for another producer notification; and
- adds a regression test for the bounded, ordered drain contract.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Updated by merge commit `a8a494575335310f93a9e49f391e0363462fed12` against `dev` at `16df1bbb35c958e8353ddeeac66b4e6f89c64800`. The earlier #4910 stacked-prerequisite description is historical: upstream #4947 now supplies the per-request future-error completion. This merge preserves that handler exactly while retaining the bounded FIFO drain, continuation notification, and both regression-test sets.

**Latest merge checks:** applicable pre-commit hooks passed on both PR files, as did Python syntax and an AST comparison of the upstream encode/send/exception handler. No fresh runtime pass is claimed: local dependency-import preflights timed out, and CPU-only jk01 attempts were rejected by the source-provenance guard because the environment imported an installed LMCache rather than the merge snapshot. title: test(serde): wait for observable TurboQuant stores
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4923/files) against `dev`.

## Summary

- make the TurboQuant StorageManager round-trip tests wait for backend-visible stores
- only treat a store as complete after the controller and L1 cleanup have also settled
- cover both MockL2Adapter object counts and final FSL2Adapter files

## Why

Buildkite build 8657 for #4912 failed `test_turboquant_fs_storage_manager_roundtrip[turboquant_k3v4_nc-0.85]` because the test observed zero stored files. The store controller removes pending keys before it increments the in-flight count, leaving a short zero/zero transition where the old predicate could return before any object reached L2. This is unrelated to #4912 itself.

The new predicates anchor completion on an observable L2 result first, then require the queue and L1 lock/temporary counters to drain. This follows the same pattern already used by the serde end-to-end tests.

## Tests

- `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy uvx pre-commit run --files tests/v1/distributed/serde/test_turboquant.py` — all hooks passed
- L20 / CUDA, Python 3.10: patched Mock-L2 + FS-L2 matrix, all four TurboQuant presets — **8 passed in 19.20s**
- unpatched L20 reproduction, FS-L2 all four presets ×20 — **75 passed, 5 failed** in 23m39s
- unpatched L20 reproduction, FS-L2 `turboquant_k3v4_nc` ×50 — **49 passed, 1 failed** in 22m57s

- patched L20 validation, FS-L2 `turboquant_k3v4_nc` ×50 — **50 passed** in 1m12s

The failures in both unpatched stress runs are the premature completion symptom fixed here. These are correctness stress results, not throughput benchmarks.

title: feat(nixl): add IBM_SCALE backend support and fix NIXL transfer performance
body:
Add IBM Storage Scale (`IBM_SCALE`) to all NIXL backend allowlists and fix
several performance bugs in the NIXL transfer path that are exposed by
`io_uring`-backed backends (IBM_SCALE, GDS).

1. Add IBM_SCALE to allowlists
   - `nixl_store_dynamic_l2_adapter.py`: `_VALID_DYNAMIC_BACKENDS` (via `FILE_DYNAMIC_BACKENDS`)
   - `nixl_store_l2_adapter.py`: `_VALID_NIXL_BACKENDS`, `_FILE_BACKENDS`

2. Fix 10 ms polling floor in `post_non_blocking` / `_post_non_blocking`
   Add a 20-iteration spin-check before falling back to a 1 ms cooperative
   sleep. Move the sleep before `check_xfer_state` so a transfer completing
   on the first poll exits immediately without paying an extra sleep.
   Eliminates the ~10 ms floor that dominated latency for `io_uring` backends.

3. Concurrent store via `asyncio.gather` in `_execute_store_in_the_loop`
   Reserve all keys under the lock first, then launch all
   `dynamic_store_file` coroutines concurrently. Per-key failure isolation
   via `return_exceptions=True`. Matches the existing concurrent load path.

4. Fix `_open_flags()`: `O_RDWR` → `O_WRONLY` (store) / `O_RDONLY` (load)
   `O_RDWR` is ambiguous for backends that infer write intent from the fd
   access mode (IBM_SCALE uses this to select the right GPFS prefetch
   hint). `O_WRONLY`/`O_RDONLY` is also better POSIX practice.

5. Move `os.stat` outside the lock in secondary lookup
   `_secondary_lookup_locked` called `os.stat` while holding `_lock`,
   blocking concurrent store/load on slow/remote filesystems. Refactored
   to a two-lock, one-stat pattern: collect missing keys under lock, stat
   them unlocked, then commit found entries under lock. Removes
   `_secondary_lookup_locked` entirely.

Refs: ai-dynamo/nixl#2134

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Enables `IBM_SCALE` as a valid backend in LMCache's static and dynamic NIXL
adapters. Without this, LMCache raises a `ValueError` at config validation
time even when the IBM_SCALE plugin is installed. The accompanying
performance fixes (items 2–5) benefit all fast `io_uring` backends — GDS
users also see reduced TTFT.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Items 2–5 are independent of IBM_SCALE and improve the general NIXL transfer
  path. They can be reviewed/merged separately if preferred.
- The companion upstream NIXL plugin PR is ai-dynamo/nixl#2265.

**If applicable**:

- [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [ ] this PR contains unit tests

title: [good-first-issue] memory: reject non-positive size in AddressManager (#5115)
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Closes #5115
Refs #3372

`AddressManager.allocate()` and `batched_allocate()` document that `size` must be
greater than zero, but they never checked it. A zero-byte request corrupted the
explicit free list instead of failing:

* `allocate(0)` carved out a zero-length block; freeing it inserted a
  zero-sized entry whose neighbours could never be coalesced again.
  `get_free_size()` kept reporting the whole heap as free while the next
  full-heap allocation failed with "no memory is available".
* `batched_allocate(0, n)` raised `ZeroDivisionError` (`block.size // aligned_size`).
  `TensorMemoryAllocator` only translates `RuntimeError`, so the exception
  escaped to `LMCacheEngine.store()` / `store_layer()`.

### Reporting the rejection correctly

The first iteration of this PR raised `RuntimeError` (the exception the
allocation stack uses for "out of memory"), and @chrisyifanjin showed that this is
the wrong signal — the stack does not merely fail, it reacts:

| | `busy_loop=False` | `busy_loop=True` |
|---|---|---|
| 10 chunks cached, one `allocate(0)` | all 10 evicted (`hot_cache: 10 -> 0`), returns `None` | never returns; "Local cpu memory is under pressure" every 0.1 s |

A zero-byte request is a caller bug, so this PR now:

1. raises **`ValueError`** from `AddressManager.allocate()` / `batched_allocate()`.
   A bad argument reported as `ValueError` is already the convention in this
   allocator API — `MixedMemoryAllocator.allocate` documents `ValueError` for an
   unsupported `fmt`.
2. makes sure the engine never asks for an empty chunk: **`store()` and
   `store_layer()` skip degenerate ranges (`end <= start`)**, which is where the
   zero-byte request came from in the first place (a leading/trailing/double
   separator produces an empty range).

Together the invalid size can no longer reach the allocator, and if it ever does
it fails loudly instead of emptying the cache or spinning.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:
- This is my first PR to LMCache 🙇 please be gentle.
- The behaviour change is deliberate and covered by tests: a zero-byte request
  is a programming error, so it raises `ValueError` rather than degrading into
  `None` (which every storage backend interprets as memory pressure).
- `batched_allocate(size, 0)` with a *valid* size still returns an empty list, as
  documented and covered by the existing `test_batch_size_zero`. The
  `batch_size < 0` guard from #5061 is intentionally left as `RuntimeError`; its
  `-> None` behaviour is asserted by `test_tensor_allocator_negative_batch_size`,
  so changing it would be a separate decision.
- I considered guarding `free()` instead (it is the function that inserts the bad
  zero-sized block), but with `allocate` rejecting non-positive sizes the
  allocator can no longer produce such a block.
- Tests: `pytest -q tests/v1/test_address_manager.py tests/v1/test_memory_management.py
  tests/v1/storage_backend/test_local_cpu_backend.py` → 175 passed, 3 skipped;
  `pytest -q tests/v1/test_cache_engine.py --timeout=300 -k "(paged_mem_leak or
  paged_store_offset or paged_store_kv_tensors_mask or paged_retrieve_after_eviction or
  force_store_wait or paged_same_retrieve_store or store or retrieve) and not remote"`
  → 31 passed. The `remote`-parametrised cases of `test_paged_mem_leak` fail with
  `TimeoutError` in my environment; they fail identically on unmodified `dev`
  (verified with `git stash`), so it is a missing remote cache server here, not a
  regression.
- `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — all green
  (`cargo` is not installed in my environment).

title: [good-first-issue] distributed: convert f-string log calls to %-format
body:
Follow-up step for the G004 rollout in #5118. #5125 enabled `G004` repo-wide with temporary `per-file-ignores` for the not-yet-migrated files, and the plan agreed there is to remove those entries directory by directory as each area is cleaned up.

This does that for `lmcache/v1/distributed/`, the last two files under it that were still ignored:

- `l2_adapters/bigtable_l2_adapter.py` (5 call sites)
- `transfer_channel/impl/mooncake_te_impl.py` (4 call sites)

and deletes both `per-file-ignores` entries, so the directory can no longer regress. Together with `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/` (already clean), both directories that enforce SLF now enforce G004 as well.

Format style only, no behaviour change. Format specifiers were chosen from each variable's type annotation per `docs/coding_standards.md` 7.4:

| Variable | Source of truth | Spec |
|---|---|---|
| `qual` | key of `shards_raw: dict[str, tuple[bytes, int]]` | `%s` |
| `ts`, `max_ts` | `int` value slot of that dict (`cell.timestamp_micros`) | `%d` |
| `(max_ts - ts) / 1e6` | true division, original used `:.2f` | `%.2f` |
| `key_str`, `rk_str` | `.decode("utf-8")` | `%s` |
| `size` | `len(obj.byte_array)` | `%d` |
| `limit_bytes` | `int(...)` | `%d` |
| `column_name` | `column_name: str = "data"` | `%s` |
| `_remote_session_id` | ctor param `remote_session_id: str` | `%s` |
| `batch_id` | key type of `self._tasks: dict[int, tuple]` | `%d` |
| `advertise_host` | `@property -> str` | `%s` |
| `mooncake_te_port`, `get_rpc_port()` | `@property -> int` | `%d` |
| `_protocol`, `_device_id` | `collect_env_var() -> tuple[str, str]` | `%s` |

All nine messages render byte-identically to the f-strings they replace.

Two details worth flagging for review:

- In `"...diff is %.2fs)"` the trailing `s` is a literal second-unit suffix, not part of the specifier.
- `get_rpc_port()` is intentionally left as a call in the argument list. Lazy formatting defers interpolation, not argument evaluation, so this preserves the existing behaviour rather than making an unrelated change.

One message changed shape but not content: the `Column ... not found in row ...` warning previously split mid-phrase across two implicitly concatenated literals. Dropping the `f` prefixes freed enough width to fit a single literal within 88 columns, matching the already-converted call a few lines above it. Every other implicit concatenation is preserved as-is.

## Testing

- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean; `isort`, `codespell` and `mypy --config-file=pyproject.toml` clean on the changed files.
- `ruff check --isolated --select G004 lmcache/v1/distributed/` now reports 0 findings (was 9).
- Verified the ignore removal is effective rather than cosmetic: a temporary `logger.info(f"...")` added to `bigtable_l2_adapter.py` is reported as `G004` with this change and passes without it. Probe removed afterwards.
- `pytest tests/v1/distributed/` gives 790 passed, 80 skipped on a CPU-only build (`NO_GPU_EXT=1 pip install -e . --no-build-isolation`, torch 2.14.0+cpu, Python 3.12). `tests/v1/distributed/test_bigtable_l2_adapter.py` gives 14 passed.
- Because `PLE1206` (too-few logging args) is not in `select`, a dropped argument or wrong specifier would only surface at runtime, so each of the 9 sites was additionally rendered both ways with representative values and compared: all 9 identical.

No new tests: the enabled `G004` rule is the regression guard for this issue class, matching the previous merged conversions (#4477, #5094, #5014, #4319, #4478), none of which carried tests.

## Note

Unrelated to this change, but spotted while working in the same config block: `lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/infinistore_adapter.py` is still listed in the `G004` `per-file-ignores` even though it is already clean. #4477 landed after #5125 and did not remove its entry. Ruff does not error on redundant ignores so nothing is broken, and I left it out of this PR to keep the scope to one directory. Happy to send it separately.

Part of #5118

title: feat: Add AWS Trainium device support
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adds LMCache support for AWS Trainium via the Neuron SDK, enabling KV cache CPU
offload on Neuron hardware, including alongside Dynamo disaggregated inference in a
MultiConnector setup where NeuronNixlConnector handles prefill-to-decode KV
transfer over NIXL/EFA.

GPU code paths are unchanged from `dev`; everything Neuron-specific is in its own
module or behind a device check.

**Changes:**

- `platform/neuron/__init__.py`: Detect Neuron via native `torch.neuron`
  (SDK >= 2.27) or the legacy `torch_neuronx` shim. Adds a wrapper supplying the
  `set_device` / `device_count` / `Stream` / `current_stream` that `torch.neuron`
  lacks.
- `platform/base/device_spec.py`: New `adapt_torch_module()` hook, returning the
  module unchanged for every other backend. Neuron wraps rather than monkey-patches
  `torch.neuron`, which is process-global and shared with other libraries.
- `gpu_connector/neuron_kv_staging.py`: New. Stages selected paged-KV blocks
  between device memory and a reusable host buffer, one `narrow` + `copy_` per
  contiguous run per layer, reusing the existing CPU pack/unpack. Neuron rejects
  device→device copies between differently-sized parents
  (`nrt_tensor_copy status=2`), so the blocks cannot be gathered into a compact
  device buffer; `index_select` is avoided because it costs time proportional to
  the whole cache.
- `platform/torch_ops.py`: HND layout support (`NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS`,
  `NL_X_NB_TWO_NH_BS_HS`), replacing a `NotImplementedError`.
- `integration/vllm/utils.py`: Force the HND layout hint on Neuron. vllm-neuron
  allocates heads-before-block-size but reports vLLM's generic NHD default, so
  detection read `NH` as `BS` and every store died on a shape mismatch.
- `integration/vllm/vllm_v1_adapter.py`: `start_load_kv` returned early whenever
  `attn_metadata` was None, which it always is on vllm-neuron — so loads were
  silently dead while stores ran. The value was never actually read. The check is
  kept for all other platforms, so CUDA is unchanged.
- `gpu_connector/{__init__,gpu_connectors}.py`: Route `"neuron"` to the paged-mem
  connectors; stream helpers that return the original `torch.cuda.Stream` /
  `torch.cuda.stream` on CUDA; devices without a pointer kernel branch out of
  `_initialize_pointers` before the pointer path, which is unchanged. Staging is
  enabled post-construction to keep it out of the shared constructors.
  `use_layerwise` and blending are rejected on Neuron.

**Two correctness fixes found on hardware:**

- Transfers are block-granular but the unpack fills only the slots it is asked to,
  so the tail block of any request not a multiple of `block_size` was scattered
  back with stale buffer contents over live KV. Unfilled staged regions are now
  seeded from the device first.
- `skip_prefix_n_tokens` was computed at both call sites and dropped on the Neuron
  path. Those tokens live in blocks prefix caching shares between requests, so
  writing them races with other requests' reads. Now a required argument.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Validated on trn2.3xlarge (single node) and 2x trn2.48xlarge (1P1D), vllm-neuron
0.24 + Dynamo, SDK 2.31, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. 1P1D needs EFA — trn2.3xlarge has
no `/dev/infiniband` and NeuronNixlConnector fails there at `agent.registerMem`.
Requires the Dynamo protocol registration from
https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13771.

### Verified results

Staging round trip on device, compared at slot granularity
(`neuron_kv_staging_benchmark.py --verify`):

```
verify: OK -- 1199 token slots across 38 blocks round tripped exactly on 16 layers
(2 partially covered block(s) kept their unmapped slots); 474 blocks untouched
```

End to end, repeated prompt, vLLM prefix caching **off** so only LMCache can serve
the hit:

| | single node, 312 tok | 1P1D, 148 tok |
|---|---|---|
| req 1 | `computed 0, hit 0`; stored 312/312 in 187 ms | `computed 0, hit 0`; stored 148/148 in 228 ms |
| req 2 | `computed 0, hit 312`; retrieved 312/312 in 11.6 ms | `computed 0, hit 148`; retrieved 148/148 in 9.5 ms |
| TTFT | — | 0.623 s → 0.287 s (2.2x) |

`Inference Engine computed tokens: 0` is the load actually happening — vLLM
contributed nothing. Warm requests are byte-identical across repeats.

In the 1P1D column each worker stores and hits its **own** `local_cpu` cache;
prefill→decode KV transfer is NeuronNixlConnector's job, not LMCache's. Sharing a
cache *between* engines needs a shared tier (`remote_url` / the LMCache server),
which is untested here — `local_cpu` and `local_disk` both index in memory and so
are per-process.

**Three caveats worth knowing:**

1. `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` is `null` on some vLLM paths even
   when LMCache served the whole prefix. Use the `LMCache hit tokens` /
   `Retrieved N out of N` log lines instead.
2. With `--enable-prefix-caching` on, vLLM's block cache serves the repeat and
   LMCache's contribution is not separable (measured: `computed 144` of 148, with
   LMCache asked for 3). Turn it off to attribute anything to LMCache.
3. vllm-neuron pads prefill into fixed graph buckets, so loading KV does not shrink
   the prefill graph. Against pure recompute on a 1B model, offload is slower below
   ~2.5k tokens and 1.12x faster above, where the load drops into a smaller bucket.
   The retrieve is ~11 ms of a ~0.45 s request, so the limit is bucketing, not
   transfer speed.

### Reproducible configuration

Prerequisites: [vllm-neuron 0.24](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-neuron/blob/release-0.24.0.1.1.0/docs/getting-started/setup-guide.md),
[Dynamo with NeuronNixlConnector](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13771),
2x trn2.48xlarge with EFA for 1P1D.

`/tmp/lmcache.yaml`:
```yaml
chunk_size: 32
local_cpu: true
max_local_cpu_size: 4.0
save_unfull_chunk: true
```

Single node (`NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES` must be left unset — vLLM rejects it under
its multiprocess executor, though raw torch scripts require it):

```bash
export LMCACHE_CONFIG_FILE=/tmp/lmcache.yaml
export FI_EFA_ENABLE_SHM_TRANSFER=0 NEURON_SKIP_EFA_AFFINITY=1
export NEURON_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0

python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --no-enable-prefix-caching --port 8000 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1Dynamic","kv_connector_module_path":"lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_connector_v1","kv_role":"kv_both"}'
```

1P1D: as above per node with `python3 -m dynamo.vllm`,
`--disaggregation-mode prefill|decode`, `--tensor-parallel-size 2`,
`NEURON_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1`, `--block-size 16`, etcd/nats on the prefill node,
and a `MultiConnector` wrapping `NeuronNixlConnector` (`kv_producer` /
`kv_consumer`, `backends: ["LIBFABRIC"]`) plus `LMCacheConnectorV1Dynamic`
(`kv_both`). Frontend: `python3 -m dynamo.frontend --http-port 8000`.

title: feat: add native 3FS (HF3FS) L2 storage backend
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a **native C++ 3FS (Fire-Flyer File System) L2 storage backend** to LMCache,
giving it high-performance distributed KV-cache storage backed directly by the
3FS **Usrbio** API.

### What this PR does / why we need it

- **What:** A complete 3FS storage backend stack — a native C++ connector, a pybind wrapper,
  a Python L2 adapter (config + factory registration), a build profile, unit/integration tests,
  and user documentation.
- **Why:** 3FS (from DeepSeek) is a high-performance distributed file system well suited
  to large, warm/cold KV-cache tiers and cross-node cache sharing. LMCache previously had no
  native 3FS backend; KV caches had to go through slower, higher-latency paths. By performing
  I/O through the 3FS Usrbio API with **GIL-free, multi-worker parallel read/write**, this PR:
  - Reduces TTFT on cold-cache misses.
  - Increases throughput for large KV caches via batched ops and multi-path balancing.
  - Provides accelerated `EXISTS` checks without hitting the filesystem (in-memory key buffer).

## How it works

The feature is layered; each layer only exposes a narrow public interface:

```
                    Hf3fsL2AdapterConfig + factory "hf3fs"
                                   │
                    hf3fs_l2_adapter.py (NativeConnectorL2Adapter)
                                   │
                    lmcache_hf3fs CppExtension (pybind.cpp → LMCacheHf3fsClient)
                                   │
                    Hf3fsConnector (connector.h/.cpp)  ── 3FS Usrbio API
```

1. **Native connector** `csrc/storage_backends/hf3fs/connector.{h,cpp}`
   - `Hf3fsConnector : ConnectorBase<WorkerHf3fsConn>` implements
     `do_single_get/set/exists/delete` and `do_batch_exists`.
   - **Per-worker connection state** (`WorkerHf3fsConn`) keeps **dual Ior + dual Iov**
     (separate read/write rings) per thread. Separate Ior are required because the 3FS Ior
     cannot handle read and write operations simultaneously; per-thread Iov avoids
     synchronization and IB-registration complexity.
   - **Multi-path load balancing:** objects are distributed across the configured
     `base_paths` based on `chunk_hash`.
   - **Accelerated `EXISTS` (key buffer):** an in-memory `sharded_flat_hash_set<std::string>`
     (built on `absl::flat_hash_set`, with per-shard locks for high write throughput) is
     populated once by scanning the base paths at startup. `do_batch_exists` then answers from
     the buffer without touching 3FS, only falling back to the FS when the buffer is disabled.
   - **Per-op worker lanes:** optional `per_op_workers` (`lookup/retrieve/store/delete`) via
     `WorkerPoolConfig` for isolated worker pools per operation class.

2. **Pybind:** `pybind.cpp` exposes the connector through a `LMCacheHf3fsClient` module.

3. **Python adapter:** `hf3fs_l2_adapter.py` adds `Hf3fsL2AdapterConfig` and registers the
   `"hf3fs"` adapter type + factory, backed by the existing `NativeConnectorL2Adapter`.

4. **Build profile:** `hf3fs.py` builds `lmcache.lmcache_hf3fs` when `BUILD_HF3FS=1`, linking
   against `libhf3fs_api_shared` and the system Abseil libs
   (`absl_hash`, `absl_city`, `absl_int128`, `absl_raw_hash_set`); Abseil availability is
   detected before building.

### Configuration example

```
[lmcache]
type = "hf3fs"
mount_point = "/3fs/stage"
base_paths  = "/3fs/stage/lmcache/p1,/3fs/stage/lmcache/p2"
num_workers = 8
# optional tunables:
ior_entries     = 256     # [128, 1024]
io_depth        = 0       # [-128, 128]
iov_size        = 209715200  # 200 MB, [100MB, 2GB]
enable_key_buffer = true
# per_op_workers = {"lookup": 2, "store": 4}
```

### Dependencies & build

- Requires the **3FS Usrbio SDK** (`hf3fs_usrbio.h`, `libhf3fs_api_shared.so`) and system
  **Abseil** (`libabsl-dev`).
- Build:
  ```bash
  export HF3FS_INCLUDE_DIR=/usr/include
  export HF3FS_LIB_DIR=/usr/lib
  BUILD_HF3FS=1 pip install -e . --verbose
  ```

### Testing

- `tests/v1/distributed/test_hf3fs_l2_adapter.py`
  - Config/validation tests (ranges, mount/base-path checks, per-op workers, key-buffer).
  - Native-connector tests: client creation, single/batch put-get roundtrip, exists, delete,
    multi-path distribution, persistence across clients.
  - L2-adapter integration: store/lookup, load, delete, end-to-end workflow, multi-object batch.
- Result on a live 3FS mount (`HF3FS_MOUNT_POINT=/3fs/stage`): **33 passed, 1 skipped**
  (the skipped case is the "extension absent" failure-path test).

### Notes for reviewers

- New public API is minimal: one connector class + one adapter config/factory.
- Files: `csrc/storage_backends/hf3fs/*`, `hf3fs_l2_adapter.py`, `hf3fs.py`,
  `test_hf3fs_l2_adapter.py`, `docs/source/mp/l2_storage/{hf3fs.rst, supported_storages.rst,
  remote_and_distributed.rst}`.

Signed-off-by: Ruyi Zhang <ruyi.zhang@samsung.com>
Co-authored-by: Wenwen Chen <wenwen.chen@samsung.com>

title: [Fix][MP] Don't store MTP's speculative scratch block as a Mamba state
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #4984

`LMCacheMPConnector` stores a garbage recurrent state for the last full chunk of a prompt when a Mamba/GDN hybrid runs with MTP, so every later hit on that prefix resumes from a bogus state. Root cause (details in https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/4984#issuecomment-5569045977):

- With MTP, vLLM's `_mamba_block_aligned_split` merges the prompt's last full block and its tail into one prefill step, so no Mamba state is ever written for that block boundary. Without MTP these are two steps with a stop at the boundary.
- vLLM handles this in its own block list: it writes the null block into that slot and moves the speculative scratch block that sat there to the tail. But `new_block_ids` only carries the tail, so the connector's tracker keeps the moved block at its old slot and hands it to the server as that chunk's recurrent state. No kernel ever wrote that block.

```
    tokens      0        1616       3232       4538
                |----------|--------------------|
    MTP on      [ step 1  ][       step 2       ]
    state slot       0                     2       <- slot 1 never written
    Mamba list  [ A ,      NULL ,      C , ...]  (vLLM's own list)
    tracker     [ A ,       S1 ,       C , ...]  (LMCache's copy, before this PR)
```

The fix is in `LMCacheMPRequestTracker.append_block_ids`: a block is never listed at two slots of one request, so a reported id that is already in the list means vLLM moved it. The tracker sets the old slot to 0 before appending. The server's existing `all_null_chunk_masks` then skips that chunk's recurrent object, and because a chunk hit needs every object group, the next lookup stops one chunk earlier instead of loading a bogus state. Models without speculative decoding never re-report a block, so this is a no-op for them.

Verified on 2x RTX 5090, vLLM 0.28.0, FlashAttention, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, `--mamba-cache-mode align --separate-object-groups`, 2408-token prompt, store -> `reset_prefix_cache` -> identical request at temperature 0:

| MTP | block = chunk | `--max-num-batched-tokens` | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| on, 4 draft tokens | 560 | 1119 | output differs, hit 2240 | output identical, hit 1680 |
| off | 544 | 1087 | output identical, hit 2176 | output identical, hit 2176 |

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Attention backend independent; #4253 is a separate attention-side issue.
- This issue only happens when MTP enabled for hybrid models, and it's across attention backends

body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4934/files) against `dev`.

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

A malformed DEALER peer could terminate the shared MessageQueueServer polling thread before handler-level exception isolation ran:

- a request with fewer than three frames hit an assertion;
- a request with an undecodable MessagePack request type raised before handler dispatch.

Both cases left otherwise healthy clients timing out. This change validates the frame count and isolates request-type decoding failures, logs the malformed request, and continues polling.

The regression test sends both malformed header variants, waits deterministically until the server processes each one, and then verifies that a healthy NOOP request still succeeds and the worker thread remains alive.

title: fix(mp): make warm-prefetch completion consumption exactly once
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4911/files) against `dev`.

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

WarmPrefetchJobs documents completion as exactly-once, but poll previously performed get, query, and pop as separate critical sections without checking which caller removed the job. Two concurrent pollers can both observe an immediately completed handle and both return COMPLETED.

This change makes the atomic job-table pop choose the single completion consumer. A concurrent loser now returns UNKNOWN, preserving the documented contract without holding the job-table lock across storage-manager polling.

title: fix(mp): harden liveness reaper fanout
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4912/files) against `dev`.

title: feat(mp): support configurable null block IDs
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**

Some serving engines use block `0` for real data and a different integer for absent sparse state. LMCache MP currently assumes block `0` is always null, which can incorrectly skip valid PAGE data.

This PR adds one server-wide option:

```bash
lmcache server --null-block-id -1 --separate-object-groups
```

`--null-block-id` defaults to `0`, so existing vLLM deployments keep their current behavior. ATOM uses `-1` globally, and explicitly enables separate object groups so dense PAGE data and sparse recurrent STATE have independent presence.

**Concrete example**

```text
              chunk 0   chunk 1   chunk 2   chunk 3
PAGE ids         0         1         2         3
STATE ids       -1        -1        -1         7

--null-block-id -1

PAGE           STORE     STORE     STORE     STORE
STATE          SKIP      SKIP      SKIP      STORE
```

Here PAGE block `0` is valid, while STATE `-1` means no checkpoint exists. A global sentinel works because all block-ID lists sent by an engine use the same absent-value convention. Python `None` is not used as a sentinel.

**How skipped copies work**

LMCache already supports skipping chunk copies, so this PR does not add another skip mechanism to `object_group_transfer.py`.

- Store computes the all-null mask using the configured sentinel, does not reserve/commit those objects, and passes `None` for them. The existing D2H loop skips each `None` object without launching a copy kernel.
- Retrieve uses the existing object/window prefix skip and `skip_first_n_tokens` handling. It starts copying from the first object/token that is actually needed.
- Block-ID staging keeps its existing slice-only behavior. A null ID may remain in the staged tensor, but skipped entries are outside every launched kernel's block-ID range and are never dereferenced.

**Object grouping requirement**

Sparse STATE and dense PAGE cannot share an object group: object presence is the retrieve-side hit signal, so a PAGE hit must not imply that a missing STATE checkpoint exists. This PR does not silently change grouping. Connectors that use sparse state must explicitly start the server with `--separate-object-groups`.

Kernel groups packed into one sparse object must also share a presence domain. ATOM satisfies this contract because its native STATE image is indivisible: every STATE ordinal is absent in the same prefix chunks and present at the same checkpoint endpoint. The companion ATOM PR includes a regression test for this invariant. Supporting independently sparse kernel groups requires an explicit presence-domain model or per-kernel transfer masks; that general design is tracked in [#5288](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/5288).

**Review notes**

- The null sentinel is global configuration; `EngineGroupInfo` and the gRPC registration protocol are unchanged.
- Per-chunk store completion events are in the separate PR [#5272](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/5272).
- The companion ATOM consumer is [ROCm/ATOM#2250](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/2250).
- The current `dev` default for `--separate-object-groups` is `False`, so ATOM's launch documentation passes it explicitly.

**Validation**

- `764 passed, 39 skipped` for `tests/v1/multiprocess` (GPU alias test run separately).
- `119 passed` in focused config, sparse transfer, lookup, grouping, and event-path tests.
- `23 passed` in focused gRPC/protobuf and group-serialization tests.
- `2 passed` in real ROCm multiprocess PAGE/STATE round-trip tests.
- Matching ATOM branch: `87 passed` for MP connector/layout tests.
- Ruff lint/format, isort, mypy on changed source files, `compileall`, protobuf regeneration, and `git diff --check` pass.

# Support LMCache in UnifiedRadixCache ## Overall flowchart: ## Related PRs - Design doc: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/5041 - `LMCacheUnifiedRadixCache` implemention: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38652 ## Functional validation The request sequence below was exercised on both model families. | Step | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Qwen-3.5-27B | Purpose | |---|---:|---:|---| | Initial request | 716 input / 512 output tokens | 726 input / 512 output tokens | Populate the cache | | Longer request sharing the same prefix | 1,021 input / 474 output tokens | 1,025 input / 512 output tokens | Verify prefix reuse | | Repeat the longer request | Tested | Tested | Verify the warm path | | Flush radix cache and repeat | Tested | Tested | Verify flush and cold fallback | ## Accuracy Evaluation configuration: - 200 examples; - 32 threads; - 5-shot prompting; - temperature `0`; - maximum output length `2,048` tokens. | Model | Evaluation | Baseline | LMCache cold | LMCache warm | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | GSM8K | 0.975 | 0.96 | 0.97 | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Mixed-prefix GSM8K | 0.985 | 0.985 | 0.975 | | Qwen-3.5-27B | GSM8K | 0.745 | 0.73 | 0.75 | | Qwen-3.5-27B | Mixed-prefix GSM8K | 0.86 | 0.865 | 0.85 | The observed score variation is at most 1.5 percentage points across the sampled runs, with no consistent degradation between cold and warm LMCache paths. ## Serving benchmark Benchmark configuration: | Parameter | Value | |---|---:| | Dataset | Random | | Requests | 256 | | Input length | 10,000 tokens | | Output length | 128 tokens | | Request rate | Unlimited | | Maximum concurrency | 32 | | Seed | 42 | | Warm-up requests | 0 | `LMCache write` is first-run measurements with zero cache hits. `LMCache FS hit` restore reusable prompt KV from filesystem storage. The reported overall hit rate is lower than 100% because not every processed token is reusable prompt KV; all cached tokens in the hit runs came from the corresponding storage backend. ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Scenario | Total throughput (tok/s) | vs. baseline | Mean E2E (ms) | vs. baseline | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Overall cache hit | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Baseline | 20,922.92 | - | 7,941.69 | - | 997.56 | 104.71 | 0.0% | | LMCache write | 19,565.31 | -6.5% | 8,488.73 | +6.9% | 1,103.30 | 114.56 | 0.0% | | LMCache FS hit | **31,479.97** | **+50.5%** | **5,255.81** | **-33.8%** | **697.64** | **69.58** | 97.0% | ### Qwen-3.5-27B | Scenario | Total throughput (tok/s) | vs. baseline | Mean E2E (ms) | vs. baseline | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Overall cache hit | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Baseline | 36,457.79 | - | 4,548.11 | - | 921.35 | 54.63 | 0.0% | | LMCache write | 29,477.15 | -19.1% | 5,632.40 | +23.8% | 1,187.59 | 71.28 | 0.0% | | LMCache FS hit | **59,801.40** | **+64.0%** | **2,747.14** | **-39.6%** | **737.82** | **31.48** | 96.9% | ## Key observations - LMCache filesystem hits increased total token throughput by **50.5%** on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and **64.0%** on Qwen-3.5-27B relative to baseline. - LMCache filesystem hits reduced mean end-to-end latency by **33.8%** and **39.6%**, respectively. - Mean TPOT improved by **33.5%** on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and **42.4%** on Qwen-3.5-27B with LMCache filesystem hits. - The zero-hit write path introduces measurable overhead. The impact is model-dependent: total throughput decreased by **6.5%** on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and **19.1%** on Qwen-3.5-27B. ## Reproduction commands
start commands - start sglang only with radix cache ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8021 \ --served-model-name sglang_test \ --tp-size 8 \ --page-size 256 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 ``` - start sglang with lmcache ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8021 \ --served-model-name sglang_test \ --tp-size 8 \ --page-size 256 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \ --enable-unified-lmcache \ --lmcache-config-file lmcache.yaml ``` - lmcache config ```yaml # lmcache.yaml mp_host: 127.0.0.1 mp_port: 15555 extra_config: lmcache.mp.mq_timeout: 300 lmcache.mp.heartbeat_interval: 10 ``` - start lmcache mp server ```bash lmcache server \ --host localhost \ --port 15555 \ --l1-size-gb 300 \ --max-gpu-workers 8 \ --max-cpu-workers 8 \ --eviction-policy LRU \ --chunk-size 256 \ --separate-object-groups \ --l2-adapter '{ "type": "fs_native", "base_path": "", "num_workers": 16, "use_odirect": false, "max_capacity_gb": 800, "eviction": { "eviction_policy": "LRU", "trigger_watermark": 0.9, "eviction_ratio": 0.1 } }' ```

title: [Bugfix][Platform] Retain exported IPC events so peers can import their handles
body:
## Problem

`DefaultEventIPCBackend.export_event()` hands out an IPC handle and immediately drops the only reference to the event it came from:

```python
def export_event(self, event: object, device: object) -> bytes:
    """Serialize ``event`` into a process-portable IPC handle."""
    return event.ipc_handle()   # event is destroyed on return
```

The handle is only meaningful while the exporting event is alive. A peer that opens it after the event has been collected gets `CUDA error: invalid argument` (`hipErrorInvalidValue` on ROCm) out of `Event.from_ipc_handle`, surfacing via `futures.py -> event_ipc.py:import_event`.

Nothing upstream of this retains the event either — both producers create a plain local and return through this method:

```python
event = event_backend.create_event(cache_context.device)   # plain local
return event_backend.export_event(event, cache_context.device), store_succeeded
```

(`lmcache/v1/multiprocess/modules/lmcache_driven_transfer.py` and `experimental/qstore.py`.) Since all producers funnel through `DefaultEventIPCBackend.export_event`, retaining there fixes them at one site rather than three. `MusaEventIPCBackend` delegates to the default backend, so it inherits the fix; the timeline-semaphore backend packs a sequence snapshot rather than a device event and is unaffected.

Whether the consumer wins the race depends on refcount/GC timing. That explains the observed signature: failure rate well under 1%, first fault several minutes into a run, and faults in both directions.

## Fix

Retain exported events in a bounded `deque` (`maxlen=8192`). The ring only needs to cover the window between export and the peer's import — microseconds to milliseconds on the `lmcache_driven` path — and being bounded means a long-lived backend cannot grow without limit.

This is deliberately a mitigation rather than the principled fix. The principled version is a registry keyed by request/transfer, released when the corresponding future completes; that needs API surface across the MP path and seemed out of scope for a bugfix. Happy to take it further if maintainers prefer that shape.

## Testing

Added two regression tests to the existing `tests/v1/platform/test_event_ipc.py`, using that file's `_FakeEventModule` harness. Both **fail on `dev` and pass with the fix** — verified by reverting only the `export_event` body:

```
########## WITH FIX ##########
2 passed, 21 deselected

########## WITHOUT FIX (revert export_event only) ##########
FAILED tests/v1/platform/test_event_ipc.py::test_export_event_retains_event_while_handle_is_usable
FAILED tests/v1/platform/test_event_ipc.py::test_exported_event_retention_is_bounded
2 failed, 21 deselected
```

Full file, on `0cf5efc7` + this change:

```
$ python3 -m pytest -q tests/v1/platform/test_event_ipc.py
23 passed, 81 warnings in 3.75s
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on both touched files.

### Real-workload evidence

Originally isolated with an 8-pass Llama-3.1-8B reproducer at TP8 (TP1 passes — the trigger is multi-worker concurrency, not the model):

| build | faults | EngineDead | result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `0.5.5.dev114` stock | 12 | 17 | fails |
| `0.5.6.dev3` stock | 12 | 17 | fails |
| `0.5.6.dev3` + this fix | **0** | **0** | 8/8 passes |

Identical counts across versions indicate the bug is untouched rather than a recent regression.

Confirmed again on current `dev` (`0cf5efc7`), built from source for ROCm, serving Kimi-K3 (TP8, MI355X, ROCm 10) through the `LMCacheMPConnector`:

- **without the fix:** engine dies ~14 minutes into a 3600 s run with `hipErrorInvalidValue`, followed by `Producer process has been terminated before all shared CUDA tensors released`; the client then aborts at 10.3% failed requests
- **with the fix:** full 3608 s, 1030 requests, 0 errors in the measured phase

### Performance after the fix
LMCache on this node lands on top of the project's published `vllm-simple` cell run on its own CI cluster:

| metric | LMCache | CI vllm-simple | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| ITL p90 | 14.53 ms | 14.53 ms | 0.0% |
| interactivity p90 | 68.82 | 68.82 | 0.0% |
| throughput / GPU | 4665.2 tok/s | 4636.6 tok/s | +0.6% |

## Not a duplicate

Searched issues and PRs for `export_event`, `ipc_handle`, `hipErrorInvalidValue` and `invalid_block_ids`; no existing issue or PR covers this. Nearby open PRs (#5141, #5139) touch multi-group KV transfer, not event IPC lifetime.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The diagnosis, the reproducer, and the before/after measurements above were produced and verified on real hardware; a human author reviewed the change and is available to defend and revise it.

title: [Feat][MP] Engine-driven multi-group transfers via KVLayerGroupsManager
body:
Rebuilt along @ApostaC's three steps, on top of #4079 (first commit is that move; it drops out when #4079 merges):

1. Registration initializes `KVLayerGroupsManager` and derives every group's geometry from it (no per-group re-detection). The manager also validates chunk and window divisibility.
2. Block IDs are parsed per group from the manager's kernel groups; sliding-window groups keep only the trailing window of each chunk.
3. Gather/scatter call the shared helpers moved in #4079, extended with `blocks_per_window`.

The chunk token count is `blocks_in_chunk * lcm(group block sizes)`, folding in the mixed-geometry fix @skaulintel found on the old branch (gemma-4 registered half of every chunk). Covers both transports: SHM reserves per-group slots, pickle sends a group-major payload. k3 lanes: kimi_linear_tp and engine-driven HMA lm-eval, both transports.

title: fix: return [None] from BytesBufferMemoryObj.get_dtypes
body:
<!--  Thanks for your contribution to LMCache!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'Fixes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'Refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
`BytesBufferMemoryObj.get_shapes()` returns a single shape, but `get_dtypes()` returned an empty list. `RemoteMetadata._prepare_params()` iterates `zip(self.shapes, self.dtypes, strict=True)`, so storing any byte-buffer serde output (e.g. `cachegen`) through a remote connector (`fs`, Redis, …) raises `zip() argument 2 is shorter than argument 1` on every put.

This fixes it at the source: `get_dtypes()` returns `[None]`, parallel to `get_shapes()` (one dtype per shape). A raw byte buffer has no per-element tensor dtype, and `None` round-trips cleanly through the metadata codec (`DTYPE_TO_INT[None] == 0`, `INT_TO_DTYPE[0] is None`), so `RemoteMetadata` serializes and deserializes correctly.

Refs #2787 (same root cause, reported for the Redis backend; reproduces identically on the `fs` connector).

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- This is a **source fix**, not a `_prepare_params` workaround. It follows the direction @chunxiaozheng gave on #2412 ("find the reason that results in the mismatch, rather than fill the dtypes") — `strict=True` and `_prepare_params` are left untouched.
- **`None` vs `torch.uint8`:** #2787 suggested `[torch.uint8]`. I chose `[None]` because a `BytesBufferMemoryObj` is an opaque compressed blob with no meaningful per-element tensor dtype; `None` states that honestly and already round-trips (`DTYPE_TO_INT[None] == 0`). `torch.uint8` would also satisfy the cardinality check but asserts a dtype the buffer doesn't have. Happy to switch to `uint8` if maintainers prefer an explicit dtype.
- The abstract `MemoryObj.get_dtypes()` return type is intentionally left unchanged to avoid widening `dtype | None` across the many tensor-backed consumers; the single divergence is annotated with `# type: ignore[list-item]` and an explanatory comment.
- Verified with the pinned pre-commit hooks (isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell, mypy on py3.12 — all green) and `pytest tests/v1/test_remote_metadata.py` (16 passed). mypy is net-zero vs `dev`.
- Two regression tests, written against the public contract: (1) `len(get_dtypes()) == len(get_shapes())` for a byte buffer; (2) a `RemoteMetadata` serialize→deserialize round-trip with a `None` dtype (the exact path the remote connector put exercises) — fails before the fix, passes after.

**If applicable**:

- [X] this PR contains unit tests

title: [MP][Bugfix] Bind a CUDA context before the IPC wrappers' driver calls
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #5168

The CUDA IPC wrappers call the CUDA driver API on whatever thread constructs them. The first `register_kv_caches` runs on the worker's main thread, which already has a current CUDA context. The **re-registration after an LMCache server restart** runs on the connector's `HeartbeatThread`, which has none, so every retry fails with `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT` and the vLLM worker never leaves degraded mode.

This PR adds `_bind_primary_context(device_index)` and calls it before the driver calls in **both** wrapper constructors. If the calling thread has no current context (`cuCtxGetCurrent` returns null), it retains the device's primary context, makes it current, and releases the extra reference again. A thread that already has a context is left untouched, so the first registration and every other caller behave exactly as before; the only outcome that changes is a call that used to fail now succeeding.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- **Rebased onto the platform package move.** The implementation moved to `lmcache/v1/platform/devices/cuda/ipc_wrapper.py` and the legacy re-export package was removed, so this is regenerated against the new paths rather than merged — hence the clean diff.
- **Both wrappers, one root cause.** `RawCudaIPCWrapper.__init__` had no binding at all. `VmmCudaIPCWrapper.__init__` wrapped its driver calls in `with torch.cuda.device(...)`, which is exactly the pattern that does **not** bind a context on a fresh thread. Fixing one and not the other would leave the same bug on a sibling path and would conflict with itself on the same file.
- Why not `with torch.cuda.device(...)`: it does not work here. On a fresh thread torch skips the underlying runtime call when the target equals its cached current device (0), so nothing is bound. Verified on an RTX PRO 6000 with torch 2.13.0+cu130 by constructing the wrapper from a fresh `threading.Thread`: unpatched fails with `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT`, the `torch.cuda.device` variant fails identically, and both `cudaSetDevice` and the primary-context binding succeed. The driver-level form is used because it never changes the thread's runtime device selection.
- **Not touched:** the other `with torch.cuda.device(...)` blocks in this file wrap *runtime* API calls, which do bind the context lazily. Only the driver-API sites needed the change.
- Why in the wrappers rather than in `HeartbeatThread`: the wrappers are the code calling the driver API, and they are also instantiated directly by the TRT-LLM adapter, so binding here covers every caller instead of one thread.
- Reference counting: the helper retains only to obtain the handle, makes it current, and releases. The thread keeps the context as its current one and the runtime's own reference (torch) keeps it alive, so the process reference count is unchanged.
- Test: `tests/v1/platform/devices/cuda/test_cuda_ipc_wrapper.py::test_raw_wrapper_constructs_on_a_fresh_thread` constructs a wrapper from a fresh `threading.Thread`. Before the fix it raises `RuntimeError: cuMemGetAddressRange failed: <CUresult.CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT: 201>`; after the fix it passes. It needs a GPU, like the rest of that file.
- **Scope honesty:** the Raw path is reproduced and verified on hardware. The Vmm path is the same mechanism at the same entry point but not separately reproduced, since it needs VMM-backed tensors.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `isort` pass on the touched files.

title: [MP][Bugfix] Bound client TCP connect attempts
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #4670

In MP mode on Kubernetes, the worker heartbeat can stay in degraded mode ~2 minutes after a restarted cache server is already healthy, delaying KV re-registration by the same amount. Root cause: `MessageQueueClient`'s DEALER sets no `zmq.CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, so a reconnect attempt whose SYN is silently dropped (racing the Service endpoint removal/restore during the pod restart) inherits the OS connect timeout (~127s on Linux) and monopolizes the socket — stalling every pending request, including heartbeat PINGs. Full mechanism in the linked issue.

This PR sets two socket options on the `MessageQueueClient` DEALER, before `connect()`:
- `zmq.CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 5000` ms (`CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`): a wedged connect attempt is abandoned and re-dialed within seconds instead of minutes. A healthy TCP handshake takes about a millisecond, so 5s only affects attempts that would otherwise hang. It is below the default 10s heartbeat interval, so one wedged attempt costs at most one missed ping.
- `zmq.RECONNECT_IVL_MAX = 1000` ms (`RECONNECT_IVL_MAX_MS`): zmq re-dials every 100ms by default with no backoff. This turns on exponential backoff (100ms → 200ms → … → 1s), so a down server is not re-dialed at a flat 100ms.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Per review, the timeout is now a hardcoded constant instead of a `lmcache.mp.connect_timeout` option. That removes the factory / adapter / `ExtraConfigDefault` plumbing and the docs row. The change is now just `mq.py` and one test.
- Earlier review: the `_failed_pings` counter and throttled logging were removed.
- Only `tcp://` connects can stall this way. `ipc://` and `inproc://` connects fail fast, so the options have no practical effect there.
- Behavioral check with a pyzmq socket monitor against a blackholed endpoint (SYN dropped, no RST): the stock DEALER logs one `connect_delayed` and then stays wedged. With this change it logs `closed` → `retried` at 5.0s, re-dials after 100ms, then again at 10.1s after 200ms.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` pass on the touched files.

title: [Bug] PeriodicThread restart overlaps a live worker after stop timeout
body:
<!--  Thanks for your contribution to LMCache!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'Fixes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'Refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

### Background

PR [#3758](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/3758) made a `PeriodicThread` restartable after an `IrrecoverableException` by clearing `_running` when the worker loop exits.

That fix handles a terminated worker, but it exposed an ownership problem when `stop()` times out while the previous worker is still alive.

A deterministic sequence is:

1. Worker A enters its callback and blocks.
2. `stop(timeout=0)` clears `_running` and sets the shared stop event, but A remains alive.
3. `start()` sees `_running == False`, creates worker B, replaces the stored thread handle, and clears the shared stop event.
4. Worker A exits and clears `_running`.
5. Worker B remains alive but is reported as stopped.
6. A subsequent `stop()` returns immediately without signalling B.

This can also allow further workers to be admitted. The zero timeout only makes the schedule deterministic; a callback exceeding the normal stop timeout creates the same lifecycle state.

### Discovery and regression test

The issue was originally reproduced with an event-controlled, CPU-only diagnostic using the real `PeriodicThread` implementation.

The historical comparison showed:

- Before #3758, the replacement remained reported as running and could receive another stop request.
- At #3758 and on the investigated `dev` revision, the exiting original worker cleared the replacement worker's running state.
- Each revision produced the same result across 10 controlled repetitions.

The regression test in this PR uses only the public API:

- `create_periodic_thread()`
- `start()`
- `stop()`
- `is_running`
- `stop_requested`
- returned worker handles

Before the fix, the test fails because `start()` returns a replacement worker while the original worker remains alive. After the fix, the restart is rejected until the original worker terminates, and a normal restart remains possible afterward.

### Fix

This PR gives a live worker ownership of the `PeriodicThread` lifecycle until it actually exits:

- Serialize lifecycle decisions with the existing lock.
- Decide restart eligibility using the stored worker's actual liveness rather than `_running` alone.
- Preserve the stop event while the previous worker remains alive.
- Capture the worker under the lock, but release the lock before `join()` to avoid deadlock.
- Allow repeated `stop()` calls to wait again after an earlier timeout.
- Guard final `_running` cleanup with worker identity.
- Preserve restart after `IrrecoverableException` once the previous worker has terminated.

Preventing overlap is intentional. Adding only a conditional final `_running` assignment would leave two workers sharing the same stop and wake events, and a replacement start could still clear the original worker's stop request.

This is a lifecycle-management fix only. It does not change callback behavior, scheduling intervals, or the public method signatures.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

The focused suite was run using:

```powershell
python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/v1 tests/v1/test_periodic_thread.py
```

title: ci: pre-merge PR base before pipeline expansion
body:
## Summary

This is a follow-up / completion of #4536.

#4536 fixed the most obvious gap by pre-merging the PR base branch inside the main k3 setup scripts, but we still had CI paths that consumed the raw PR checkout before those setup scripts ran. In practice that means some Buildkite jobs could still expand/upload pipeline steps, diff against the base branch, or build/install from source using the unmerged PR head instead of `PR head + latest target branch`.

The current issue is still visible in this Buildkite run:
- https://buildkite.com/lmcache/k3-multiprocess-test/builds/4479

## What this PR changes

- generalize `merge_pr_base_branch()` with `LMCACHE_PR_BASE_MERGE=auto|always|never`
- pre-merge before dynamic pipeline upload in the k3 shared upload helper
- convert several repo-defined pipelines into `bootstrap -> upload merged steps` so the step definitions themselves also come from the merged checkout
- wire the same pre-merge behavior into remaining direct CI entrypoints that install LMCache or build the multiprocessing image
- make the operator integration diff logic follow `BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST_BASE_BRANCH` instead of assuming `dev`

## Why this is needed

Without this, #4536 only protects the subset of jobs that happen to reach `setup-env.sh` / `setup-lmcache-only-env.sh` first. Other paths can still validate stale pipeline definitions or stale source state, which is the same class of problem #4536 was meant to eliminate.

- temporary git-repo simulation confirming `merge_pr_base_branch` creates the expected merge commit, is idempotent on rerun, and can be disabled with `LMCACHE_PR_BASE_MERGE=never`

title: [MP][Coordinator] Add Key Directory placement metrics
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This PR adds Key Directory placement metrics for the MP Coordinator, building on the Coordinator metrics infrastructure introduced in #4389.

It adds two OpenTelemetry observable gauges:

- `lmcache_mp.key_directory_placement_count`
- `lmcache_mp.key_directory_placement_size_bytes`

Both metrics are reported with `tier="l1"` / `tier="l2"` attributes.

The metrics represent the current placement state recorded by the Coordinator Key Directory:
- placement count is the number of current `Placement` entries
- placement size is the sum of reported logical object sizes for those placements

To avoid scanning the full Key Directory on every metrics collection, the directory maintains incremental per-tier aggregates and exposes an O(1) snapshot for the gauge callbacks.

Refs #4239
Follow-up to #4389

**Special notes for reviewers**:

- Aggregates are updated under the same Key Directory lock as placement mutations.
- STORE/upsert, DELETE, fencing, shared placements, and checkpoint restore are covered.
- Aggregate values are not persisted directly; they are rebuilt from restored placements after checkpoint restore.
- The size metric represents reported logical object bytes, not physical storage usage or unique-object size.
- No HTTP API, CacheEvent semantics, quota/eviction behavior, or generic OpenTelemetry infrastructure is changed.

title: [MP][Trace] Add the events trace level: record the cache-event stream
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adds `--trace-level events` to `lmcache server`. It records every cache-event batch the server builds for the MP coordinator, in the exact wire form `POST /events` carries, into the existing `.lct` trace format. **It needs no coordinator**: a fleet that runs without one (a benchmark, for example) can capture what it would have reported, and the file can later be replayed into a coordinator or a test double of one.

How it fits the existing pieces:

- The `CacheEventSubscriber` already delivers through a `CacheEventSink`. The new `TraceCacheEventSink` writes each flushed batch into an `EventsTraceRecorder`; `MultiCacheEventSink` fans a flush out to the trace and the coordinator when both are configured, and a failure of one does not stop the other.
- `EventsTraceRecorder` is a `TraceRecorder` with no bus subscriptions (the subscriber does the mapping) and leaves the `@enable_tracing` gate off, so no `TRACE_CALL` events are built for a level that would not read them. A new `captures_calls` class attribute expresses that; `StorageTraceRecorder` behaves as before.
- `TraceRecorder.write_record` is factored out of `_on_trace_call` so a non-bus producer can append records.
- `Header.level_meta` (defaulted, so older files decode) carries `instance_id`, `cache_event_schema_version` and `lmcache_version`. `CACHE_EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` in `mp_coordinator/api.py` names the wire shape.
- Records: `events.lifecycle` (`start` with identity, `stop`) and `events.batch` (wire form). Heartbeats are not recorded.
- `lmcache trace info` summarizes an events file by instance, restarts, batches per type/tier/backend/shared, entries, bytes, token-carrying entries. `lmcache trace replay` refuses a non-storage file with a clear message.
- `run_http_server` rejects `--trace-level events` with observability disabled, mirroring the existing check for coordinator event reporting.

Design doc: `docs/design/v1/mp_observability/trace.md` §12; `cache_events.md` lists the new sinks. User docs updated for the flag.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Tests: `tests/v1/mp_observability/trace/test_events_recorder.py` (recorder, sink wire form and round trip through `CacheEventsRequest`, lifecycle marks, drop-counting on a closed recorder, `MultiCacheEventSink`, lifecycle helper, `trace info` output). Existing trace, cache-event, replay and HTTP server suites pass.
- Store entries carry `token_ids`; the design doc notes files are sensitive and points at redaction as out-of-tree tooling.

title: fix(mp): improve device IPC error when the receiver lacks accelerator access
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

In MP mode, when a process that receives an accelerator IPC handle has no accelerator visibility (for example an `lmcache server` started without GPU access), `DeviceIPCWrapper._get_device_index_from_uuid` failed at `REGISTER_KV_CACHE` with a generic "Device UUID ... not found in the discovered devices" error. That points operators at device visibility, when the real issue is that this process has no accelerator at all. This is the failure reported in #4186.

This PR makes the error actionable while keeping it engine- and role-agnostic: `DeviceIPCWrapper` is platform-base code, below the engine integration layer, so the message names no specific engine, process role, or config key. It points at the two supported topologies: give the receiving process visibility of the same accelerator devices, or configure the MP deployment to use `engine_driven` transfer so the sending client performs the device-side copy. Device-capable hosts are unaffected -- the discovery/lookup path is unchanged, and an available-device/unknown-UUID lookup still raises the original error.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Scoped to the runtime diagnostic. The `examples/multi_process/` topology is intentionally out of this PR: per #2128 the example was originally a GPU-visible server using CUDA IPC, so switching it to `engine_driven` would be choosing a new topology rather than a fix. Better handled separately once the intended deployment is settled.
- Addresses the inline review: the message no longer assumes vLLM or a server role, and no longer implies a client-only change is always sufficient.

**Testing**:

```
pytest tests/v1/platform/test_ipc_wrapper.py -q
3 passed
```

Covers: a device-incapable host raises the actionable engine-agnostic error; a device-capable host with an unknown UUID still raises the original error; a known UUID resolves to its ordinal.

title: feat(security): disable /run_script and bind admin HTTP to localhost by default
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #5128.

The admin HTTP surface currently ships two insecure defaults, which combine into unauthenticated in-process code execution for any network-reachable deployment:

1. `POST /run_script` (`internal_api_server/common/run_script_api.py`) `exec()`s an uploaded Python script. The restricted `__builtins__` are not a security boundary — the injected `app` object alone reaches the whole interpreter object graph — as the docs themselves already warn ("treat it as full remote code execution"). The endpoint is served unconditionally:
   - by the vLLM-embedded internal API server whenever `internal_api_server_enabled=true`, and
   - by the standalone `lmcache server` HTTP frontend, whose `http_apis/common_api.py` auto-aggregates every `internal_api_server/common` router (`_MP_INCOMPATIBLE_MODULES` is empty).
   Neither server authenticates requests.
2. Both servers bind `0.0.0.0` by default (`internal_api_server_host`, `--http-host`).

**Changes:**

- New `run_script_api_enabled` setting (`LMCACHE_RUN_SCRIPT_API_ENABLED`), default **false**: `/run_script` returns 404 unless the operator explicitly opts in. Works for both modes via the same `app.state` lookup pattern the endpoint already uses for `script_allowed_imports` (`lmcache_adapter.config` in-process, `app.state.configs["mp"]` on the standalone server).
- `lmcache server`: new `--run-script-api-enabled` flag (default false) wired into `MPServerConfig`.
- `internal_api_server_host` and `--http-host` now default to `127.0.0.1`.

Backward compatibility: operators who use `/run_script` set one flag; multi-node admin access sets the bind host explicitly. The route remains registered (visible in OpenAPI) so clients get a clear 404 with an enablement hint rather than a confusing connection error, and existing tests that exercise the endpoint keep working by opting in.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- The gate is enforced at request time (not registration time) because the MP frontend builds its FastAPI app at module import, before server config exists; a request-time check covers both servers uniformly with one code path.
- `test_run_script_endpoint_present` in `tests/v1/multiprocess/http_apis/test_common_api.py` still passes: the route stays registered, it is only inert until enabled.
- Docs updated: `internal_api_server/common_apis.rst`, `mp/http_api.rst`, `mp/configuration.rst`, `api_reference/configurations.rst` (incl. the new `run_script_api_enabled` row and corrected bind defaults).

title: fix(trtllm): trim partial-chunk blocks before MP transfers
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #3917.

TensorRT-LLM's block list covers the request's trailing partial LMCache chunk, while the MP key ends at the last complete chunk. With `chunk_size=256`, `tokens_per_block=32`, and a 2176-token request, the key covers 2048 tokens but the adapter sends 68 block IDs. The core downsampler requires complete 8-block chunks and rejects that list.

Trim the block list to the key's aligned end before both STORE and RETRIEVE, and skip requests without a complete chunk. The original metadata is unchanged. Undersized block lists still reach the server's existing validation. Both calls use the current `RequestClient` interface.

This follows the maintainer's feedback on the closed, unmerged #3918: correct the TRT-LLM caller while preserving the core helper's contract.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Regression tests use the actual worker constructor, public metadata binding, and stubs for optional TensorRT-LLM and request-client interfaces. They cover partial chunks (2176 tokens / 68 blocks), partial blocks (2049 / 65), aligned requests, short and empty requests, missing or undersized block lists, non-contiguous physical block IDs, metadata preservation, and failed-retrieve handling.
- On upstream `59a56a2c`, the same test file gives **3 failed, 5 passed**; with this fix, **8 passed**.
- Validation after merging upstream `08fac932` (no merge conflicts or additional code changes required): `pytest tests/v1/test_tensorrt_mp_adapter.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_client.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_transport_factory.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_futures.py -q` — **55 passed**, including available CUDA event IPC tests.
- `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy pre-commit run --all-files` passed. No Rust files changed.
- The real core downsampler rejects 68 block IDs with the reported assertion and stages the aligned 64 IDs on an RTX 5060 Ti using a controlled cache-context fixture. This does not exercise model KV transfers; a full TensorRT-LLM model deployment was not run.
- The standard Python suite stops during collection because the local environment does not include the optional `vllm` package.

title: [Perf][RawBlock] Batch uring_cmd recovery reads
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

NVMe passthrough (`use_uring_cmd=true`) restart recovery currently validates
slot headers one at a time. This PR routes multi-entry recovery through the
existing queue-depth-bounded batched reader while retaining per-slot retries
for failed completions. It also updates the raw-block documentation and adds a
regression test for the recovery dispatch.

The synthetic benchmark prepares checkpoint metadata and per-slot headers
without writing full payloads, then measures checkpoint loading and slot-header
validation. On a Samsung BM1743 NVMe device with `io_uring_cmd`, queue depth
256, and a checkpoint containing 524,224 entries, two three-run A/B sets
produced these combined medians:

| Recovery path | Median bringup time | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|
| Serial `io_uring_cmd` | 104.02 s | 1.00x |
| Batched `io_uring_cmd` | 11.85 s | **8.78x** |

Every run recovered all 524,224 entries.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- The scope is limited to restart recovery validation. Normal KV load and write
  paths, the on-device metadata format, and the configuration interface are
  unchanged.

title: Add gRPC runtime metrics export
body:
## Summary

- Register gRPC Python's OpenTelemetry observability plugin with LMCache's existing MP OTel `MeterProvider` so gRPC runtime metrics are exported through the same Prometheus/OTLP paths as LMCache metrics.
- Keep ZMQ metrics behavior unchanged: gRPC runtime metrics now use an auto setting that resolves to enabled only for `--transport grpc` and disabled for `--transport zmq`.
- Add `--disable-grpc-metrics` and `ObservabilityConfig.grpc_metrics_enabled` as an explicit escape hatch while keeping LMCache EventBus metrics enabled.
- Add the Linux-only `grpcio-observability==1.78.0` runtime dependency; non-Linux hosts skip the integration without treating the missing package as an error.
- Document the exported `grpc.*` metrics and the transport-gated behavior.
- Move `LookupHashLogConfig` into the lightweight observability config module and stop eager-importing subscriber packages from `subscribers/__init__.py`, so config/logging-only paths do not require native metrics modules.

## Actual /metrics smoke output

To make the exported gRPC runtime metrics concrete, I also ran a Linux smoke e2e that uses this PR's `init_otel_metrics(..., enable_grpc_metrics=True)` path, starts a local unary gRPC client/server pair, sends **8 successful RPCs** and **1 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` RPC**, then scrapes the in-process Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint.
