title: fix(mp): start scheduler heartbeats for all servers
body:
## Summary

Fix a scheduler heartbeat initialization regression affecting both single-server and multi-server MP deployments. The scheduler stored its heartbeats in an empty dictionary but used a non-None check as its not-yet-started guard, so its lazy first-lookup path always returned before creating any heartbeat threads.

This fix is **not optional cleanup**. `LMCacheMPSchedulerAdapter` already has scheduler-side health events, heartbeat threads, timeout-based unhealthy marking, and `is_healthy` gating. The intended design is: foreground RPCs can mark a server unhealthy, and background heartbeats later detect recovery and re-enable the scheduler. Without this fix, that recovery half of the design is unreachable.

- Use None as the explicit pre-start sentinel and publish the complete per-server heartbeat map after startup.
- Make scheduler shutdown handle the pre-lookup state.
- Add coverage that a two-server scheduler starts, retains, and stops exactly one heartbeat per server.
- Keep nonblocking lookup-status tests independent of live background polling.

## Impact

This bug does not necessarily break the steady-state lookup happy path: while every LMCache server stays up, the scheduler can still submit LOOKUP and QUERY_PREFETCH_STATUS RPCs directly. That is why the regression can be easy to miss in normal cache-hit tests.

But this does **not** mean the heartbeat is unnecessary. The heartbeat is the recovery mechanism for scheduler-side health state. `LMCacheMPSchedulerAdapter` initializes every server as healthy and is supposed to lazily start one `HeartbeatThread` per backing server on the first lookup. Without those heartbeat threads:

- the scheduler cannot proactively detect that a backing LMCache server has gone away;
- health can only be updated indirectly when a foreground lookup/status RPC times out;
- once a server is marked unhealthy, the scheduler has no background ping loop to observe recovery and set the health event again;
- in both single-server and multi-server setups, one transient server failure can therefore keep the scheduler in degraded/unhealthy mode until the process is recreated, even after the LMCache server comes back.

So the failure mode is not "all lookups immediately fail". It is "the scheduler's intended failure-detection and recovery path is disabled". The fact that normal lookup can still work while all servers remain healthy is only the happy path; it is not evidence that scheduler heartbeats are disposable.

## Root Cause

Before this change, the scheduler initialized:

```python
self._heartbeats = {}
```

but `_ensure_heartbeat_started()` used this guard:

```python
if self._heartbeats is not None:
    return
```

An empty dictionary is already non-None, so the first lookup returned before creating or starting any `HeartbeatThread`. The intended lazy-start path was therefore unreachable.

## Reproduction

One LMCache MP server is sufficient, including with `--tensor-parallel-size 2`. Both TP workers connect to the same server; the scheduler needs one heartbeat for that server. The failure does not require a multi-server deployment.

This is a source-checked manual E2E procedure, not a completed GPU E2E run. Prerequisites: a Linux host with two CUDA GPUs capable of running Qwen/Qwen3-8B, at least 20 GiB available host memory for L1, a working CUDA-enabled vLLM/LMCache build environment, and `git`, `curl`, and `jq`. Use a vLLM version supporting the LMCache-shipped connector module, `cached_token_stats`, and the dev-mode prefix-cache reset endpoint. Keep that vLLM version and all settings identical between the two runs.

1. Install the pre-fix revision in the active vLLM environment. Use a fresh checkout; the CUDA toolkit and PyTorch must already be available for the native build.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache.git lmcache-heartbeat-repro
cd lmcache-heartbeat-repro
git checkout --detach 7dac8bcd5dbcfe510f9ebdeac118c4f2a6481554
python -m pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
```

2. In terminal A (Bash), start one LMCache server and capture its PID. Keep this shell open for the request and signal commands below.

```bash
lmcache server --transport zmq --host localhost --port 6555 \
  --l1-size-gb 20 --eviction-policy LRU --chunk-size 256 \
  > lmcache-heartbeat-repro.log 2>&1 &
LMCACHE_REPRO_PID=$!
```

3. After the LMCache startup completes, start vLLM in terminal B using the same Python environment. Explicitly select the connector from this LMCache checkout. Both TP ranks share `tcp://localhost:6555`.

```bash
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --port 8000 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector":"LMCacheMPConnector",
    "kv_connector_module_path":"lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_mp_connector",
    "kv_role":"kv_both",
    "kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{
      "lmcache.mp.server_urls":"tcp://localhost:6555",
      "lmcache.mp.mq_timeout":3,
      "lmcache.mp.heartbeat_interval":1
    }
  }'
```

4. After vLLM is ready, run the following in terminal A. The first request populates LMCache. Reset vLLM's local prefix cache before the warm request to confirm a working LMCache hit before injecting any failure.

```bash
REPRO_REQUEST=$(jq -n '{
  model: "Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
  messages: [{
    role: "user",
    content: ("Explain the history of computer science in detail. " +
      ("The Turing machine defines an abstract model of computation. " * 100))
  }],
  max_tokens: 1,
  kv_transfer_params: {cached_token_stats: true}
}')

repro_request() {
  curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 60 \
    http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$REPRO_REQUEST"
}

repro_reset() {
  curl --fail --silent --show-error -X POST \
    http://localhost:8000/reset_prefix_cache
}

repro_request > cold.json
sleep 2
repro_reset
repro_request > warm.json
jq -e '.kv_transfer_params.cached_token_stats |
  .num_vllm_cached_tokens == 0 and .num_lmcache_cached_tokens > 0' warm.json
```

Do not continue unless the warm-hit check passes; otherwise the setup has not established that LMCache is serving cached tokens.

5. In terminal A, pause the LMCache process and issue another request. `SIGSTOP` preserves the process and its cache contents while preventing it from responding. Resume it immediately after the request returns.

```bash
repro_reset
kill -STOP "$LMCACHE_REPRO_PID"
repro_request > outage.json
kill -CONT "$LMCACHE_REPRO_PID"
```

On the pre-fix revision, the vLLM scheduler log should contain `LOOKUP to tcp://localhost:6555 timed out` and `Marking server as unhealthy`. Confirm this before interpreting the recovery result. On the fixed revision, the scheduler heartbeat may detect the outage before the foreground LOOKUP times out, so that exact timeout log is not required.

6. Without restarting vLLM, wait for recovery, clear the local prefix cache again, and repeat the same request.

```bash
sleep 10
repro_reset
repro_request > recovered.json
jq '.kv_transfer_params.cached_token_stats |
  {num_vllm_cached_tokens, num_lmcache_cached_tokens}' recovered.json
```

Expected on the pre-fix revision: `num_vllm_cached_tokens == 0` and `num_lmcache_cached_tokens == 0`. The scheduler's health event remains cleared after the timeout. With no scheduler heartbeat to set it again, `is_healthy` keeps suppressing subsequent lookups even after the server resumes. The worker heartbeats update separate worker health events and cannot repair the scheduler's event.

7. Stop vLLM in terminal B and stop the LMCache server in terminal A. Install this PR's revision, then repeat steps 2-6 with fresh processes.

```bash
kill -CONT "$LMCACHE_REPRO_PID"
kill -TERM "$LMCACHE_REPRO_PID"
wait "$LMCACHE_REPRO_PID"
git fetch origin refs/pull/5233/head
git checkout --detach d56d4699161b2cc52af7adae5377811284de485a
python -m pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
```

Expected with this PR: the scheduler starts its heartbeat on the first lookup. After `SIGCONT`, a successful PING sets its health event again and lookups resume. With the warm-hit precondition established and the prefix cache reset, `num_vllm_cached_tokens == 0` and `num_lmcache_cached_tokens > 0` should be observed. Restarting vLLM between revisions is required; restarting it between the outage and recovery request would hide the bug.

## Validation

- Adapter unit tests: 64 passed, 3 skipped.
- Scheduler heartbeat and nonblocking lookup tests: 20 passed.
- Full non-Rust pre-commit: passed. Rust hooks are intentionally skipped on macOS.

title: feat(mp): enable per-layer KV cache load for LMCache-driven MP mode
body:
Add per-layer (layerwise) KV cache transfer to LMCache-driven multiprocess mode so vLLM can overlap attention compute with the H2D transfer, instead of blocking on a single per-chunk (all layers per-request) transfer before the forward pass starts.

The feature is selected at runtime for CUDA. It activates only when the cache server is started with --layerwise-batch N for N > 0 and vLLM is pointed at the layerwise connector through kv_connector_module_path like below example.

lmcache server --layerwise-batch 8 --l1-size-gb 20 --eviction-policy LRU --port 5555

vllm serve --kv-transfer-config \
'{"kv_connector":"LMCacheLayerwiseMPConnector",
"kv_connector_module_path":"lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_mp_connector_layerwise", "kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"lmcache.mp.host": "tcp://localhost","lmcache.mp.port":5555}}'

Separate code path:
- lmcache_mp_connector_layerwise.py and vllm_multi_process_adapter_layerwise.py subclass the existing connector and worker adapter.
- modules/lmcache_layerwise_transfer.py subclasses LMCacheDrivenTransferModule and imports the helpers it reuses. lmcache_driven_transfer.py only does a minor change to accommodate per-layer path.
- protocols/layerwise.py declares REGISTER_LAYERWISE_IPC_EVENT_POOL and RETRIEVE_LAYERWISE for clear boundary without impacting existing request types.
- transfer_context/worker_layerwise_transfer.py and layerwise_futures.py hold the worker-side context and future.
- csrc/cuda/mp_mem_kernels_layerwise.cu holds the layerwise kernel and its launch code. The device helpers it shares with the per-chunk path moved verbatim into mp_mem_kernels_device.cuh, so both translation units include them rather than duplicating them.

Extension points added to existing files:
- LMCacheDrivenTransferModule.retrieve() routes every object-group copy through a new _transfer_object_group() hook so the subclass avoids hundreds of lines of duplicated code. The base implementation just calls transfer_kv_per_object_group in lmcache_driven_transfer.py.
- LMCacheMPConnector._worker_adapter_cls and LMCacheMPWorkerAdapter._create_transfer_context let the subclasses swap in their own components.
- server._build_modules selects the layerwise module when --layerwise-batch > 0

Multi-frame responses:
- MessagingFuture gains deliver() which reports whether a request is complete, and a blocking handler may declare a response_channel parameter to answer with more than one frame. Buffering intermediate frames and deciding when the exchange ends happens inside LayerwiseDeviceMessagingFuture.
- LayerwiseDeviceMessagingFuture intercepts frames by installing itself as the raw future's delivery sink, and that has to happen before the request reaches the wire. Add tests/v1/multiprocess/test_layerwise_retrieve_submit_ordering.py.

Layout:
PageBufferShapeDesc gains kv_interleaved. When set, an LMCache object uses the L2TD layout [L, 2, T, D] (K0,V0,K1,V1,...) instead of the default 2LTD layout [2, L, T, D] (all K then all V), so a per-layer transfer reads one contiguous span per layer. The flag is fixed at registration time to keep it off the per-request path.

Event pool:
EventPool in platform/base/event_pool.py allocates EVENT_POOL_SIZE IPC events once and exports their handles during REGISTER_LAYERWISE_IPC_EVENT_POOL, so the per-layer path signals a pooled event by index instead of exporting a handle per layer.

Mode exclusivity:
The two modes (per-layer and per-chunk) are mutually exclusive per server node, and the worker's mode is fixed at process start by the connector vLLM imports, not negotiated during registration.

title: feat(local-disk): extend by_gpu sharding for worker-aware multi-device paths
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This PR extends the existing `by_gpu` sharding policy in the local disk
backend to support worker-aware multi-device path assignment.

Previously, local-disk `by_gpu` selected a single path from the physical GPU
device id. That had a few limitations:

1. extra disk paths could remain idle when `#paths > #workers`
2. physical device id is not the right key in data-parallel or device-remapped
   deployments
3. global cache management in multi-path mode could break path locality after
   eviction, causing KV cache to be re-inserted on a different path than the
   one originally mapped for that key

This change extends `by_gpu` to use local worker metadata when available:

- `#paths == #workers`: one path per worker
- `#paths > #workers`: each worker gets a contiguous subset of paths
- `#workers > #paths`: workers share paths by modulo mapping

Within an assigned subset, KV cache is routed by stable per-key hashing.

This PR also changes multi-path local-disk cache management from global to
path-local. Each assigned path now has its own quota, usage tracking, and
eviction-policy state, which keeps cache placement aligned with the intended
path mapping even after eviction.

When local worker metadata is not available, `by_gpu` keeps the legacy
single-path `device_id % num_paths` behavior.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- This extends the existing `by_gpu` policy; it does not introduce a new
  sharding mode.
- The worker-aware branch is keyed by local rank, which makes path assignment
  coherent in DP and device-remapped setups.
- Path count and local worker count must be equal or exact multiples;
  unsupported uneven layouts fail at startup.
- In multi-path mode, cache management is path-local rather than global.
- Tests were added for worker-aware assignment, legacy compatibility, subset
  routing, and multi-path local-disk backend behavior.
- Docs and the local backend example were updated accordingly.

title: [Bug] fix(disk): wrap async_save_bytes_to_disk write in try/except to prevent MemoryObj leak on I/O failure (#3533)
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Closes #3533
Refs #3372

When `async_save_bytes_to_disk` encounters an I/O exception (disk full, NFS timeout, O_DIRECT alignment failure, etc.), `ref_count_down()` was skipped because it lives after the `write_file()` call. This causes a MemoryObj leak with non-zero refcount:

1. `write_file()` raises → execution jumps past `ref_count_down()`
2. MemoryObj leaks with `ref_count > 0`
3. Python GC eventually collects → `__del__` → `parent_allocator.free(self)` → `AddressManager.free()` acquires `self._lock`
4. If another thread holds `AddressManager._lock` in `batched_allocate()` → **self-deadlock**

**Fix**: Wrap `write_file()` in `try/except` so that `ref_count_down()` and `remove_put_task()` are guaranteed to execute on any I/O failure before the exception is re-raised.

**Root cause chain** (from issue):
```
disk full / IO error
  → write_file() raises (local_disk_backend.py:542)
  → ref_count_down() skipped (local_disk_backend.py:555)
  → MemoryObj leaks: ref_count > 0
  → GC collects → __del__ → parent_allocator.free(self)
  → AddressManager.free() acquires self._lock
  → if batched_allocate() already holds _lock → self-deadlock
```

**Special notes for your reviewers**:
- Minimal change: only the exception path is affected; the normal (happy) path is identical to before
- `ref_count_down()` and `remove_put_task()` are called in the except block to prevent both the memory leak and the put-task tracking leak

title: [Bench] Support --served-model-name in engine bench (alias vs HF path)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3809.

`lmcache bench engine` used a single `--model` value for three incompatible
purposes:

| Purpose | Needs |
|---|---|
| Match LMCache `/status` entries | HF model path |
| vLLM OpenAI API request `model` field | the `--served-model-name` alias |
| Tokenizer loading | HF model path |

When the engine runs with `--served-model-name`, no single `--model` value
works — either `/status` matching fails (`Model 'kimi-k2.5' not found on LMCache
server`) or the API request 404s (`The model '/llm/...' does not exist`).

## Fix (bench-side, no protocol change)

- Add a `--served-model-name` flag and an `api_model` field on
  `EngineBenchConfig`.
- `--model` stays the **HF path** used for `/status` matching and tokenizer
  loading; `api_model` (the **alias**) is used only for the OpenAI API request
  in `RequestSender`.
- `api_model` defaults to `model`, so behaviour is unchanged when the flag is
  absent (backward compatible).
- The flag flows through the interactive and saved-config (`--config`) paths via
  the central `ALL_ITEMS` schema registry and is persisted on export.

So the reporter's case now works:

```
lmcache bench engine --engine-url ... --lmcache-url ... \
    --model /llm2/Moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5 --served-model-name kimi-k2.5
```

## Tests

`test_config.py`: `api_model` defaults to `model` (dataclass + parse path), and
`--served-model-name` sets `api_model` to the alias while `--model` stays the HF
path. Verified end-to-end against the real config module.

## Note

This is a focused bench-side fix. A more invasive alternative (per the issue) is
to propagate `served_model_name` through the KV-cache registration chain
(`REGISTER_KV_CACHE` / adapters / `report_status`) so `/status` exposes the alias
directly across vLLM/SGLang/TRT-LLM. Happy to pursue that instead if maintainers
prefer the server-side approach.

title: Fix race condition in `memcheck()` during `LazyMemoryAllocator` expansion
body:
### Problem
Fix #3834

`TensorMemoryAllocator.memcheck()` reads `AddressManager._size` twice through two separate unprotected calls (`get_free_size()` then `get_heap_size()`). During lazy expansion, the background thread can call `sbrk()` — which holds `_lock` — between those two reads, causing the check to observe `old_size != new_size` and incorrectly report the allocator as unhealthy.

### Fix

**`AddressManager.size_snapshot()`** — new `@synchronized("_lock")` method that returns `(_size, total_allocated_size)` in a single critical section, ensuring the two values are always consistent.

**`AddressManager.check_consistency()`** — add `@synchronized("_lock")` so the free-list traversal and size comparison are also protected against concurrent `sbrk()`.

**`TensorMemoryAllocator.memcheck()`** — replace the two separate reads with a single `size_snapshot()` call. Check 1 (`free + allocated == heap`) remains logically a tautology, but the lock prevents any future refactor of `get_free_size()` from re-introducing the race silently.

### Testing

Verified that inserting the following two debug sleeps makes the race fire on
every run without the fix, and disappear with it:

```python
# lazy_memory_allocator.py — _commit_expansion()
import time; time.sleep(0.01)  # delay sbrk until memcheck has read get_free_size()

# memory_management.py — memcheck(), between get_free_size() and get_heap_size()
import time; time.sleep(0.01)  # keep window open for sbrk to fire
```

### Performance

No impact on the hot path. `memcheck()` is only called from the `/status` monitoring endpoint and explicit `clear()` operations — never from `allocate()` or `free()`. `_lock` is already acquired on every `allocate()` and `free()` call; the two additional acquisitions in `memcheck()` add negligible overhead.

title: raw-block: persist stable device identity in checkpoints
body:
<!--  Thanks for your contribution to LMCache!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'Fixes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'Refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Raw-block checkpoint recovery previously relied on the configured `device_path`
to identify checkpoint metadata. That is fragile because device paths can change
across reboot, and the same NVMe namespace may be opened as `/dev/nvme*` or
`/dev/ng*` depending on whether `io_uring_cmd` is used.

This PR adds a stable `device_id` to raw-block checkpoint metadata:
- NVMe namespaces use `nvme:<wwid>` from `/sys/block/<namespace>/wwid`
- regular files use `file:<st_dev>:<st_ino>:<st_size>`

Recovery now validates `device_id` instead of relying on `device_path`, so path
changes do not reject valid checkpoints. Unsupported paths fail fast when
checkpoint loading or periodic checkpointing is enabled.

For upgrade compatibility, this PR also adds an opt-in legacy migration switch:
- MP `raw_block`: `allow_legacy_checkpoint_without_device_id=true`
- non-MP `rust_raw_block`: `rust_raw_block.allow_legacy_checkpoint_without_device_id=true`

This option allows loading older checkpoints that were written before `device_id`
was recorded. It only applies when the checkpoint is missing `device_id`;
checkpoints with a mismatched `device_id` are still rejected. After the legacy
checkpoint is loaded and a new checkpoint is written, the option should be
disabled again.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:
`device_path` may still appear in diagnostics or legacy metadata, but recovery
validation uses stable `device_id`.

The legacy migration option is disabled by default and is intended only as a
one-time upgrade path for pre-`device_id` checkpoints.

title: [Fix][NIXL] Fail store tasks atomically on pool exhaustion
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The static NIXL L2 adapter previously stopped preparing a store batch when its storage pool could not allocate enough slots. If no objects had been prepared, the task incorrectly succeeded with zero transferred bytes. If earlier objects had already received slots, the adapter transferred and published that partial batch while reporting the entire task as successful.

This change treats pool exhaustion as a task failure before any transfer occurs.

- Route empty storage allocations through the existing failure path.
- Free every provisional storage slot accumulated for the task.
- Return an unsuccessful result with zero transferred bytes.
- Avoid publishing keys, notifying listeners, or updating usage for failed batches.
- Preserve zero-byte success when every submitted key already exists.
- Add regression coverage for oversized batches, already-full pools, and existing-key-only stores.

title: feat(fs_native): decouple read depth from num_workers and size it in bytes
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adds `read_io_depth` and `read_max_bytes_in_flight` to the `fs_native` L2 adapter. The native filesystem connector inherits `ConnectorBase`'s tiling and serial `do_batch_get`, so reads in flight against the device equal `num_workers`, default 4. On an 8x NVMe RAID0 array that reads 30 GB/s at LMCache's default `chunk_size` of 256 where the array delivers 54; end to end, 100 concurrent 120k-token requests served from L2 take 24.1 s per round instead of 14.5 s (1.66x).

Raising `num_workers` is the obvious fix and it is not enough, for two reasons. First, it sets bytes in flight only indirectly, as `num_workers x object_size`, and object size moves by 128x with `chunk_size`: 4 workers is the best setting at 192 MiB objects and 78% below best at 1.5 MiB, 256 workers is the reverse (6.5% below at 192 MiB). No single value is right at more than one `chunk_size`. Second, even the value tuned for this workload loses end to end: `num_workers=64` ties the pool in an isolated read benchmark (54.0 against 54.1 GB/s) but is 7.4% slower in the vLLM round (15.6 s against 14.5 s, 0.3% drift between repeats). Both hold at most 64 reads in flight there, so the gap is not in bytes outstanding and its cause is not established; the measurement is what the PR claims. A budget in bytes is within 0.8% of the best at every object size measured, with one default, for batches large enough to fill the depth; the design doc records where small batches fall short.

`FSConnector` starts `read_io_depth` reader threads and overrides `do_batch_get()` and `choose_num_tiles()`, the shape `MooncakeConnector` already uses. `ConnectorBase` is unchanged. Both fields default to 0, which keeps the current path. The sweep behind the 1536 MiB default is in `docs/design/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/fs_native_read_depth.md`. Benchmark scripts and raw logs: https://github.com/BoJiang03/LMCache/tree/fs-native-read-depth_dev/benchmarks/microbenchmark/fs_native_read_depth

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Only `fs_native` gains the knobs. `redis` has the same coupling, but a reader thread there is a socket and what that path needs is pipelining, a separate change.

title: [Perf][MP] Carry token ids as a packed uint32 buffer instead of a list of ints
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`IPCCacheServerKey.token_ids` and `LoadStoreOp.token_ids` become `token_bytes`: one big-endian uint32 word per token, encoded in the new `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/token_codec.py`. Every scheduler step each in-flight request emits an op carrying its whole token prefix, across three process hops; as a `list[int]` every hop materializes one Python `int` per token, packed each hop is a memcpy.

No cache is invalidated: `_make_blake3_hash_func` already hashed `struct.pack(f">{n}I", *tokens)`, so the packed buffer is the byte string blake3 was being fed.

DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 200k x 12, TP8, `--long-prefill-token-threshold=256`: LMCache server CPU 204.0 s -> 98.0 s, prefill wall 256.6 s -> 160.8 s over seven A/B pairs. Flat at the default threshold, where the connector is not on the critical path. Harness and raw results: [run_packed_token_ids_ab.sh](https://github.com/BoJiang03/LMCache/blob/delta_token_ids_pr_dev/benchmarks/e2e/run_packed_token_ids_ab.sh), [packed_token_ids_results/](https://github.com/BoJiang03/LMCache/tree/delta_token_ids_pr_dev/benchmarks/e2e/packed_token_ids_results).

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Breaking: client and server must be upgraded together. `common.proto` retires field 4 rather than reusing it, because proto3 encodes a packed `repeated int64` and a `bytes` identically, so an old client's blob would otherwise decode as garbage token ids.

Most of the 42 files are one rename at one call site each. `lazy_offload_manager` is in the diff because it builds `LoadStoreOp`s directly; its own tests are in flight separately.

Not here: sending only the new tokens each step instead of the whole prefix, a follow-up stacked on this.

title: [CI][MP] Add an EVICTION_AWARE lazy offload test
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`launch-processes.sh` hardcodes `lmcache.mp.lazy_offload_policy` to FIFO, so the `lazy_offload` step covers FIFO only. EVICTION_AWARE, the default policy, has no coverage. This adds an `eviction_aware_lazy_offload` step for it.

That policy ignores request counts, so it needs a different shape. A buffered store comes due when one of its GPU blocks reaches the danger depth of the free queue, and on an idle engine that depth is zero. Phase 1 sends three small requests to an otherwise idle engine and requires that nothing is written to L1; eager would write after each one and FIFO at threshold 2 would write on the third. Phase 2 sends a long-document workload twice the size of the pinned block pool, so the pool turns over, and requires that L1 writes rise and that the policy's counter ledger shows it emitted and closes.

title: [MP][Perf] Add opt-in cudaMemcpyBatchAsync direct copy path for LMCache-driven transfer
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adds an opt-in copy path to the MP server's LMCache-driven STORE/RETRIEVE
transfer that moves each chunk straight between the pinned host object and the
engine's paged KV buffers with one `cudaMemcpyBatchAsync` call per chunk, with
no GPU staging buffer and no scatter kernel. The existing kernel path stays the
default.

Motivation: on Kimi-Linear-48B (TP 2, 1024-token MLA pages, 128k prefix) an
nsys A/B shows the kernel path's scatter kernels each waiting ~1.6 ms to be
scheduled on a GPU busy with vLLM's prefill, about 50 ms of stream idle per
128k retrieve while the copies themselves already ran at line rate. 

Changes:
- `csrc/cuda`: `execute_direct_copy_transfer`, `batch_memcpy_supported`,
  `direct_copy_format_supported`, plus `DirectCopyGroupSpec` /
  `DirectCopyObject` descriptors. One `resolve_block_addressing` switch turns
  each eligible `EngineKVFormat` into a base-pointer rule and three byte
  strides (mirroring `calculate_engine_global_offset`, including
  `block_stride_elems` padding); the per-entry loop has no format branches.
  Host ranges are split at `PIN_CHUNK_SIZE` boundaries. Requires CUDA runtime
  and driver >= 12.8; compiled out on HIP.
- `MPServerConfig.transfer_copy_policy` with `--transfer-copy-mode
  {kernel,direct,auto}` (default `kernel`) and `--direct-copy-min-block-bytes`
  (default 128 KB, used by `auto`), carried on `MPCacheServerContext`.
- `lmcache_driven_transfer.py`: `select_transfer_copy_path` chooses per object
  group; `_run_direct_copy_plan` mirrors the staged planner's window/skip
  logic. `transfer_kv_per_object_group` takes `block_ids_host` and
  `copy_policy`. Ineligible layouts (HND, blocked-scale, (K,V)-tuple), GDS
  objects, or missing native support fall back to the kernel path with a
  one-time warning.
- `BaseCacheContext.get_kernel_group_offset_in_object` and
  `get_kernel_group_kv_pointer_list` (cached on `GPUCacheContext`).
- Torch fallbacks for the two query functions; design doc at
  `docs/design/v1/multiprocess/modules/lmcache_driven_transfer_copy_paths.md`;
  tip in the Kimi Linear recipe.


**If applicable**:

- [x] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [x] this PR contains unit tests
  - `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_direct_copy_transfer_gpu.py`: bit-exact parity
    with the kernel path for every eligible format, both directions, skipped
    block prefix, two-group objects, padded MLA stride, pin-boundary splits,
    and rejection of ineligible layouts / out-of-range ids.
  - `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_direct_copy_planner_gpu.py`: end to end through
    `transfer_kv_per_object_group` with a real `GPUCacheContext` and
    `LazyMemoryAllocator`, including a Kimi-like 1024-token MLA geometry.
  - `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_transfer_copy_policy.py`: config flags and
    path selection (CPU only).

title: [Bugfix] Chunk native host registration for large pinned pools
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Large host KV-cache pools can fail to initialize on NVIDIA R580+ even when enough host memory is available. With 4 KiB pages, a single 512 GiB registration requires 2 GiB of driver page-table metadata, exceeding the `INT_MAX` limit of the driver's `kvzalloc()` path. This was reproduced with vLLM + LMCache on CXL-backed memory; anonymous mmap and tmpfs-backed shared memory hit the same per-call limit.

Register native mmap-backed pools in chunks of at most 64 GiB and unregister each chunk at its original address. This covers the NUMA, hugepage and shared-memory allocators. For `alloc_pinned_ptr`, requests of at least 512 GiB with Default/Portable/Mapped flags use anonymous mmap plus chunked registration; smaller requests retain `cudaHostAlloc`.

Registration failure rolls back earlier chunks in reverse order and clears the pending CUDA error through the same runtime. Free attempts every chunk even if one unregister reports an error. A mutex-protected ownership map lets the existing pointer-only `free_pinned_ptr` API select the matching release path, without changing callers.

References:
- [NVIDIA/open-gpu-kernel-modules#1234](https://github.com/NVIDIA/open-gpu-kernel-modules/pull/1234): proposed driver fix and our reproduction report, including successful registration of the same buffer in smaller chunks. The driver PR is still open.
- [vllm-project/vllm#51080](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51080): independent reproduction of the same 512 GiB per-call boundary during CPU KV offload on H200.
- [vllm-project/vllm#51081](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51081): KV-offload workaround using 64 GiB registrations, rollback and CUDA error draining; merged into vLLM main on September 17, 2026. This PR applies that size cap to LMCache's native allocator paths. vLLM's application-level workaround does not fix the underlying driver or LMCache's independent native allocation calls.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

`cudaHostAllocWriteCombined` has no registration equivalent. Requests carrying it (or unknown flags) continue through `cudaHostAlloc`, preserving CUDA's semantics rather than silently dropping flags; the large-allocation workaround does not cover that case. The separate platform pin-memory API and lazy allocator are outside this change.

Validation:
- CPU-only regression harness compiles the production C++ allocator against a fake CUDA runtime. It checks the 512 GiB boundary, 520 GiB and partial tails, flag preservation, failure at each registration, reverse rollback, retry, unregister errors, and the NUMA/hugepage/shm allocation/free paths. Large mappings reserve virtual addresses only.
- `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python -m pytest --noconftest tests/v1/test_native_mem_alloc.py -q` — passed.
- Real CUDA 13.0 build and 4 MiB H2D/D2H round trips for ordinary pinned, shared-memory and NUMA allocations — passed on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, driver 580.126.20.
- `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy pre-commit run --all-files` — passed. Rust hooks explicitly skipped; no Rust changes.

The full integration suite and a physical allocation of at least 512 GiB were not rerun for this revision. The earlier local workaround recorded a successful 520 GiB allocation; this revision tests the large-size control flow with the fake runtime.

title: fix(xpu): preserve cached prefixes in V2/V3 H2D transfers
body:
## Summary

- bind all six V2/V3 XPU `multi_layer_kv_transfer` call sites with explicit
  keyword arguments
- pass the computed nonzero prefix through
  `skip_prefix_n_tokens=skip_prefix_n_tokens`
- extend the existing XPU connector tests to verify that cached destination
  slots remain untouched while the uncached suffix is restored

## Root cause

Both V2 and V3 compute the intended prefix skip correctly, but their H2D calls
passed it as positional argument 9. The XPU pybind signature places
`head_size` at position 9 and `skip_prefix_n_tokens` at position 10, so the
value bound to the currently unused `head_size` parameter while the actual
skip retained its default of zero.

This is a pre-existing XPU caller bug and was not introduced by #4467. Using
keywords at every call site also prevents future optional-parameter insertions
from silently changing the caller contract.

## Validation

- `ruff check` passed for both changed files
- `ruff format --check` passed for both changed files
- `git diff --check` passed
- source-level binding probe confirmed six keyword-only calls and, for V2/V3,
  `head_size=0` with `skip_prefix_n_tokens=3`

I do not have Intel XPU hardware, so the updated hardware regression has not
been run locally. Please add the `xpu` label to trigger the repository's
dedicated Intel XPU Buildkite pipeline. This PR remains a draft until that
runtime result is available.

title: [Fix][Native Connector] Balance batch tiles
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Native connector batching previously calculated a rounded-up tile size and derived every range from that fixed size. When the item count was only slightly larger than the tile count, this concentrated work in the first tiles and produced empty requests, reducing worker-pool utilization.

For example, distributing 9 items across 8 tiles previously produced:

```text
2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 0, 0, 0
```

This PR:

- Uses quotient/remainder partitioning so tile sizes differ by at most one and every tile is nonempty.
- Produces the following distribution for 9 items across 8 tiles:

```text
2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1
```

- Centralizes range calculation in a shared helper used by GET, SET, EXISTS, and DELETE.
- Removes the obsolete fixed tile size from batch preparation and tile request construction.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- The default tile count remains the smaller of the operation's worker count and item count.
- Mooncake continues to use one tile through its existing tile-count override.
- This changes no public API or configuration.
- No repository unit test was added because `ConnectorBase` does not currently have a C++ unit-test harness.

title: [Test][MP] Cover hybrid STORE boundaries and incremental group mapping
body:
## Summary

Add behavior-level regression tests for the boundary semantics of `LMCacheMPRequestMetadata.GetStoreMetadata` on hybrid layouts, where the storable prefix is the minimum over engine groups of `allocated_blocks * tokens_per_block`, restricted to non-scratch groups.

The scratch exclusion (#5042) and the recurrent last-token reservation (#5249) already have focused tests (`test_store_metadata_ignores_scratch_groups`, `test_recurrent_lookup_reserves_final_prompt_token`). This PR covers the remaining boundary behavior those tests don't reach:

| # | case | assertion |
|---|---|---|
| A | chunk-edge inputs `kC−1 / kC / kC+1` | store ends floor to `(k−1)C / kC / kC`; `kC−1` on a fresh request stores nothing |
| B | per-group capacity bottleneck among linear groups (6 vs 4 blocks) | the least-covered group binds: end = 64, not 96 |
| C | scheduled-token bottleneck (63 scheduled, allocation larger) | only full chunks of scheduled tokens store |
| D | scratch group at first / middle / last position | each permutation keeps the scratch group's (empty) slot and the engine-group order of `op.block_ids` |
| E | incremental multi-step stores across decode steps | second store starts at the stored frontier (`(32, 64)`), a step with no new full chunk stores nothing |
| F | all-linear four-group layout (no scratch, mixed capacities) | min-over-groups behavior unchanged |
| G | small (even single-block) **non-scratch** group | still caps the store: to `None` below one chunk, to its chunk floor above it — guards against over-correcting the scratch exclusion into a block-count heuristic |

## Test validity (mutation-checked)

Each mutation was applied locally and reverted; none of these mutations are part of this PR:

- reverting the scratch-group exclusion (span-0 groups counted) → all three D cases fail
- replacing the group minimum with a maximum → the four capacity-bound cases (B, F, G×2) fail
- restarting the incremental offset from zero each step → E fails

On dev (`0cf5efc7`): the new file passes 16/16, and the existing `tests/v1/test_mp_connector_mm_keys.py` suite stays green alongside it.

## Related real-world evidence

We independently reproduced the store-blocking failure this area fixes on an **older fork build (pre-#5042, base `e5078730`)** with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next + MTP: the recurrent-state group (one 8-token block) froze the group minimum at 8 tokens, so `num_chunks` floored to 0 and no STORE was ever emitted, while an all-linear control model stored normally under identical configuration. Numbers and probe output were shared in #5268 and #4966. An end-to-end store/retrieve/fidelity validation on current dev (including the #5249 full-hit semantics) is planned; we'll report results when done.

Refs: #5042, #5249, #5268, #4966

title: RawBlock: add SPDK I/O engine with zero-copy DMA support
body:
Introduces a new SPDK-based I/O engine for RawBlockCore, enabling high-performance zero-copy NVMe direct I/O for both NVMe-over-Fabrics (NVMe-oF) and local PCIe NVMe devices.

### Key Features
**SPDK I/O Engine**: Implements SPDK support for all transport types (NVMe-oF TCP, RDMA, and PCIe) with a two-thread architecture (I/O worker + admin worker)
**External Memory Registration**: For payload we registers CPU memory backed by Hugepages with SPDK for direct I/O without intermediate copies.
**Zero-Copy DMA**: Uses pre-allocated DMA memory pools (HeaderBufferPool for headers.
**Metadata checkpoints**: On demand SPDK memory allocation.
**Batched IO**: Both SPDK read and write mode leverages the batched submission and completion
**Configurable Core Reservation for SPDK workers**: Allowing flexibility and ensuring optimal CPU affinity across different system topologies.
**Lockless rte_ring**: Asynchronous I/O submission using lockless ring buffers for high-throughput operations
**GIL-Safe Execution**: Python ctypes FFI wrapper with GIL-release for parallel thread execution.

### Changes Missing
- SPDK backend works only in poll mode. Interrupt mode not added.

**For Reviewers**
- Yet to handle IO timeout from SPDK.
- Yet to handle IO re-enqueue for larger in-flight requests.
- Benchmarking for NVMe-of is ongoing.
- Out of 4025 LOC changes only 2600 are code related to SPDK integration. Rest are unit tests , README, build related changes.
- In Process mode is not supported, only MP mode.

title: Fix scratch group blocking store metadata in hybrid models
body:
## Summary

Fix a critical bug where LMCache fails to store any KV cache data when used with hybrid models like DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.

## Problem

Hybrid models have two types of KV cache groups:
- **Main groups** (e.g., group 0-8 in DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash): Standard attention layers with `prefix_cacheable=True`
- **Scratch group** (e.g., group 9): `CircularBufferSpec` for compressor state with `prefix_cacheable=False`

The scratch group only holds 1 block × 8 tokens, but `GetStoreMetadata()` calculates:
```python
allocated_tokens = min(all_groups' allocated_tokens)
```

This gets capped at 8 tokens by the scratch group, causing `num_chunks = 0` and the function silently returns `None`, preventing any STORE operations.

## Solution

Skip scratch groups (where `prefix_cacheable=False`) in the `allocated_tokens` min calculation.

### Changes

1. **`integration/vllm/kv_cache_groups.py`**:
   - Add `is_scratch_spec()` helper to identify scratch groups
   - Modify `get_tokens_per_block()` to return 0 for scratch groups
   - Exclude scratch groups from layer index collection

2. **`integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_metadata.py`**:
   - Filter out `tokens_per_block=0` groups in `GetStoreMetadata()` min calculation

3. **`integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector.py`**:
   - Filter scratch groups in `get_vllm_scheduler_block_size()`
   - Exclude scratch groups in `get_resolved_attention_block_sizes()`
   - Update validation logic to allow `tokens_per_block=0`

4. **`v1/multiprocess/group_view.py`**:
   - Handle `tokens_per_block=0` in `slice_block_ids_per_group()`

## Testing

### Before Fix
```
Stored tokens: 0
External hit rate: 0.0%
```

### After Fix
```
Stored tokens: 4197
External hit rate: 8.3% ~ 44.7%
```

### Performance Impact (RPS=1.3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash)
- Mean TTFT: 73.2s → 21.8s (**-70%**)
- Median TTFT: 73.0s → 14.7s (**-80%**)
- Throughput: +6%

## Environment

- **Model**: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- **vLLM**: nightly (0.30.0+) from [recipes.vllm.ai](https://recipes.vllm.ai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash)
- **CUDA**: cu129
- **LMCache**: 0.5.5rc7
- **KV cache groups**: 10 groups (8 sliding window + 1 full attention + 1 scratch)

## Related Issues

- LMCache #4966: Same bug with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
- vLLM PR #55027: Similar fix for MooncakeStore connector
- vLLM PR #55033: Similar fix for CPU offload

title: fix(integration/vllm): guard state transition for non-chosen connector
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Syncs the state transition fix from [vLLM PR #47505](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47505) to LMCache's three `lmcache_mp_connector` variants.

**Bug**: In `update_state_after_alloc`, the condition `tracker.needs_retrieve()` only checks `num_lmcache_hit > num_vllm_hit` — it does not check whether this connector was the chosen one in a MultiConnector. When a non-chosen connector receives `num_external_tokens=0`:

| Consequence | Impact |
|---|---|
| State enters `WAITING_FOR_LOAD` instead of `READY` | State machine corruption |
| `free_lookup_locks` not called → read locks held until TTL (10 min) | Lock leak |
| `allocated_block_ids` populated → retrieve task created (after vLLM #46865) | Unwanted KV transfer |

**Fix** (one line per file):
```python
# Before
condition = tracker.needs_retrieve()
# After
condition = tracker.needs_retrieve() and num_external_tokens > 0
```

When `condition=False`, the existing `else` branch correctly sets state → `READY`, frees all locks, and calls `cleanup_lookup_result`.

**Files changed** (3 variants for different vLLM versions):
- `lmcache/integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector.py` (latest)
- `lmcache/integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector_0201.py` (vLLM 0.20.1)
- `lmcache/integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector_0180.py` (vLLM 0.18.0)

**Version compatibility verification**:

MultiConnector was introduced in vLLM PR #17564 (2025-05-14), before all three targeted versions. Verified that all three vLLM versions have identical `MultiConnector.update_state_after_alloc` behavior — non-chosen connectors receive `(empty_blocks, 0)`:

| vLLM version | Release date | MultiConnector present | Non-chosen receives `num_external_tokens=0` | `needs_retrieve()` logic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.18.0 | 2026-03-20 | ✅ | ✅ `c.update_state_after_alloc(request, empty_blocks, 0)` | `num_lmcache_hit_blocks > num_vllm_hit_blocks` |
| v0.20.1 | 2026-05-04 | ✅ | ✅ `c.update_state_after_alloc(request, empty_blocks, 0)` | `num_lmcache_hit_blocks > num_vllm_hit_blocks` |
| main | — | ✅ | ✅ `c.update_state_after_alloc(request, empty_blocks, 0)` | `num_lmcache_hit_tokens > num_vllm_hit_tokens` |

The bug exists in all three versions, and the fix applies identically to each.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- This is the LMCache-side sync of vLLM PR #47505 (already submitted, reviews the identical logic)
- LMCache maintains three connector copies for different vLLM API versions; all three have the same bug
- This fix is a prerequisite for safely merging vLLM PR #46865 (MultiConnector passes real blocks to non-chosen connectors)
- Refs vllm-project/vllm#47505, vllm-project/vllm#46865

title: feat: Add MP server autostart for vLLM connector
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #3065.

Adds opt-in startup of a local LMCache MP HTTP server when vLLM uses the
LMCache-shipped `LMCacheMPConnector`. Existing deployments remain
connect-only unless auto-start is explicitly enabled.

Configuration is provided through `kv_connector_extra_config`:

- `lmcache.mp.autostart`: enable auto-start; defaults to `false`.
- `lmcache.mp.autostart.wait_timeout`: readiness timeout in seconds;
  defaults to `90.0` and must be positive and finite.
- `lmcache.mp.autostart.server_args`: extra server CLI arguments,
  including required settings such as `--l1-size-gb` and `--eviction-policy`.

The implementation:

- Uses the actual vLLM worker rank 0 to start the server when it is not
  already healthy. Other workers wait for readiness before connecting.
  The scheduler and legacy positional adapter callers remain connect-only.
- Checks ZMQ readiness through `RequestClientFactory.create` and
  `client.ping(None)`, preserving lazy loading of probe dependencies.
- Supports single-node, single-server auto-start on `localhost` or
  `127.0.0.1`. Multiple server URLs fail early during connector
  initialization. IPv6 is explicitly rejected because the current MP
  ZMQ transport does not enable IPv6 sockets.
- Uses the connector's resolved server URL, respecting `server_urls`
  precedence over host/port extras. Endpoint overrides in `server_args`
  are rejected.
- Cleans up failed launcher startup attempts and adds a k3 TP=2
  auto-start smoke test with explicit test-process cleanup.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

**Lifetime contract correction:** the auto-started server is a child of
worker 0, not an independently managed service. LMCache adapter shutdown
does not explicitly terminate it, but vLLM process-tree cleanup can.
Neither survival after vLLM exit nor automatic cleanup is guaranteed
across versions and exit paths.

Persistent or cross-instance shared servers must be started and managed
separately, outside the vLLM process tree. Reusing an already healthy
server remains supported. This replaces the earlier unconditional
survival promise and needs reviewer confirmation.

This PR does not add daemonization, remote startup, crash recovery, or
automatic restart.

**Validation**:

- 137 focused tests passed with zero skips using vLLM 0.28.0+cu129,
  Torch 2.13.0+cu129, and rebuilt LMCache native extensions.
- Real-weight Qwen3-0.6B on two H20 GPUs with TP=2 confirmed auto-start,
  readiness on both ranks, inference, and KV store/retrieve. The warm
  request reused 768 of 851 prompt tokens from LMCache, with vLLM prefix
  caching disabled and KV load failure policy set to `fail`.
- The original server-survival assertion failed: vLLM 0.28.0's default
  SIGTERM/abort shutdown recursively killed the MP server. The subsequent
  restart/reuse stage was not reached; this is not a full restart e2e pass.
- Pre-commit passed on the 10 relevant changed files, with Rust hooks
  explicitly skipped. Shell syntax and `git diff --check` passed.
- Strict Sphinx build still fails on pre-existing baseline issues.
  The changed configuration page was rendered and visually checked,
  with no new diagnostics.

The GPU validation used a different runtime from k3's pinned nightly/cu130
environment. A maintainer-triggered `k3-multiprocess-test`, including
`mp_autostart_tp2`, is still needed.

**If applicable**:

- [x] This PR contains user-facing changes — docs updated.
- [x] This PR contains unit tests.

title: fix(mp): honor num_external_tokens==0 contract in update_state_after_alloc
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

vLLM PR [#46865](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46865) established a connector contract for `update_state_after_alloc`:

> Decide whether to load based on `num_external_tokens`, not on whether `blocks` is empty: `blocks` may be non-empty even when `num_external_tokens == 0` (e.g. a non-chosen sub-connector of MultiConnector still receives the request's real blocks).

All other vLLM connectors (Mooncake, Moriio, NIXL, non-MP LMCache) honor this contract. The **LMCache MP connector does not** — it completely ignores `num_external_tokens`, relying on tracker state (`needs_retrieve()`) to decide whether to load.

### The problem

In a MultiConnector topology (e.g. Mooncake + LMCache MP), when Mooncake wins the load:
1. MultiConnector calls `LMCache.update_state_after_alloc(request, blocks, num_external_tokens=0)` with **real blocks**
2. The MP connector ignores `num_external_tokens` and checks `tracker.needs_retrieve()`
3. If a prior `get_num_new_matched_tokens` lookup hit (setting `num_lmcache_hit_tokens > 0`), the tracker enters `WAITING_FOR_LOAD` and generates RETRIEVE metadata
4. **Two connectors simultaneously attempt to load the same request** — conflict

Additionally, server-side lookup read locks are leaked: the lookup acquired locks on matched chunks, but the non-chosen connector never retrieves them, so they persist until TTL expiry (default 300s).

### The fix

Add an early return when `num_external_tokens == 0`, after block recording (which the store path needs):

1. Transition tracker from `PREFETCHING` → `READY` (no retrieve)
2. Clean up scheduler-adapter lookup tracking state
3. Release any server-side read locks from a prior lookup hit (`free_lookup_locks`)
4. Return — the store path continues to work via `_process_new_requests` / `_process_cached_requests`

### What doesn't change

- The `num_external_tokens > 0` path is untouched — existing single-connector behavior is identical
- The `BYPASS_LMCACHE` state handling is preserved (it already returns early)
- Block recording (`append_block_ids`) happens before the early return, so the store path has correct block IDs

## Special notes for your reviewers

- This is a standalone bug fix independent of #4761 (`enable_lookup`). It fixes the contract violation that exists even without `enable_lookup`.
- The `num_lmcache_hit_tokens > 0` check inside the early return handles the MultiConnector case where `get_num_new_matched_tokens` was called (by MultiConnector's loop) and hit, but this connector was not chosen for loading. In single-connector mode with `num_external_tokens == 0`, `num_lmcache_hit_tokens` is 0 (lookup missed or was skipped), so the lock release is a no-op.
- Related: vLLM PR [#46865](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46865) (contract), LMCache issue [#4665](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/4665) (MP connector ignores kv_role / skip_save).

## If applicable

- [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [ ] this PR contains unit tests

title: fix: unpin KV caches for aborted requests in sync mode
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

In sync mode, `lookup(pin=True)` pins KV caches in the Worker's `LocalCPUBackend`. Normally unpin happens in `wait_for_save()`, but **aborted requests may skip `wait_for_save()` entirely**, leaving the pin count unbalanced and leaking pinned memory.

The Scheduler-side `request_finished()` calls `storage_manager.cancel_request()`, but `LocalCPUBackend` does not override `cancel_request()` (it is a no-op in the base class), so the Scheduler cannot release Worker-side pins across processes.

Fix: call `lookup_unpin()` for all `finished_req_ids` in `get_finished()` (Worker-side API) when `async_loading` is disabled.

**Why guard with `not self.async_loading`?**

In async mode, abort cleanup is already handled via `lookup_client.cancel_lookup()` on the Scheduler side, which triggers Worker-side `cleanup_memory_objs()`. Adding `lookup_unpin` here for async mode would risk double-cleanup.

**Is this safe for normally-completed requests?**

Yes. `lookup_unpin()` uses `dict.pop()` to remove the `lookup_id` from `lookup_pins`. If `wait_for_save()` already unpinned, the second call is a safe no-op (key not in dict).

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Related: PR #2786 (pin count balancing for `kv_consumer`), PR #3340 (graceful skip on Scheduler-role abort). These fix Scheduler-side abort cleanup, but do not address the Worker-side pin leak in sync mode.
- Related: PR #2045 (async abort handling) covers the async mode path.

title: fix: prevent busy_loop deadlock in EIC connector retrieve path
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`EICConnector._batched_get` uses `asyncio.gather` to run N concurrent `_get` calls, each calling `get_data()` → `memory_allocator.allocate()` with the default `busy_loop=True`.

When the CPU staging buffer is full, each concurrent retrieve enters the busy_loop in `LocalCPUBackend.allocate()`, sleeping and retrying indefinitely. The loop assumes "stores will clear" to free space, but all retrieve coroutines are blocked in the busy_loop — no store is running, so space is never freed, causing a **deadlock**.

This contradicts the `LocalCPUBackend` docstring which states `busy_loop` should only be used for single-retrieve scenarios, not concurrent ones:

> 1. synchronous case: one retrieve at a time (okay to busy loop because stores will clear)
> 2. asynchronous case: many retrieves happen concurrently (if they busy_loop, deadlock happens)

Fix: pass `busy_loop=False` to `allocate()` in `get_data()`. On allocation failure, `get_data()` returns `None` and the caller (`_get`) filters it out, degrading to a cache miss instead of deadlocking.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- This is a 1-line fix. The EIC connector's `_batched_get` bypasses the async serializer (unlike the storage manager's retrieve path), so concurrent retrieves can deadlock on CPU staging buffer contention.
- Related: #2942 (deadlock in LocalCPUBackend when `use_hot=False`) and PR #3804 (not yet merged) address the same class of bug at the backend level, but EIC's concurrent retrieve path needs this fix at the connector level regardless.

**If applicable**:

title: fix: eager-init kv_layer_groups_manager in V3 connector
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Override `initialize_kvcaches_ptr()` in `VLLMPagedMemGPUConnectorV3` to build `kv_layer_groups_manager` when kvcaches are first registered, not lazily on the first `to_gpu()`/`from_gpu()` call.

**Problem**: `cache_engine.store()` calls `metadata.get_shapes()` to allocate memory objects **before** `from_gpu()` runs. Without eager init, `kv_layer_groups_manager` is `None` at that point, so `get_shapes()` falls back to the legacy single-group path `[kv_shape[1], kv_shape[0], num_tokens, kv_shape[3]*kv_shape[4]]`. For models with heterogeneous layer groups (e.g. DeepSeek V4 with mixed compressed + dense groups), the fallback returns a single shape instead of per-group shapes, causing `memory_obj.group_prefix_sum` to be computed wrong. When `from_gpu()` later slices `memory_obj.get_tensor(i)` by `group_prefix_sum`, it reads out-of-bounds or misaligned data.

Also fix `memory_obj.tensor` → `memory_obj.raw_tensor` in `eic_connector` (3 sites). EIC needs the raw flat buffer for RDMA registration and cudaMemcpy; the `.tensor` property returns a reshape view that may be non-contiguous or offset, giving wrong `data_ptr()` under multi-group layouts.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- The V3 connector currently initializes lazily in `to_gpu()`/`from_gpu()`. This PR adds eager initialization at `register_kv_caches` time. The lazy path in `to_gpu`/`from_gpu` is preserved as a safety net (no-op if already init via `self.init` flag).
- The `eic_connector.py` change (`tensor` → `raw_tensor`) aligns with how other connectors access memory object data — `raw_tensor` is the underlying physical tensor, while `tensor` may return a permuted view.

title: [Feature][MP] Add an optional L2 prefetch load deadline with recompute fallback
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #4945.

Today a lookup-mode prefetch waits for the slowest L2 adapter. When a remote/disk tier stalls, the request stalls with it, even though recomputing the missing chunks would be faster. The only bounds we have are `lmcache.mp.mq_timeout` (a transport error after ~300 s) and the caller-side wait in `wait_prefetch_result`, which returns `None` and leaves the job running. Neither gives the caller a usable result.

This adds `--l2-prefetch-load-timeout <seconds>` (`StorageManagerConfig.prefetch_load_timeout`, default unset = current behaviour). The budget starts when the request is submitted to the `PrefetchController` and covers queueing, L2 lookup and L2 load. When it expires the caller gets a normal final result: whatever is usable right now, run through the existing `build_trim_mask`, with the rest reported as a miss. WARM requests are not armed since nobody is waiting on them.

The main change is splitting what `_complete_request` did into two lifecycles:

- caller: `ACTIVE -> PUBLISHED | PUBLISHED_TIMEOUT`, via a single `_publish_result_once`
- resources: `ACTIVE -> DRAINING -> RETIRED`, via `_retire_request_once`

Normal completion publishes and retires in one step, as before. On timeout the result is published and the request keeps draining: adapters that are still running keep their L1 write reservations and L2 locks until they report. Every buffer that belongs to an adapter task that has already returned is resolved right away, at the deadline and again on each late completion (loaded keys become resident, failed keys are deleted), so a failed key does not wait for the slowest adapter. When the last task reports, `_finish_drain` returns the L2 locks and retires the request. Nothing is cancelled and no adapter interface changes. Late completions cannot republish or alter the result.

What counts as usable at the deadline:

- lookup phase: L1 hits only. An L2 key that was found but not loaded is not a hit.
- load phase: L1 hits plus loads whose completions the controller has already observed. Completions signalled in the same event-loop wake are processed before expiry. This is an event-loop ordering rule, not a timestamped guarantee about physical I/O completion time.
- still queued: the L1 lock + trim is done synchronously and only L2 is skipped.

L1 read locks outside the retained set are released at publish time; loaded-but-trimmed keys stay resident and unlocked so the next request can use them. Write-buffer finalization for the normal, deadline and drain paths goes through one helper (`_finalize_write_reserved`).

The event loop bounds its poll by the nearest deadline: in-flight requests and the first armed entry in the pending queue (deadlines are stamped under the submission lock, so armed entries are ordered; WARM entries in between carry no deadline and are skipped). A request that has gone past its deadline by the time it is admitted takes the queued fallback instead of starting L2 work. The deadline is checked again when the last lookup result would transition the request into the load phase, so an already-expired request does not allocate load buffers or submit new L2 I/O. The timeout must be a finite positive number, checked both in config validation and in the controller constructor. With the option unset no request is armed and the loop never reads the clock.

Observability: `L2_PREFETCH_DEADLINE` event with `phase` (queued / lookup / load), budget, elapsed, retained and missed chunk counts; `lmcache_mp_l2_prefetch_deadline_{requests,retained_chunks,missed_chunks}_total{phase=…}`; `deadline_timeout_count` and `draining_request_count` in `report_status`.

One behaviour to be aware of: a draining request keeps its `max_in_flight` slot, because its buffers and locks are still owned by the adapter. With a persistently slow L2 the slots fill with drainers and queued requests then fall back at their own deadline with their L1 hits. I think that is the right backpressure, and `draining_request_count` makes it visible, but it is a choice.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Config placement: this is a server flag rather than an `lmcache.mp.*` connector key (where `mq_timeout` from #4935 lives), because the controller is built from `StorageManagerConfig`; the name follows `prefetch_max_in_flight` / `--l2-prefetch-max-in-flight`. Happy to rename.
- `mq_timeout` should stay well above this value so the fallback returns over a healthy RPC; documented in `docs/source/mp/configuration.rst`.
- Shutdown is out of scope and unchanged. `PrefetchController.stop()` still frees the remaining write reservations after joining the loop thread, before `StorageManager` closes the adapters, exactly as on `dev`; an adapter that is still writing at that point is a pre-existing hazard that this PR does not attempt to resolve. The shutdown test here only checks the controller's own bookkeeping. Tracked separately in #5263, with a repro that fails the same way on `dev`.
- L2 read locks are returned when the drain finishes rather than at publish time. Releasing the finished adapters' locks earlier needs a per-adapter split in `_release_l2_locks`; I left it out to keep this PR contained.

Tests use an injected clock and a mock adapter that is gated before it writes into the buffer (so the load really is late, not just its notification); partial and late-load tests wait on explicit events (slow load entered, fast result consumed by the controller) before moving the clock. `tests/v1/distributed/test_prefetch_deadline.py` (49) covers: disabled = unchanged; timeout in queue / lookup / load; zero and partial completion under PREFIX / SEGMENTED_PREFIX / SPARSE with a hole before a completed key, asserting L1 lock and reservation state rather than just the bitmap; hit already reported at load submit, then a smaller retained set; completion-vs-deadline in both orders, each forced by the gate; late completion leaves the result untouched; load failure during drain; fast-success + slow-failure adapters; drainers holding slots, queue expiry, then admission; same-key retry; config validation. `test_prefetch_deadline_edges.py` (5) covers nan/inf/huge timeouts, a WARM entry at the queue head with the production 500 ms poll and no other wakeups, no clock reads while disabled, expiry at admission, and failed buffers of a returned adapter being freed while another adapter is still loading. `test_prefetch_deadline_transition.py` adds 11 focused cases for the lookup-to-load deadline boundary, the unarmed path, completion precedence, drain-only requests and unsignalled requests. `tests/v1/multiprocess/test_lookup_deadline_status.py` checks the MP handler returns a normal final status and removes the `_PrefetchJob`, and that the existing wait-timeout-returns-`None` behaviour is unchanged.

The following repository and service results are from head `c0265b9c`, before the final lookup-to-load transition guard in `ce25ee33`. The added file compiles and the transition logic passed its focused CPU method-level checks; the complete repository suites and E2E run still need to be repeated on the latest head.

```

pytest tests/v1/distributed                                     1164 passed

```

End to end on `c0265b9c` (`lmcache server` + vLLM `71fc70d3` with `LMCacheMPConnector`, Qwen2.5-1.5B, RTX 4090 D; mock L2 throttled with `mock_bandwidth_gb`, `--l2-store-policy skip_l1` so the second request has to load 6 chunks from L2):


After the late load drained, a third request with the same prefix was served from cache (6 of 6 chunks, 337 ms) with no second timeout. I could not get a partially-retained fallback out of the public CLI (a mock load is all-or-nothing per adapter and the store policy is server-wide), so partial completion is covered by the unit tests only.

title: feat(storage): expose native CPU residency snapshots and replay
body:
Native CPU cache consumers currently cannot distinguish submitted writes from readable objects or reliably recover after eviction and missed events. Add opt-in, metadata-only `LocalCPUBackend.residency_snapshot()` and `residency_events()` APIs backed by a bounded journal under the existing mutation lock.

Actual insertions and removals, including batched allocator eviction, advance object versions and the replay cursor. Snapshots have a consistent cut; expired cursors and changed boot epochs require resnapshot. Duplicate puts are idempotent, and observation does not pin objects, change LRU state, invoke user callbacks, or retain KV allocations.

Validation: 34 LocalCPUBackend tests passed inside `rocm/atom-dev:nightly_202609200436-lirzhang-rocm-ordering-edge`, including concurrent writers/replay, duplicate put/recreate, pinned clear and replay expiry. The image's native extension was retained while the modified Python modules were overlaid. Ruff checks/formatting passed in the Ruff container image. The full multi-backend suite was not run.

This is an independent API proposal. The ATOM routing implementation in ROCm/ATOM#2307 and ROCm/ATOM#2308 uses stock LMCache's existing public get_keys() API and does not require this PR. The ATOM-only path trades per-mutation replay for periodic key snapshots; this proposal can be reviewed separately as a more efficient observation API.

The branch remains a draft managed with gh stack and is pushed through a fork because upstream write access is unavailable.

title: [Core] Avoid redundant work in ranked bitmap folding
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Ranked bitmap folding keeps checking longer prefixes after a full-attention group has a missing shard, even though none of those prefixes can be served. Track the remaining candidate-prefix bound and stop that group's scan at the first incomplete chunk. Later groups and output construction use the same bound. Full-attention groups also avoid maintaining a sliding-window run.

Inline the existing bounds-checked `Bitmap::test` query so the per-rank loop does not make an out-of-line call for every bit. For windowed groups, express `run < min(window, prefix_len)` as two comparisons, avoiding the preceding bitmap read. Sliding windows can still recover after earlier misses; the ranked layout, output size and retain-mask semantics are unchanged.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Measured the real Python `build_trim_mask(..., TrimPolicy.PREFIX, ...)` path, including fold/unfold and wrapper overhead, against dev `1a4b40b1d79b0e76244f127f96ee0982f8bd270f`. Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+, GCC 13.3 / `-O3 -std=c++17`, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Separate processes ran base/patch/patch/base/base/patch pinned to one allocated CPU core; each process used one warm-up batch and five timed batches. The table shows medians of the three process medians, in microseconds. Input construction and correctness checks are outside timing.

Here, hit chunks are a contiguous present prefix; the rest are absent. `-1` denotes full attention and `4` a four-chunk sliding window.

| Chunks | Ranks | Group windows | Hit chunks | Before (µs) | After (µs) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | 1 | `[4, 4]` | 0 | 1.788 | 1.827 |
| 512 | 8 | `[-1]` | 0 | 3.001 | 1.757 |
| 512 | 8 | `[-1]` | 256 | 7.155 | 4.690 |
| 512 | 8 | `[-1]` | 512 | 9.982 | 7.468 |
| 512 | 8 | `[-1, 4]` | 0 | 4.121 | 1.765 |
| 512 | 8 | `[-1, 4]` | 512 | 15.949 | 11.340 |
| 512 | 8 | `[4, 4]` | 512 | 14.647 | 10.298 |

The smallest controls are effectively flat: the largest increase was 0.039 µs (+2.2%), with overlapping baseline/patched process ranges. The broader checks cover 96 contiguous-prefix cases and 120 first-gap cases with a present suffix, including all hits, mixed windows, and ranks 1/8. These are synthetic metadata workloads, not end-to-end serving throughput or TTFT results. Bitmap allocation remains proportional to the request length; this is not a constant-time operation.

This helper runs at cache lookup/prefetch phase boundaries, not once per generated token or transformer layer. Pending status polls return before folding; the completed result is consumed once. Several folds can occur during one prefetch lifecycle, with different bitmap sizes and contents. The table measures one whole bitmap invocation, so chunks/ranks are not additional invocation multipliers. No request-level or model-level speedup is claimed.

Validation:

- `pytest tests/v1/lmcache_native tests/v1/distributed/test_bitmap_ops.py -q`: **520 passed** on both baseline and patch, with the added tests on both.
- `pytest tests/v1/distributed/test_prefetch_controller.py tests/v1/distributed/test_distributed_storage_manager.py tests/v1/distributed/test_bitmap_ops.py -q`: **239 passed** on both baseline and patch with one RTX 5090 (overlaps bitmap_ops above). The real native C++ extension was built; GPU-adjacent tests used the existing Torch CUDA fallback, without building custom LMCache CUDA kernels.
- AddressSanitizer + UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: standalone oracle using the actual Bitmap/fold sources passed, including full/mixed/sliding windows and first-gap boundaries.
- `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy pre-commit run --all-files`: passed all applicable hooks; no Rust changes.

New tests check non-positive full-attention values, missing shards across groups/ranks and byte boundaries, empty/full-hit inputs, and mixed-window group ordering against the existing Python reference. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation preparation.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the contiguous-prefix microbenchmark</summary>

Run this unchanged in separate baseline/patched processes with the native extension built, alternating their order as above. It asserts the hit length, retained indices and input immutability.

```python
"""Production helper benchmark for empty, contiguous-prefix, and full hits."""
import gc
import json
import os
import statistics
import time

import torch
from lmcache.lmcache_native import Bitmap
from lmcache.v1.distributed.api import AttnWindowDesc, TrimPolicy
from lmcache.v1.distributed.storage_controllers.prefetch_controller import build_trim_mask

os.sched_setaffinity(0, {min(os.sched_getaffinity(0))})
torch.set_num_threads(2)
for chunks in [16, 128, 512, 2048]:
    for ranks in [1, 8]:
        for windows in [[-1], [-1, -1], [-1, 4], [4, 4]]:
            stride = ranks * len(windows)
            count = chunks * stride
            desc = AttnWindowDesc(num_chunks_in_sw=windows, world_size=ranks)
            for hit in [0, chunks // 2, chunks]:
                found = Bitmap(count, hit * stride)
                expected = []
                for g, window in enumerate(windows):
                    for j in range(0 if window <= 0 else max(0, hit - window), hit):
                        expected.extend(range((j * len(windows) + g) * ranks, (j * len(windows) + g + 1) * ranks))
                expected.sort()
                result = build_trim_mask(found, count, TrimPolicy.PREFIX, desc)
                assert result[0] == hit and result[1].get_indices_list() == expected
                before = repr(found)
                reps = max(30, min(2000, 100000 // chunks))
                samples = []
                gc.disable()
                try:
                    for sample in range(6):
                        start = time.perf_counter_ns()
                        for _ in range(reps):
                            result = build_trim_mask(found, count, TrimPolicy.PREFIX, desc)
                        elapsed = (time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / reps / 1000
                        if sample:
                            samples.append(elapsed)
                finally:
                    gc.enable()
                assert result[0] == hit and result[1].get_indices_list() == expected
                assert repr(found) == before
                print(json.dumps(dict(chunks=chunks, ranks=ranks, windows=windows, hit=hit,
                                      median_us=statistics.median(samples), samples_us=samples)), flush=True)

```

</details>

title: [Bugfix] Synchronize the KV tensor device in engine-driven transfers
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**

Engine-driven copies follow the KV tensor device, but synchronization still uses the process-global backend. CPU transfers can therefore wait for unrelated CUDA work, and CUDA transfers may synchronize the wrong GPU.

This patch makes synchronization follow the KV device and skips it for CPU tensors. Existing synchronization boundaries, async STORE stream/event ordering, and buffer lifetime guarantees are preserved.

**Reproduction and results**

Run the CPU regression test:

```
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/multiprocess/test_engine_driven_device_dispatch.py \
  -k test_cpu_context_never_synchronizes_accelerator
```

The same test fails on unpatched `dev` with `unexpected accelerator sync` and passes with this fix.

A separate real-CUDA experiment queued unrelated GPU work before CPU STORE:

| CPU STORE | CUDA sync calls: before → after | Time: before → after |
| --------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| pickle    | 2 → 0                           | 118.334 → 0.352 ms   |
| SHM       | 2 → 0                           | 118.504 → 0.417 ms   |

After the fix, CPU data remained correct while GPU work was still pending. These are controlled diagnostic timings, not application speedup claims.

**Validation**

| Path                         | Verified guarantee                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Sync CUDA engine-driven      | Copies complete before commit or buffer release              |
| Async engine-driven STORE    | Producer-event dependencies and staging lifetime are preserved |
| Async engine-driven RETRIEVE | Inherited synchronous retrieve completes copies before release |
| Shared gather/scatter        | Staging is CPU-readable and temporary pinned buffers outlive copies |

On two RTX 4090 GPUs, **128 rounds per version** passed across sync/async contexts, both GPUs, FP16/BF16, and pickle/SHM buffers. Completion checks ran before `.cpu()` verification to avoid masking missing synchronization.

title: [Bugfix] Fix full-hit Mamba checkpoint restoration in vLLM MP connector
body:
## Summary

Fix incorrect recurrent-state restoration when a vLLM request fully hits LMCache on an LMCache chunk boundary.

Fix issue: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/5151

## Problem

vLLM recomputes the final prompt token after a full external-cache hit.

This is safe for full attention and sliding-window attention because the final token's KV is overwritten. For Mamba/recurrent layers, however, the restored checkpoint already includes the final token. Recomputing it applies the recurrent-state transition twice and may cause incorrect output.

## Solution

- Detect Mamba cache modes that restore reusable checkpoints (`align` and `all`).
- Exclude the final prompt token before aligning the LMCache lookup range.
- Make the lookup server honor `IPCCacheServerKey.end` when computing chunk hashes.
- Keep full-attention and SWA behavior unchanged.

## Tests

Added unit tests covering:

- Last-token reservation and chunk alignment.
- Recurrent lookup submission.
- Server-side enforcement of the lookup end boundary.
