title: Allow vllm cache salt
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #2878 

Before this change, vLLM local APC respected `cache_salt`, but LMCache external KV lookup/store did not. That allowed two requests with the same prompt but different salts to reuse the same LMCache entry.

This PR threads salted request configs through all relevant vLLM adapter paths:
- lookup
- req meta / tracker creation
- retrieve
- layerwise retrieve
- blending retrieve
- store
- layerwise store

It also stores a backend-safe salt-derived tag instead of the raw salt:
- tag key: `lmcache.tag.cachesalt`
- tag value: `sha256(cache_salt).hexdigest()`

This avoids backend key-format issues and avoids exposing the raw salt in LMCache object keys.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- This is important to align with vLLM cache salt behavior and properly enabled cache isolation. 
- Requests without `cache_salt` keep the existing LMCache behavior.

**If applicable**:

- [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [x] this PR contains unit tests

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how LMCache keys are scoped by threading `cache_salt` into lookup/retrieve/store paths, which can affect cache hit rates and correctness of cross-request reuse. Risk is mitigated by hashing the salt into a stable tag and adding focused unit tests around the new plumbing.
> 
> **Overview**
> Ensures vLLM `cache_salt` is honored by LMCache by extending `extract_request_configs` to add a backend-safe `lmcache.tag.cachesalt` tag (SHA-256 of the salt) and propagating the resulting `request_configs` through request tracking and connector metadata.
> 
> Plumbs `request_configs` into **all** relevant execution paths (lookup, layerwise/non-layerwise retrieve, blending, and layerwise store), and adds new unit tests validating salt hashing and that `request_configs` are passed through to engine/blender calls; updates existing layerwise save tests to include `request_configs` on requests.

title: refactor: single-source the EngineKVFormat enum via engine_kv_format.def
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Refs #3674 (follow-up to #3676, per @hlin99's request to single-source the fallback enum).

`EngineKVFormat`'s members were hand-duplicated across **four** places that had to be kept in sync manually — the #3673 rename had to touch all of them:
- the C++ `enum class` — `csrc/kv_transfer_types.h`
- the CUDA pybind registration — `csrc/pybind.cpp`
- the SYCL pybind registration — `csrc/sycl/pybind_sycl.cpp`
- the pure-Python fallback enum — `lmcache/python_ops_fallback.py`

This makes **`csrc/engine_kv_format.def` the single source of truth** (an X-macro list). The C++ enum and both pybind `.value()` blocks generate their members from it via the preprocessor (`#include`); a pre-commit hook (`gen-engine-kv-format`) runs `tools/gen_engine_kv_format.py` to render a static, typed Python mirror (`lmcache/_engine_kv_format.py`) that the fallback imports. **Adding a KV layout is now a one-line edit to the `.def`.**

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- **No behavioral change.** Enum names and values (0–10) are identical to `dev`; the `GPUKVFormat` back-compat alias is preserved. Verified `.def` == generated mirror == the previous hand-written enum.
- **Why codegen rather than parsing the `.def` at runtime (Python side):** the fallback references enum members by name in ~40 places and mypy is enforced — a dynamically-built `IntEnum` loses statically-known members and breaks type-checking. Generating a static module keeps it fully typed and ships normally (committed `.py`, **no packaging or build-system changes**). Enum parity between the compiled `c_ops` enum and the Python mirror then holds **by construction**.
- **No build-system change.** The C++ side is pure-preprocessor `#include` (hipify-safe; nothing generated before compile); only the Python mirror is generated, via pre-commit (freshness enforced in CI like `ruff-format`).
- **New pattern for LMCache.** No prior codegen in the repo; used a pre-commit codegen hook (closest in-ecosystem precedent: SGLang `code_gen.py`, vLLM `tools/generate_*.py`). Happy to adjust if you'd prefer a different mechanism.
- **`TransferDirection`** left hand-written (2 values, effectively never changes) — still guarded by the parity test. Can fold it in too if you'd like uniformity.
- **Design doc** `docs/design/v1/gpu_connector/layout-invariant.md` "Adding a new format" updated to the `.def` workflow (rebased on top of the recent `kv_format/` specs/detectors restructure).

**Testing** — built from source and run on **H100, CUDA 13.0**:

```bash
uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation     # builds: .def #include compiles under nvcc 13 (sm_90, ninja)

pytest tests/v1/test_c_ops_fallback_parity.py            # 38 passed, 1 skipped
pytest tests/v1/test_mem_kernels.py tests/v1/test_gpu_connector.py   # passed
pytest tests/v1/test_python_ops_fallback.py              # passed
pytest tests/test_gen_engine_kv_format.py                # 9 passed (CPU-only)
pre-commit run --all-files                               # green
```

- **`test_c_ops_fallback_parity.py` (the key check):** `test_enum_parity[EngineKVFormat]`, `[GPUKVFormat]`, `[TransferDirection]`, plus `test_all_c_ops_enums_have_fallback` / `_callables_` / `_descriptors_` all pass → the **compiled `c_ops` enum equals the generated Python mirror**.
- **Runtime smoke:** `c_ops.EngineKVFormat.__members__` → 11 entries (0–10); `GPUKVFormat is EngineKVFormat` → `True`.

title: feat(s3): opt-in per-cache_salt bucket isolation for multi-tenancy
body:
## Summary

Opt-in **per-`cache_salt` S3 bucket isolation** for the S3 L2 adapter: route each tenant's KV to its **own physical S3 bucket**, keyed by `cache_salt`. On a shared multi-tenant inference box, no two tenants share a bucket — one tenant's writes never consume or evict another's cache, and there is no cross-tenant read path. Default behavior is **unchanged** (single bucket); the feature is entirely opt-in.

## Motivation

Today the S3 backend is single-bucket: every tenant's KV lands in one bucket and `cache_salt` only prefixes the object key. For multi-tenant serving that means **shared capacity** (one tenant can fill or LRU-evict another's entries) and a shared blast radius. Physical per-tenant buckets give hard isolation plus independent lifecycle/capacity per tenant.

## Design (default-safe)

Two new optional `S3L2AdapterConfig` fields, both defaulting to **exact current behavior**:

- `s3_bucket_mode`: `"single"` (default) | `"per_cache_salt"`
- `s3_bucket_template`: bucket-name format for per-salt mode; supports `{salt}` (sanitized `cache_salt`) and `{base}` (the configured bucket name), e.g. `"kv-cache-{salt}"` or `"{base}-{salt}"`.

In `per_cache_salt` mode:

- **Routing** — `_make_request` (PUT/GET/HEAD/DELETE) sets the virtual-hosted `Host` per key. The CRT `S3Client` is **region-bound, not bucket-bound**, so a single client serves all tenant buckets — only the per-request `Host` changes. Unsalted keys and `single` mode keep the configured bucket.
- **Listing / eviction** — `list_l2_keys` iterates the base bucket plus every observed tenant bucket with a composite cursor, so the eviction controller sees keys across all tenant buckets and issued deletes route back to the correct bucket.
- **Provisioning** — the first write to a tenant bucket idempotently creates it (plus a configurable lifecycle TTL) via boto3; failures are logged, not raised. Can be turned off to require buckets be pre-created by an onboarding hook.

The routing logic lives in a new **dependency-free** module `s3_bucket_router.py` (no `awscrt` / `lmcache` imports) so it is unit-testable and reviewable in isolation.

## Tests

- `tests/v1/distributed/test_s3_bucket_router.py` — 10 unit cases: sanitize, `single`-mode no-op, per-salt routing, distinct tenants → distinct buckets, unsalted → base, `{base}`/`{salt}` placeholders, cross-bucket listing, cursor roundtrip.
- **Validated end-to-end** on a multi-replica 8×GPU box (vLLM + LMCache MP, S3 L2), not just unit tests:
  - **Isolation** — two tenants → two separate buckets, `0` objects leaked into the base/other bucket.
  - **Read reuse** — identical prompt twice under one tenant → cold prefill then a full KV cache hit (the load path works through per-tenant routing).
  - **Provisioning** — tenant buckets auto-created with the lifecycle TTL on first write.
  - **Eviction** — under sustained load the L2 eviction controller crossed its watermark and evicted (deleted) from the per-tenant bucket; footprint stayed bounded by the cap.
  - `single` mode is byte-for-byte unchanged (covered by the existing `test_s3_l2_adapter.py`).

## Notes

Draft for now — happy to take feedback on the config surface and on whether auto-provisioning belongs in the adapter or in a separate onboarding hook.

title: feat(s3-l2): make LRU eviction survive process restarts (opt-in)
body:
## Summary

Make the **S3 L2 cache's LRU eviction survive process restarts**. Today the adapter's byte counter and the eviction policy's key index are **in-memory** — they reset to 0 on every restart / pod replacement / spot reclaim. So a fresh process doesn't "see" the objects already in the bucket, can't evict them, and the bucket grows across process generations until the lifecycle TTL ages it out. The configured **LRU cap stops bounding the bucket across restarts**. This adds two opt-in mechanisms to fix that. Both default **off** → no behavior change for existing deployments.

Independent of (and complementary to) the per-`cache_salt` bucket PR (#3892) — different branch, different files-of-concern.

## (a) `s3_seed_usage_on_start` (default `False`)

On startup, scan the bucket (paginated `ListObjectsV2`, progress-logged, non-fatal on error) and **seed both**:
- the adapter usage counter (`_total_bytes_used`), and
- the eviction **policy's** key index,

using S3 `LastModified` as the access-order proxy (oldest-modified = first victim). After seeding, `_check_and_evict_global` sees the true footprint and evicts down to the cap immediately — across any restart.

The load-bearing detail: seeding usage alone is useless; the policy must get the keys too. The path is `_notify_keys_stored` → `L2EvictionPolicy.on_l2_keys_stored` → `policy.on_keys_created` → `LRUEvictionPolicy._order`. `on_keys_created` reverses keys within a call, so seeding is done **one key at a time, oldest-LastModified-first**, which lands the oldest object at the front of `_order` (first eviction victim) — verified against the real `LRUEvictionPolicy`.

## (b) `s3_persist_lru_index` (default `False`, `s3_lru_index_checkpoint_interval_s` default 300)

(a) uses `LastModified` as the order proxy, which mis-ranks a **hot-but-old** prefix (created first, reused thousands of times, never rewritten) → it could be evicted despite being hot. To preserve **true access-order** across restarts:
- A daemon thread periodically serializes the access-order index (key → size + last-access tick) to a compact JSON sidecar (`_lmcache_lru_index.json`); access ticks are only recorded when the flag is on (hot path untouched otherwise).
- On startup, restore the index from the sidecar (true LRU order), reconcile against the live listing (drop vanished keys; append new-since-checkpoint keys by `LastModified` as coldest), and rebuild the tick counter. A missing/partial/corrupt/unknown-version sidecar is treated as absent → falls back to (a)'s scan. `close()` writes a final checkpoint.

## Tests

`tests/v1/distributed/test_s3_l2_adapter_seed.py` — 18 unit tests (stub awscrt/torch; pure logic runs for real, including against the real `LRUEvictionPolicy`): `LastModified` parsing + ordering, size-summing, **policy `_order` population in eviction order**, skip-already-known, sidecar serialize/deserialize roundtrip, corrupt/partial/unknown-version → treated as absent, tick recording gated by the flag.

## Notes / open questions (flagged, not guessed)
- Tick-tracking lives in the **adapter** (it already sees every store/read) rather than reaching into the policy's private `_order`. If you'd prefer the checkpoint to live with the policy, that's a design call.
- On restore, objects present in the bucket but absent from the sidecar are placed as **coldest** (evicted first). If brand-new-since-checkpoint objects should instead be treated as hot, that ordering should flip.
- Seeding calls `_notify_keys_stored` once per key to preserve exact order (one-time startup cost); a batched order-preserving insert on the policy would speed huge-bucket seeds but doesn't exist today.

Draft for now — feedback welcome on the config surface and the two ordering questions above.

title: docs(mp): correct hybrid-model support surface + connector config gotchas
body:
## Problem

The MP hybrid-models doc contradicts itself. The support table lists **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **GLM 5.2** as supported (with recipes), but the *What Is Not Supported Yet* section still says:

> DeepSeek-V4-style compressed / indexer caches are not yet handled by the multiprocess connector.

That is stale. `validate_kv_cache_groups` (`lmcache/integration/vllm/kv_cache_group_edits.py`) does **not** reject slot-compression specs (`compress_ratio > 1` / `tq_slot_size > 0`) — they are served by the compression path in `lmcache.v1.kv_layer_groups` and are explicitly skipped by the edits. The connector actually rejects only two spec kinds.

Validated end-to-end: GLM 5.2 (Dynamic Sparse Attention / IndexShare, INT4 TP4) serves through `LMCacheMPConnector` and stores KV to an S3 L2 tier via the `lmcache server`.

## Changes (docs/docstring only — no behavior change)

- **`docs/source/mp/hybrid_models.rst`** — replace the stale "not yet handled" bullet with the real reject list: `CrossAttentionSpec` (encoder-decoder) and non-`align` Mamba groups only; state plainly that DeepSeek-V4-style compressed/indexer caches **are** supported, with links to the DeepSeek-V4-Flash and GLM 5.2 recipes.
- **`lmcache/integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector.py`** — clarify in the docstring that `lmcache.mp.host` must include the transport scheme (default `tcp://localhost`); the final URL is `{host}:{port}`, so a bare host silently builds an invalid ZMQ address. Point users to `lmcache.mp.server_urls` for full control.
- **`docs/source/mp/deployment.rst`** — broaden the `--ipc host` note: it's required for CUDA IPC to a **host-process** LMCache server too (not only container-to-container); without it the connector hangs at `Creating transfer context`.

## Notes

Follow-up to #3892 / #3932. Pure documentation + one docstring; no code paths touched.

title: [TPU] Add tpu integration: LMCacheStorageKVStore host-bytes backend
body:
## Summary

Adds `lmcache.integration.tpu` — a host-side raw-bytes KV store (`LMCacheStorageKVStore`) that lets LMCache serve as a persistent storage tier behind the vLLM **[tpu-inference](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference)** `TPUOffloadConnector`. Companion PR: vllm-project/tpu-inference (adds the `LMCacheHostBackend` that calls this).

## Context / why this design

On TPU, KV cache lives as **JAX arrays** in an XLA mesh, and tpu-inference's `TPUOffloadConnector` already owns the HBM↔host movement, staging, and scheduler-side content hashing. Rather than port LMCache's torch/CUDA GPU connectors to JAX (LMCache has no `torch_xla` device path today, and `tpu_platform` hard-allowlists KV connectors), the connector hands LMCache a flat, host-resident **byte buffer** per KV block (bit-exact, incl. bfloat16) + a stable key, and LMCache provides the tiers below host RAM.

## What's in this PR

`lmcache/integration/tpu/lmcache_storage_kv_store.py`: `LMCacheStorageKVStore` exposes `put/get/remove/contains` over raw bytes, persisting via content-addressed `CacheEngineKey` (`model@world@worker@hash@dtype`) + disk serialization with LRU disk-usage accounting. No `torch_xla` / JAX dependency — runs on any host. Plus a README and host-only unit tests.

## Testing

`tests/v1/integration/tpu/test_lmcache_storage_kv_store.py` — 6 host-only tests (put/get/remove, overwrite, content-addressed file naming, LRU disk eviction, stable hashing, from_env). Runs standalone (`--noconftest`), no torch_xla/JAX/transformers needed.

## Real-hardware validation (tpu7x)

The paired tpu-inference `LMCacheHostBackend` + this raw-bytes path (reference `file` backend) was validated **bit-for-bit on a real tpu7x 2x2x1 slice** via tpu-inference's `offline_inference_kv_cache_verification.py`: both the default-off path and a forced-spill run produced output bit-for-bit identical to the no-connector baseline; a direct probe confirmed disk eviction+reload is bit-exact including bfloat16.

We also ran a 4-arm KV-cache benchmark (0.5B + 7B, real tpu7x): the disk tier is correct and materializes bit-exact spilled KV, and beats the native CPU-offload tier on extended-tier hit-rate. Honest caveat: on dense-reuse single-host workloads the reuse pool stays HBM-resident so the tier is rarely read back — its win is temporally-sparse reuse (large working set, low prompts/group). Follow-up: wire the full `StorageManager` so TPU serving can use the remote/distributed tiers (Redis/Mooncake/NIXL) for cross-instance sharing.

Note: this targets `dev`; I saw #3924 (device-detection refactor) landed recently — this PR adds only new files under `lmcache/integration/tpu/` so it's independent of that change.

---
*Developed with assistance from Navi (an AI coding assistant); all code was reviewed and the benchmarks were run + verified on real tpu7x hardware.*

title: Optimize gRPC normal handler dispatch
body:
## Summary

- run non-affinity gRPC `HandlerType.BLOCKING` handlers directly on the gRPC worker while preserving `max_cpu_workers` with a bounded semaphore
- add an internal persistent gRPC stream transport for request dispatch, shared per target, so multiple logical `GrpcMultiprocessClient`s can reuse one gRPC stream instead of paying one unary RPC setup per tiny request
- micro-batch frames on the shared stream with a short 5 us coalescing window; each frame carries its logical client key so affinity handlers still route by logical client, not by the shared stream
- add regression tests for the CPU worker limit, gRPC future polling semantics, shared-stream logical client affinity, and shared transport close/ref-count behavior
- add `benchmarks/microbenchmark/grpc_dispatch_benchmark.py` for reproducible ZMQ/gRPC dispatch overhead measurements

## Performance

Environment: local macOS CPU-only run, Python 3.12, generated gRPC protobuf bindings, `grpcio==1.78.0`. Commands:

```bash
python lmcache/v1/multiprocess/transport/grpc_impl/_proto_gen/_generate.py
uv run python benchmarks/microbenchmark/grpc_dispatch_benchmark.py \
  --transport grpc \
  --warmup 100 --calls 2000 --workers 8 --calls-per-worker 500 \
  --max-cpu-workers 8 --grpc-server-workers 32
uv run python benchmarks/microbenchmark/grpc_dispatch_benchmark.py \
  --transport zmq \
  --warmup 100 --calls 2000 --workers 8 --calls-per-worker 500 \
  --max-cpu-workers 8 --grpc-server-workers 32
```

### ZMQ versus optimized gRPC

3-run median on this branch:

| Case | ZMQ | optimized gRPC | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| sequential throughput | 5608.1 req/s | 7189.6 req/s | gRPC +28.2% |
| sequential p50 latency | 0.175 ms | 0.130 ms | gRPC -25.7% |
| concurrent-8 throughput | 9561.7 req/s | 19191.5 req/s | gRPC +100.7% |
| concurrent-8 p50 latency | 0.785 ms | 0.394 ms | gRPC -49.8% |

The main difference from the unary implementation is that the optimized gRPC path now amortizes gRPC call setup across a persistent stream and batches simultaneous tiny requests from multiple logical clients while preserving logical-client affinity metadata in each frame.

Full CPU server bench gRPC path also passed on this branch:

```bash
LMCACHE_REQUEST_TRANSPORT=grpc \
LMCACHE_BENCH_TRANSFER_MODE=engine_driven \
BENCH_NUM_REQUESTS=3 \
BENCH_NUM_TOKENS=512 \
bash .github/scripts/cpu_server_bench_test.sh
```

Result: 3/3 checksum matches, pass rate 100%.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest -q tests/v1/multiprocess/test_grpc_transport.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_affinity_pool.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_client.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_futures.py` -> 51 passed, 13 skipped
- `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy uv run pre-commit run --all-files` -> passed

- **`docs/source/mp/index.rst` — `modules/blend.py` reference is a broken path (in two places).** The MP overview describes the blend module as a single file (`modules/blend.py`) in the "Engine and Modules" narrative and again in the "Key Source Files" table. title: Add LMCache Operator Helm chart
body: **What this PR does / why we need it**: - Add a Helm chart for the LMCache Operator, CRDs, RBAC, services, webhooks, and certificates. - Generate `install.yaml` from the chart while preserving the existing `make deploy` command. - Package and publish the chart through the Operator release and nightly workflows. **Two follow-ups for publishing:** - Verify that the release and nightly workflows can push the Helm chart to Docker Hub OCI using the existing credentials. Confirm that `lmcache/lmcache-operator-chart` is public, the token has write access, and the published chart can be pulled anonymously. - Since Operator v0.5.5 is already released, manually package and publish Helm chart 0.5.5 after this PR merges, and attach the `.tgz` to the existing release. Merging this PR will not automatically publish a chart for that release. **If applicable**: - [x] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added - [ ] this PR contains unit tests **Validation** Install cert-manager: ```bash kubectl apply -f https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/download/v1.19.1/cert-manager.yaml kubectl rollout status deployment/cert-manager-webhook -n cert-manager --timeout=5m ``` Build the Operator image from this branch. The built image was made available on the test cluster nodes. ```bash cd operator docker build -t lmcache-operator:helm-2f84ec47 . ``` Install the Helm chart: ```bash helm upgrade --install lmcache-operator ./charts/lmcache-operator \ --namespace lmcache-operator-system --create-namespace \ --set image.repository=lmcache-operator \ --set image.tag=helm-2f84ec47 \ --wait --timeout 5m ``` Create the LMCache engine (`demo-engine.yaml`): ```yaml apiVersion: lmcache.lmcache.ai/v1alpha1 kind: LMCacheEngine metadata: name: demo-cache namespace: lmcache-demo spec: image: repository: lmcache/vllm-openai tag: latest pullPolicy: IfNotPresent l1: sizeGB: 10 server: port: 6555 chunkSize: 128 maxWorkers: 3 hashAlgorithm: blake3 ``` Create the vLLM workload (`demo-vllm.yaml`). It loads the pretrained Qwen2.5-0.5B weights; the Operator webhook injects the LMCache connection settings. ```yaml apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: vllm-demo namespace: lmcache-demo spec: replicas: 1 selector: matchLabels: app: vllm-demo template: metadata: labels: app: vllm-demo lmcache.ai/lmcache-inject: "true" annotations: lmcache.ai/lmcache-engine: demo-cache spec: runtimeClassName: nvidia nodeSelector: nvidia.com/gpu.present: "true" containers: - name: vllm image: lmcache/vllm-openai:latest imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent args: - Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B - --no-enable-prefix-caching - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.5" ports: - name: http containerPort: 8000 resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: 1 readinessProbe: httpGet: path: /v1/models port: http initialDelaySeconds: 20 periodSeconds: 5 failureThreshold: 120 ``` Apply the manifests: ```bash kubectl create namespace lmcache-demo kubectl apply -f demo-engine.yaml kubectl wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Running lmcacheengine/demo-cache -n lmcache-demo --timeout=5m kubectl apply -f demo-vllm.yaml kubectl rollout status deployment/vllm-demo -n lmcache-demo --timeout=10m ``` The Operator and both workload Pods were ready, and the serving certificate was `Ready=True`. Two identical requests each returned HTTP 200 with 1,548 prompt tokens and 32 generated tokens. The first stored 1,536 tokens in LMCache; the second retrieved them. Both responses contained the same generated text. LMCache logs: ```bash kubectl logs -n lmcache-demo daemonset/demo-cache ``` vLLM logs: ```bash kubectl logs -n lmcache-demo deployment/vllm-demo -c vllm ```

title: [Refactor] Group built-in devices under platform/devices
body:
## Summary

This is a structural follow-up to the directory-layout discussion in #4940. Instead of treating every package directly under `lmcache.v1.platform` as a device implementation, this PR gives built-in devices an explicit namespace.

- move the CPU, CUDA, HPU, MUSA, Neuron, NPU, RBLN, ROCm, and XPU packages under `lmcache/v1/platform/devices/`
- mirror device-specific tests under `tests/v1/platform/devices/<device>/`, while keeping cross-device abstraction tests at the platform test root
- mirror device-specific design docs under `docs/design/v1/platform/devices/`
- scope built-in `DeviceSpec` discovery to `lmcache.v1.platform.devices`
- keep generic platform modules, including torch operation fallbacks, outside device discovery
- update Python imports and dynamic module strings across runtime code, tests, benchmarks, build scripts, workflows, CODEOWNERS, and documentation
- update the pre-commit device-directory scan and all hardcoded Buildkite/test paths; the generic Buildkite path filter needs no directory-specific change
- add a regression test that verifies discovery scans only the device namespace

This keeps `torch_ops` directly under `platform` without making it look device-specific, while making both source and test device hierarchies explicit.

## Validation

- `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy pre-commit run --all-files`
- focused platform, MUSA, TensorRT-LLM, and multiprocess regression: `298 passed, 79 skipped`
- import/discovery smoke test: all eight built-in specs resolve from `lmcache.v1.platform.devices.*`, and `lmcache.v1.platform.backends` is absent

title: [cb] skip rope-less engine-group
body:
## What

Lets a kernel group declare "I have no rope content" by registering `-1` in `group_to_cache`. Both `rot_for_group` and `cache_for_group` return `None` for those groups, so the retrieve planner sends them down its existing skipped-group path. Validation widens from `[0, n_caches)` to `[-1, n_caches)`.

## Why

Rope-bearing recurrent hybrids (Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 GDN) have groups with no rotary content at all. Without a way to say so, the blend server assumes every group is rope-bearing, tries to compute re-RoPE geometry for the aux plane,  

Nothing caught this earlier because no model had both: NemotronH is NoPE (zero caches, everything skips), and attention-only models have no non-rope groups. Qwen3.5 is the first with both.

## Validation

- New test `test_ropeless_group_sentinel_skips_rerope`; `test_blend_rope.py` green (9/9).
- E2E on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3.8-27B with `group_map=[-1,-1,-1,0,-1]`: native plans build, blends complete at delta-0 and shifted positions, warm-vs-cold F1 delta −0.003.
- Backward compatible — uniform (`[]`) and NoPE registrations are untouched.

title: [Bugfix][CB] Per-token scatter mis-addresses padded blocks-first pools (missing block_stride_elems)
body:
## Descriptions

vLLM 0.29.x added padding between Mamba state blocks in hybrid models such as Nemotron-3-Nano. Engine-driven gather/scatter and CB per-token scatter ignored this padding, reading and writing the wrong memory for every block after the first.

This corrupted outputs and slowed CB workloads. vLLM 0.28’s unpadded layout masked both bugs.

## Fix

Pass the physical block stride through both transfer paths to the CUDA kernels, which already support it. Unpadded layouts retain existing behavior.

## Validation

- All 8 byte-level regression tests pass, covering both layouts and checking neighboring blocks and padding. Padded cases reproduce the corruption without the fix.
- All 178 adjacent tests pass.

title: [Feature][MP] windowed kv commit policy
body:
<!--  Thanks for your contribution to LMCache!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'Fixes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'Refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

This is the draft implementation discussing in https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/5073

> Problem
Hybrid models (Gemma 3, gpt-oss, Command-A, Qwen3-Next, ...) have object groups that only need the last w chunks for a prefix hit (SWA, Mamba). Older windowed chunks are never read back, and they are the big ones. default writes them all to L2. But skipping them isn't enough: once L1 evicts the window, the next turn pays a full prefill. We should commit only the last w chunks, at the turn boundary.

> Proposal
Two pieces that work together: stop writing windowed KV to L2, and copy the live window to L2 at natural timing (turn boundaries) so cross-turn prefix reuse isn't lost.

title: [fix] gpu_connector: fix direct transfer in VLLMPagedMemLayerwiseGPUConnector
body: ## Summary Fix two bugs in `VLLMPagedMemLayerwiseGPUConnector` that broke the direct (non-buffered) transfer path: KV format metadata was never initialized when `use_gpu=False`, and `batched_to_gpu` passed the wrong `slot_mapping` slice per chunk. ## Bug 1: `_lazy_initialize_buffer` skipped format discovery when `use_gpu=False` Problem: `_lazy_initialize_buffer` only ran format discovery and metadata setup inside if `self.use_gpu` and `self.gpu_buffer_allocator` is None. When `use_gpu=False`, the function returned without setting engine_kv_format, tokens_per_layer, or elements_per_layer. Impact: The direct transfer path in `batched_to_gpu` (and batched_from_gpu) still calls `lmc_ops.single_layer_kv_transfer(..., self.engine_kv_format, ...)`, which requires the engine KV layout to be discovered first. With use_gpu=False, that attribute was never initialized, so the direct path could not work. Fix: Split lazy initialization into two phases: 1. Always discover KV format metadata from `kv_caches` on first use (needed for both direct and buffered transfers). 2. Create the GPU buffer pool only when `use_gpu=True`. Also updated the docstring and inline comments to reflect this two-phase behavior. ## Bug 2: `batched_to_gpu` used full `slot_mapping` in the direct path Problem: In the `use_gpu=False` branch, each chunk’s H2D transfer passed `slot_mapping_full` to single_layer_kv_transfer instead of the chunk-local slice `slot_mapping_full[start:end]`. Impact: For batched requests with multiple chunks, every chunk was mapped using the entire slot mapping. That misaligns token-to-page placement relative to each chunk’s `memory_obj`, leading to incorrect or corrupted KV cache writes. This matches the bug pattern already avoided in `batched_from_gpu`, which correctly uses `slot_mapping[start:end]` in its direct path. Fix: Pass `slot_mapping_full[start:end]` so each chunk’s transfer only uses the slots corresponding to that chunk’s token range. Tests - Parameterize test_layerwise_vllm_paged_connector_with_gpu over use_gpu=[True, False] to cover both buffered and direct paths. - Guard the gpu_buffer_allocator.memcheck() assertion with if use_gpu, since no allocator is created in direct mode. Test plan pytest - [✅] tests/v1/test_gpu_connector.py::test_layerwise_vllm_paged_connector_with_gpu -v passes for both use_gpu=True and use_gpu=False - [✅] Existing layerwise connector tests still pass with use_gpu=True

title: feat(kv_format): declarative KV layout descriptor with EngineKVFormat bijection (RFC #3560, step 1)
body:
**Update 2026-09-02:** rebased onto dev after #4729; the registry now covers all 17 current members (`NL_X_TWO_X_NB_BS_NH_HS` from #3968 added, #4729 added no members) and the tests tie the descriptor to the `KVLayoutName` vocabulary. Details in [this comment](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4592#issuecomment-5511126608). Line and member counts below describe the original 16-member revision.

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Refs #3560.

## Summary

Step 1 of the migration plan posted in #3560: a declarative `KVLayoutDescriptor` that states a physical KV-cache layout as data, plus a bijection with every current `EngineKVFormat` member, pinned by an exhaustive round-trip test. Additive only. No behavior change, no call-site changes, csrc untouched.

One correction to the design comment: the enum is now at 16 members, not 15. #4450 added `NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS` (vLLM-RBLN) after the comment was written, which is the growth pattern the RFC names: a new (engine, backend) pair costing an enum member, a spec class, a `FormatFacts` row, and detector support, for a layout that differs from `NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS` by one singleton dim. In descriptor terms that member is one empty fold.

## Changes

- `lmcache/v1/gpu_connector/kv_format/descriptor.py` (new, 576 lines):
  - `Axis` (`KV`, `L`, `B`, `N`, `H`, `C`), `Grouping` (`SINGLE_TENSOR` / `PER_LAYER` / `KV_LISTS`), `KVPacking` (`SPLIT` / `FUSED` / `SHARED`), `QuantSpec` with `ScalePlacement`.
  - `KVLayoutDescriptor`: frozen dataclass with `extents`, `dims` (ordered partition of axes into physical dims; a multi-axis tuple is a row-major fold, so SGLang's page-buffer dim is `(B, N)` and the unified content dim is `(KV, C)`; the empty tuple is a materialized singleton, which is all the RBLN format needs), `grouping`, `kv_packing`, `storage_dtype` / `logical_dtype`, sparse `dim_strides` overrides generalizing `block_stride_elems`, and `quant`. Structural consistency is validated at construction.
  - Every classification fact is derived from structure with one definition each: `is_hnd` = H's dim precedes N's, `is_mla` = `SHARED` packing, `is_pbs_fused` = some fold contains both B and N, `kv_size` = 2 iff `SPLIT`, etc.
  - `ENGINE_KV_FORMAT_DESCRIPTORS`: one canonical descriptor per member, keyed by member name (native and fallback enum types share names, same reason `specs/registry.py` indexes by value). The DSA indexer entry turns the magic constants into declared facts: `uint8` storage, `float8_e4m3fn` logical dtype, C extent 132, one `float32` scale per 128 values, `BLOCK_REGION` placement.
  - Compat shim: `from_engine_kv_format` / `to_engine_kv_format` / `to_engine_kv_format_name`. Matching is structural (grouping, packing, dims, scale placement), so a concrete descriptor with bound extents and stride overrides projects onto the same member as its canonical template. The module imports neither torch nor the compiled extension at module level; the enum stays the single source of truth for which formats exist.
- `tests/v1/gpu_connector/test_kv_layout_descriptor.py` (new, 208 lines), companion to `test_kv_format_classification.py`:
  - every member has a descriptor (a 17th member fails the test until mapped, mirroring `test_every_format_is_pinned`);
  - round-trip enum -> descriptor -> enum for all 16 members, exhaustive rather than sampled;
  - all 16 canonical descriptors are structurally distinct (bijectivity);
  - the 8 derived facts equal the declared `KVFormatSpec` facts for every member, so the descriptor, the spec classes, and `csrc/engine_kv_format.h` cannot drift;
  - `len(dims)` equals the tensor rank `describe_shape` renders from the enum name grammar;
  - one `dim_strides` entry reproduces the padded-pool per-layer view stride (the case `block_stride_elems` covers today);
  - construction rejects inconsistent structures; unmapped structures raise `ValueError`.

Direction follows maintainer precedent: #4431 moved the per-format facts from inline format lists onto the spec classes as data; #4515 (in flight, no file overlap with this PR) centralizes the transfer-path shape descriptors in `lmcache_native`. This PR continues the same movement one level up: the layout itself as data. Meanwhile the enum keeps growing: this week's #4586 adds a new SGLang DSA detection branch keyed on `uint8` plus last-dim divisibility by 132, the same magic constants the descriptor declares once.

Later steps per the #3560 plan (not in this PR): detection emits descriptors with the enum as a derived view, engine-supplied descriptors through extended `LayoutHints`, kernels consuming descriptor-derived `PageBufferShapeDesc`.

## Validation

On an M-series Mac, Python 3.13.3, torch 2.13.0 CPU, `lmcache_native` compiled from `csrc/lmcache_native` with clang:

- `pytest tests/v1/gpu_connector/`: 161 passed, 18 skipped (GPU-gated), including the 9 new tests and the untouched `test_kv_format_classification.py` golden suite.
- Standalone module load on a bare Python 3.14 with neither torch nor the extension installed: import succeeds, all 16 canonical descriptors build and classify.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy --config-file=pyproject.toml`: clean on both files.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

The descriptor is intentionally unexported from the `kv_format` package facade until step 2 gives it a consumer; tests import the module path directly.

One deliberate deviation from coding standard 7.2 (no lazy imports): `to_engine_kv_format` imports `lmcache.lmcache_native` inside the function. A top-level import would defeat the module's extension-free importability (verified in the tests) and would also need `torch` imported first per the same section, which this module deliberately avoids. The module docstring documents this.

title: [MP][Coordinator] Evict local L2 by routing deletes to the owning instance
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Coordinator-side L2 eviction only worked for a fleet-*shared* L2 pool. `DELETE /cache/objects` is node-scoped — it removes keys from the L2 adapter of whichever server receives it — but `execute_evictions` sent every victim to `registry.random_instance()` with the primary adapter. That is fine for one S3 bucket the whole fleet mounts; for a **local** (private) L2 the bytes live on the storing instance's own disk, so the delete hit the wrong node, removed nothing, produced no `DELETE` event back on the cache-event stream, and the key stayed in the coordinator's LRU and usage totals forever — re-planned every cycle, never converging.

`FleetEvictionController` is now placement-aware. It takes the `KeyDirectory` view (via `from_config`) and resolves each victim's L2 placements into delete routes:

| Placement | DELETE goes to | Requests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shared=True` | The placement's reporter, else any registered server | 1 |
| `shared=False` (local) | The **owning** instance | 1 per owner |
| Local, owner deregistered | Nowhere — key is skipped | 0 |
| No directory placement | Any server, primary adapter (prior behavior) | 1 |

Each request also names the placement's `backend` as the `adapter` selector, so a multi-adapter server deletes from the one that actually holds the key.

Stranded keys are excluded during *planning*, not just dispatch. That matters: a departed owner's key sits at the LRU head, and letting it consume the salt's `eviction_ratio` budget every cycle would stall the deletable keys behind it.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Quota semantics are unchanged: the limit is still per `cache_salt` across the whole fleet, and a key held privately by N instances counts N times — which is what `CacheUsageManager` already accounted for. Per-instance budgets for local L2 would be a separate design.
- Two signature changes, all callers updated here: `FleetEvictionController.__init__` gained a required `key_directory` (production builds it through `from_config` → `views.get(KeyDirectory)`), and `compute_eviction_plan()` became `compute_eviction_plan(registry)` — a victim's eligibility depends on whether anyone can still delete it. `execute_evictions(registry, http_client)` is unchanged. No subclasses.
- `_is_evictable` runs under the LRU policy's lock and takes the directory's; nothing reverses that order (the directory never reaches into eviction). Route resolution is memoized per cycle, so the policy does one directory lookup per candidate it scans, not per tracked key.

title: fix(observability): make the shared observability lock reentrant
body:
## Summary

`lmcache/utils.py` defines one module-global, non-reentrant lock shared by all 30
`@thread_safe` methods in `observability.py`:

```python
_shared_observability_lock = threading.Lock()

def thread_safe(func):
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        with _shared_observability_lock:      # acquire
            result = func(*args, **kwargs)    # inside
```

`MemoryObj.__del__` (`memory_management.py:672`) calls `parent_allocator.free(self)`, and the
paged allocator's `free()` calls two `@thread_safe` methods —
`update_local_cache_usage` and `update_active_memory_objs_count`
(`paged_tensor_memory_allocator.py:257-258`).

Because the garbage collector can run `__del__` at any allocation point, that update can land
on a thread **already holding** the lock, which hangs permanently. It is reachable in normal
operation through `PrometheusLogger.GetOrCreate` (itself `@thread_safe`), which allocates via
`prometheus_client` while binding label views. Stack captured with py-spy on a hung run:

```
GetOrCreate (observability.py:1863)          <- holds the lock (utils.py:700)
  _create_label_view (observability.py:1920)
  _bind_dynamic_metric_children (observability.py:1493)
  labels (prometheus_client/metrics.py:176)
  <genexpr> (prometheus_client/metrics.py:176)
  __del__ (memory_management.py:688)         <- collector runs here
  free (mixed_memory_allocator.py:201)
  free (paged_tensor_memory_allocator.py:257)
  wrapper (utils.py:699)                     <- re-acquires. Deadlock.
```

Both the holding frame and the acquiring frame are in the **same thread's** stack, so this is
same-thread re-entry, not lock ordering across threads.

**Re-entry is safe here.** The two methods reached through `free()` each assign a single
`LMCStatsMonitor` attribute. They touch no `PrometheusLogger` state and do not iterate the
collector dict that `_bind_dynamic_metric_children` is walking, so allowing re-entry breaks no
invariant.

## Reproducers

Minimal — needs no GPU, hangs with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""`:

```python
from lmcache.utils import thread_safe

@thread_safe
def inner(): return 1

@thread_safe
def outer(): return inner()

outer()   # hangs forever on dev
```

The real path, public APIs only:

```python
import torch
from lmcache.utils import thread_safe
from lmcache.v1.memory_allocators.mixed_memory_allocator import MixedMemoryAllocator
from lmcache.v1.memory_management import MemoryFormat

shape = torch.Size([2, 16, 8, 64])
alloc = MixedMemoryAllocator(size=256 * 1024 * 1024, use_paging=True,
                             shapes=[shape], dtypes=[torch.float16],
                             fmt=MemoryFormat.KV_2TD)
holder = {"obj": alloc.allocate(shape, torch.float16, fmt=MemoryFormat.KV_2TD)}

@thread_safe
def locked_region():
    holder["obj"] = None   # __del__ -> free -> update_local_cache_usage

locked_region()   # hangs forever on dev
```

## How it surfaced

The unit suite hangs at `tests/v1/test_remote_mla_worker_id_as0.py:91` (a `LocalCPUBackend`
constructor) with an identical stack each time. It hit **3 of the 5 runs in which that test
executed** — found while running the suite 8 times to validate an unrelated CI change.

Seen on MI300X/gfx942 with torch 2.10.0+rocm7.0 and MI350X/gfx950 with torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 —
two architectures, two toolchains, two hosts. I have not reproduced it on NVIDIA, but nothing
in this path is vendor-specific: it is pure Python, and the minimal reproducer needs no GPU.

It is a permanent hang, not a slow test, and there is no per-test timeout
(`pytest-timeout` is not in `requirements/test.txt`), so a job burns its full
`timeout_in_minutes: 60` and reports a timeout naming no test — which reads as an agent
problem and invites a retry rather than an investigation.

## Test plan

The regression test runs the nested call in a worker thread, so a future regression **fails
the test instead of hanging the suite**:

- with this fix: passes in 2.6s
- with the fix reverted to `threading.Lock()`: fails in 32.6s (the 30s wait)

Also on an MI300X:

- 434 passed across `tests/test_observability.py`, `tests/v1/mp_observability`,
  `tests/v1/mp_coordinator/test_observability.py`, `tests/v1/distributed/test_l1_l2_state_metrics.py`
- full unit suite: 9 failed / 5881 passed / 239 skipped vs 10 failed / 5879 passed / 239 skipped
  without the fix, on the same workspace and toolchain. The failure sets differ by one entry, the
  already-flaky `TestDiscoverApiRouters` member that oscillates run to run. Runtime 15:06 vs 14:58.
- `test_remote_mla_worker_id_as0` **passes** in that run

## Note on scope

This is the stop-gap, not the design fix. Keeping `__del__` out of observability entirely
(deferring the stats update rather than taking a lock under the collector), or splitting the
lock so `PrometheusLogger` registration and `LMCStatsMonitor` counters don't share one global,
would remove the hazard rather than tolerate it. Those are judgement calls for the owners of
this area rather than something to decide here.

Adding `pytest-timeout` with a per-test cap is worth doing separately, so a hang surfaces as a
named test rather than an opaque job timeout.

cc @sammshen @ApostaC — you own `memory_management.py`, the other half of this path, though
this diff doesn't touch it.

title: fix(build): make the hipify guard reachable in the ROCm profile
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

`_hipify_wrapper()` in `setup_extensions/build_profiles/rocm.py` documents:

```
    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If hipify did not yield a path for every requested source.
```

That check can never fire. `hipified_sources` gains exactly one entry per iteration over `source_names`, so `len(hipified_sources) != len(source_names)` is never true. The case the docstring describes is handled a few lines earlier, silently, by falling back to the input path:

```python
        hipified_s_abs = (
            hipify_result[s_abs].hipified_path
            if (s_abs in hipify_result and ...)
            else s_abs          # <- the original, un-hipified source
        )
```

So when hipify does not process a source, the profile hands setuptools the original CUDA file and the ROCm build compiles it under hipcc, with no diagnostic pointing at hipify.

Running the repository's own function with a hipify that returns nothing:

```
docstring says: RuntimeError: If hipify did not yield a path for every requested source.

hipify behaves (control)        -> ['csrc_hip/cuda/ac_dec.hip', 'csrc_hip/cuda/pybind.cpp']
hipify yields an empty result   -> ['csrc_hip/cuda/ac_dec.cu',  'csrc_hip/cuda/pybind.cpp']
hipify silently skips the .cu   -> ['csrc_hip/cuda/ac_dec.cu',  'csrc_hip/cuda/pybind.cpp']
```

The `.cu` comes back un-hipified and nothing is raised.

This PR raises on the sources hipify did not process, naming all of them so one build reports the whole problem, which is what the docstring already promised.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

The fair question is whether tightening this can fail a build that works today. It cannot, and I checked rather than argued it. Running the patched wrapper against the real `csrc/cuda` tree with the real `torch.utils.hipify`, on gfx1101 / ROCm 7.2.2:

```
patched _hipify_wrapper on the real tree -> 12 sources, no raise
    csrc_hip/cuda/pybind_hip.cpp
    csrc_hip/cuda/mem_kernels.hip
    ... (all 12 requested sources resolved)
Successfully preprocessed all matching files.
```

Every requested source is present in hipify's result with a non-None path, including the `.cpp` ones — real hipify renames those too (`pybind.cpp` → `pybind_hip.cpp`), which is worth noting because the stub in the existing tests models hipify as leaving non-`.cu` names untouched. That difference does not affect production code, since it reads `hipified_path` rather than reconstructing the name, so I left the stub alone rather than widen this PR.

Verification:

- the two new tests against `dev`: both fail with `Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class 'RuntimeError'>`, which is the dead guard
- `pytest tests/test_build_profiles_rocm.py` with the fix: **4 passed** (the 2 existing ones still pass, so the honest path is unchanged)
- `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: all hooks pass

The tests stub hipify, as the existing ones do, so they need neither torch nor ROCm.

- [x] this PR contains unit tests

title: [Fix][MP] Release imported events and send transfer replies on stream facts
body:
Refs #4419, #4640, #5116.

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

A `STORE` / `RETRIEVE` / `STORE_Q` / `CB_RETRIEVE_PRE_COMPUTED` handler returns while its device work is still queued, and today it drops two things it cannot yet safely drop:

- the worker's **imported producer event**, which the queued stream wait still references;
- its own **completion event**, exported in the reply for the worker to import later and destroyed at handler return.

Whether either survives depends on how the device runtime treats a destroyed event, not on anything the server observes. Both lifetimes are now released on facts the transfer stream reports.

```
Before
engine                                server
ev_w ───────────────────────────────▶ import ev_w; queue wait(ev_w)
                                      enqueue copy
                                      create ev_s; record ev_s
handle(ev_s) ◀─────────────────────── return            ev_w and ev_s die here
import(ev_s) ... query() each step

After
engine                                server                          transfer stream
ev_w ───────────────────────────────▶ import ev_w; hold it;  queue wait(ev_w)
                                      queue host func: release ev_w   fires after the wait
                                      enqueue copy
                                      queue host func: resolve reply  fires after the copy
                                      return Future
(b"", ok) ◀─────────────────────────── transport sends the resolved reply
future done: transfer complete
```

- **Imported events** are held in `TransferCompletion` (one per server context) until a host callback queued on the same stream directly behind the wait fires.
- **No server-side completion event.** The reply is resolved by a host callback queued behind the copy, so its arrival means the transfer is complete. The wire shape is unchanged: the handle bytes are always empty, which `DeviceMessagingFuture` already treats as "nothing to wait for". Workers need no change and old and new versions interoperate in both directions.
- **Transports**: a blocking handler may return a `Future` for its reply. The message queue chains its send callback onto it; the gRPC servicer waits for it. Handlers annotate `T | Future[T]` and the signature checks strip the `Future` member.

Design doc: `docs/design/v1/multiprocess/transfer_completion.md`.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Exits before the producer wait is queued (unknown instance, block-id underflow, blend no-op reasons) reply immediately; every exit after it defers, including failures, since kernels may be in flight.
- Handlers pass whatever owns their transfer stream (the cache context, or a `TransferStreams` triple for blend's private retrieve stream); the completion object builds the reply tuple, so no handler spells out the wire shape.
- The gRPC servicer blocks its worker thread for the copy duration, as it already did for the affinity-pool future.

**If applicable**:

- [x] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [x] this PR contains unit tests

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes completion semantics on the hot multiprocess KV/Q transfer and CacheBlend retrieve paths; mistakes would show up as subtle GPU memory ordering or stuck futures, though behavior is anchored on stream callbacks and covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a class of lifetime/ordering bugs where multiprocess **STORE**, **RETRIEVE**, **STORE_Q**, and **CB_RETRIEVE_PRE_COMPUTED** handlers could return while GPU work was still queued, dropping imported worker events too early and exporting server completion events the worker might never reliably import.
> 
> Introduces **`TransferCompletion`** on `MPCacheServerContext`: **`wait_for_producer`** keeps imported producer events until a stream host callback proves the wait was consumed; **`reply_when_done`** resolves **`(b"", ok)`** only after everything queued on the transfer stream (including storage **`finish_write`** / **`finish_read_prefetched`**) has run. Handlers may return **`Future[TransferReply]`**; the message queue and gRPC path wait on that future before sending the wire reply.
> 
> **Server-side completion event export is removed** (blend no-op / early-error paths reply immediately with empty handles). Workers stay compatible: **`DeviceMessagingFuture`** already treats an empty handle as “reply arrival = done,” and non-empty handles still work against older servers. Docs and tests cover the new contract and deferred-reply transport.
>

title: fix(vllm): safely wire MP cache reset
body:
## Summary
- Add scheduler-role `LMCacheMPConnector.reset_cache()` for the MP vLLM connector.
- Send `clear(force=False)` through the transport-neutral `RequestClient` to every backing LMCache server.
- Keep reset best-effort and bounded by one MQ timeout across all servers.
- Preserve active request trackers, scheduler lookup bookkeeping, and server health state when CLEAR fails or times out.
- Exercise reset through real vLLM and LMCache servers in the CPU E2E validation for both ZMQ and gRPC.

## Context
This PR continues the work from inactive PR #3643 against the current `dev` branch. PR #5158 has since added the optional CLEAR `force` argument across ZMQ and gRPC, so this PR relies on that shared protocol and is limited to the vLLM integration. Locked objects from in-flight work are preserved, and a failure from one server does not suppress CLEAR attempts to the others.

## Testing
The CPU E2E validation now verifies the full store, hit, external reset, miss/repopulation, hit, and cross-vLLM-instance hit sequence with both ZMQ and gRPC. See the [E2E validation comment](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/5091#issuecomment-5727732562) for the summarized results and expandable details.

title: [Bugfix] Allow MLA workers to recover remote backend health
body:
**Bug:** A nonzero MLA worker's remote-health probe takes the normal no-op write path, then reads an object that was never stored and remains unhealthy.

**Root cause:** Health probes use ordinary cache-write admission, although every worker needs its own actual write/read round trip.

**Fix:** Add an opt-in used by health probes to bypass the filter; scope their keys to instance/rank/backend/schema and zero-initialize the payload.

**Regression:** Local target checks changed from 2 failed / 3 passed to 5 passed; the follow-up allocation-failure case brings the corrected target set to 6 passing cases.

## Review scope

Production change is **+41/-9 across 2 files**; tests are **+336/-0 across 1 file**. Focus on [the keyword-only health-probe bypass](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/6c34d4b669aab4c3e41eed914c89a67438a6119c/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/remote_backend.py#L222-L250) and [probe identity/allocation handling](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/6c34d4b669aab4c3e41eed914c89a67438a6119c/lmcache/v1/health_monitor/checks/remote_backend_check.py#L271-L336): ordinary nonzero MLA writes must still be skipped, while logical ranks do not share a probe object.

## Validation

CI: [Buildkite unit tests](https://buildkite.com/lmcache/k3-unit-tests/builds/9835) passed on this head.

<details>
<summary>Evidence and environment</summary>

- On pinned dev `e8cb1324b4852da625c98c1ff1ac5ecb4c5a9de9`, the original 5 CPU regressions passed; the frozen baseline and a production-only withdrawal each had 2 failures and 3 passing controls.
- On the pinned-dev integration checkout, the follow-up public-path allocation-failure case confirms that the backend remains unhealthy, submits no put, and returns allocator use to zero. All 6 health regressions passed with real `RemoteBackend`, filesystem connector, CPU allocator, and naive serde.
- Controls cover worker zero, non-MLA, and disabled remapping, and assert ordinary nonzero MLA puts remain skipped. `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy pre-commit run --all-files` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Two logical ranks recover concurrently against one filesystem root and leave distinct probe objects. Reconstructing the health check reuses its persisted probe key.

</details>

## Limitations

No physical multi-rank inference, GPU, health-monitor scheduler, engine restart, live network service, CacheGen, or stress run was performed. Duplicate processes with the same logical probe identity have no distributed lock, and probe objects persist. Existing timeout and serialization-error handling are unchanged.

title: [Bugfix] Preserve MLA cache identity in remote reads
body:
**Bug:** In MLA worker-as-zero mode, a nonzero worker can find a cached prefix then miss it on an asynchronous read; rewriting a layer key can also discard its layer identity.

**Root cause:** The async connector path omitted worker normalization, while key rewriting rebuilt a base key instead of preserving subclass fields.

**Fix:** Normalize keys before asynchronous connector reads and use `dataclasses.replace` to change only the worker ID.

**Regression:** Local target checks changed from 5 failed / 3 passed to 8 passed; withdrawing the production repair restored 5 failures.

title: [Bugfix] Deserialize asynchronous remote cache reads
body:
**Bug:** Asynchronous remote reads return compressed wire objects instead of decoded KV; for CacheGen, the Future can also resolve before GPU decode work is complete.

**Root cause:** The non-blocking path forwarded connector results and did not establish the decoder's construction-device stream or a completion barrier.

**Fix:** Deserialize the available prefix after the remote read; for CacheGen, retain its construction stream and synchronize it once before the coroutine resolves.

**Regression:** Local decode checks changed from 2 failed / 6 passed to 8 passed. The completion test fails on the earlier head `b30336fe`; the corrected local suite passes all 9 cases.

## Review scope

Production change is **+40/-2 across 1 file**; tests are **+455/-0 across 1 file**. Focus on [CacheGen stream capture](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/3cf20a6c9ccaaf3bef3a2a2e382cbf961749b69b/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/remote_backend.py#L72-L82) and [the decode/completion boundary](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/3cf20a6c9ccaaf3bef3a2a2e382cbf961749b69b/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/remote_backend.py#L559-L618): CacheGen returns decoded objects only after its batch completes, including the exception path; existing remote timeout handling remains unchanged.

## Validation

**CI:** [Buildkite #9834](https://buildkite.com/lmcache/k3-unit-tests/builds/9834) fails in the new GPU completion test: `producer_queued.wait(30)` times out. The cause is unresolved; this PR remains Draft.

<details>
<summary>Evidence and environment</summary>

- On pinned dev `e8cb1324b4852da625c98c1ff1ac5ecb4c5a9de9`, target decode checks moved from 2 failed / 6 passed to 8 passed; a production-only withdrawal restored 2 failures.
- Real public `RemoteBackend` store/read methods, a loopback LMServer transport, and the CacheGen CUDA codec cover all-hit, hit-prefix, first-miss, and empty requests for CacheGen and naive serde.
- A follow-up NVIDIA B300 host-callback oracle holds the decoder's final write. Earlier head `b30336fe` fails with `DID NOT RAISE TimeoutError`; the corrected version passed 9 GPU cases, and withdrawing only the production correction reproduced that failure. Non-Rust pre-commit hooks passed.

Its queueing timeout has not been isolated to production code or the test synchronization mechanism; the local passes remain separate evidence.

</details>

## Limitations

Synchronizing the CacheGen stream blocks the storage event-loop thread until that batch's decode finishes; no throughput improvement is claimed. Only one visible GPU was available, so a nonzero device index was not tested. No full model, inference-quality, physical multi-rank, concurrent blocking/non-blocking CacheGen, cross-device serialized-object, or end-to-end paged-KV run was performed.

title: [Bugfix] Preserve cache identity in S3 and Azure object names
body:
**Bug:** S3 and Azure can return one model's KV bytes to another when distinct legal names collapse after `/` is replaced with `_`.

**Root cause:** The object-name encoding is lossy before either provider reads or writes the cache object.

**Fix:** Hash the complete UTF-8 cache-key string into a bounded `lmcache-v2/<sha256>` name for both providers.

**Regression:** Local target checks changed from 12 failed / 2 passed to 14 passed; withdrawing the production repair restored 12 failures.

## Review scope

Production change is **+15/-13 across 2 files**; tests are **+368/-0 across 1 file**; documentation is **+27/-3 across 2 files**. Focus on the identical complete-key mapping in [Azure](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/6a028c0b7624e89df39f6a89afb7d545dbb80c0a/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/azure_connector.py#L137-L140) and [S3](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/6a028c0b7624e89df39f6a89afb7d545dbb80c0a/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/s3_connector.py#L169-L176); absent v2 objects must not fall back to an ambiguous legacy name.

Compatibility: this intentionally starts a cold remote cache. Legacy objects are neither read, migrated, nor deleted; old and new clients may share storage but not these chunks. Prefix-scoped policies must allow `lmcache-v2/`.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Evidence and environment</summary>

- On pinned dev `e8cb1324b4852da625c98c1ff1ac5ecb4c5a9de9`, 14 CPU regressions passed; the frozen baseline and a production-only withdrawal each had 12 failures and 2 passing controls.

The S3 page passed a strict standalone build.
- `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy pre-commit run --all-files` and `git diff --check` passed.

</details>

## Limitations

No cloud endpoint, MinIO, Azurite, IAM policy, or live credential flow was tested. SHA-256 provides collision resistance rather than mathematical injectivity. Existing connector shutdown behavior is outside this patch.

title: [Bugfix] Roll back remote put state when serialization fails
body:
**Bug:** A synchronous serialization exception leaves a put key reserved and its temporary input reference held, so a later healthy write of that key is suppressed.

**Root cause:** Serialization ran after reserving the key and taking an input reference, with no cleanup if it raised.

**Fix:** Reserve the key atomically under the existing lock, discard it if serialization raises, and release the temporary input reference in `finally`.

**Regression:** Local target checks changed from 4 failed / 1 passed to 5 passed; withdrawing the production repair restored 4 failures.

## Review scope

Production change is **+12/-7 across 1 file**; tests are **+410/-0 across 1 file**. Focus on [`submit_put_task`](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/8f7242a08ce74309055a36e4897791e4f87101e9/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/remote_backend.py#L222-L262): reservation must be atomic, a serialization failure must release both the marker and temporary reference, and the original exception must propagate.

## Validation

- On pinned dev `e8cb1324b4852da625c98c1ff1ac5ecb4c5a9de9`, 5 CPU regressions passed; the frozen baseline and a production-only withdrawal each had 4 failures and 1 passing control.
- The public-path test uses a real `RemoteBackend`, naive serializer, instrumented filesystem connector, CPU allocator, and a matching full chunk. A controlled `MemoryError` is injected only at the serializer boundary; this is not a CacheGen or GPU-OOM claim.
- Cases check reference and pending-key cleanup, a same-key retry, normal byte/shape round trips, and deterministic same-key admission with event gates. `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy pre-commit run --all-files` and `git diff --check` passed.

title: [Bugfix] Wait for in-flight chunk recorder work to finish
body:
**Bug:** `AsyncRecorder.wait_for_completion()` can return `True` after a worker dequeues an item but before preprocessing or recording finishes.

**Root cause:** Two `queue.empty()` observations cannot see work already owned by the worker.

**Fix:** Wait on the queue's unfinished-task condition with a monotonic deadline, and acknowledge every dequeued item once in worker, drain, and clear paths.

**Regression:** Local target checks changed from 3 failed / 4 passed to 7 passed; withdrawing the production repair restored 3 failures.

## Review scope

Production change is **+24/-15 across 1 file**; tests are **+140/-0 across 1 file**. Focus on [acknowledgment placement in both worker paths](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/7c2921d0e7db08ebc0fa91089df78bf2fe117553/lmcache/v1/lookup_client/record_strategies/base.py#L197-L235) and [the completion predicate](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/7c2921d0e7db08ebc0fa91089df78bf2fe117553/lmcache/v1/lookup_client/record_strategies/base.py#L286-L303): completion must wait for in-flight work, while handled failures still terminate that work.

The typed callback helpers were included in a 7-target-test pass on the pinned-dev integration checkout. `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy pre-commit run --all-files` and `git diff --check` passed.

title: [Bugfix] Apply the configured hit limit to cached lookup results
body:
**Bug:** A `HitLimitLookupClient` can apply the configured miss ratio to an immediate result but return an unlimited cached result for the same lookup.

**Root cause:** `lookup_cache()` lacked the request token count needed to apply the same chunk-aligned policy to cached results.

**Fix:** Record each lookup's token count, route immediate and cached results through one limiter, and remove that state when the lookup is cleared or the client closes.

**Regression:** Local target checks changed from 5 failed / 4 passed to 9 passed; withdrawing the production repair restored 5 failures.

Also review [state cleanup](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/1259852c8344375b809319d4112881766e3dbe9b/lmcache/v1/lookup_client/hit_limit_lookup_client.py#L96-L107).

title: [Bugfix] Await asynchronous Redis Sentinel client commands
body:
**Bug:** RedisSentinelConnector reports missing keys as present, returns from writes without sending them, and fails reads on coroutine values.

**Root cause:** It creates redis.asyncio Sentinel child clients but invokes their commands and close methods as synchronous functions.

**Fix:** Await the child-client operations and bridge exists_sync through the configured loop; preserve payload-before-metadata writes and wrapper reference ownership.

**Regression:** Baseline: 5 failures / 1 pass; fix: 6 passes. A real master/replica/Sentinel experiment also changes from 4 failures to 4 passes.

## Review scope

Production change is **+75/-12 across 1 file**; tests are **+367/-2 across 2 files**. Most added lines are regression tests.

- Review [exists_sync](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/f8fa0864a4bd8af5903bc2e6e85cc113f46049c5/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/redis_connector.py#L534) and [get](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/f8fa0864a4bd8af5903bc2e6e85cc113f46049c5/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/redis_connector.py#L549): the synchronous bridge uses the configured loop, and all child reads/deletes are awaited.
- Review [put](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/f8fa0864a4bd8af5903bc2e6e85cc113f46049c5/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/redis_connector.py#L613) and [close](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/f8fa0864a4bd8af5903bc2e6e85cc113f46049c5/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/redis_connector.py#L648): await payload before metadata and both closes; the wrapper remains the sole owner of its reference decrement. Fixture changes make child clients asynchronous.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Evidence and environment</summary>

Baseline: `e8cb1324b4852da625c98c1ff1ac5ecb4c5a9de9`; Python 3.12.11, redis-py 8.1.0, CPU.

- Identical regression tests/fixtures: 5 failed / 1 passed → 6 passed → production fix withdrawn 5 failed / 1 passed.
- Separate real loopback Redis 7.0.15 master/replica/Sentinel experiment, 16-byte payloads: 4 failed → 4 passed → 4 failed. Native Sentinel and ordinary Redis roundtrip controls passed in each phase; all services exited normally.
- Final collection fix keeps connector imports under TYPE_CHECKING. A binding probe reproduces the old collection interference (6 passes / 1 failure); correction passes 21 checks including metadata, reversed collection passes 7, and withdrawing the import correction restores the same failure.
- New/existing Sentinel/Cluster checks: 15 passed / 15 deselected on one B300 with mocked transport. Jointly with the Redis prefix PR, 23 selected cases passed; this is a combined result.
- Non-Rust pre-commit and diff checks passed; Rust hooks were explicitly skipped.

Regression module: `tests/v1/storage_backend/test_redis_sentinel_async.py`; shared fixture: `tests/conftest.py`.

The earlier Cluster DNS comparison still collected the new test module; it was not evidence of an independently failing upstream Cluster suite. The collection interference is fixed; the earlier exit timeout remains unattributed. An initial 8 GiB adjacent job hit its memory limit; later successful checks used larger allocations.

Related: closed #2095 addressed missing awaits. This keeps the write ordering from #2186 and wrapper ownership from #2202.

</details>

## Limitations

Call exists_sync from outside the configured loop’s thread. Writes remain two sequential, non-atomic records. Sentinel parent lifecycle, failover, authentication/TLS, removal/listing and allocation-cleanup redesign are outside scope; existing stale-read GC warnings remain. The ordinary Redis control used public async shutdown rather than validating its existing close path. No model validation was run.

title: [Bugfix] Keep priority executor workers alive after caller cancellation
body:
**Bug:** Cancelling a submit_job caller can kill its priority-executor worker; later requests then remain queued without a worker.

**Root cause:** After the job returns or raises, the worker calls set_result/set_exception on the caller’s already-cancelled Future and exits with InvalidStateError.

**Fix:** Deliver results or exceptions only while the Future is pending, in both async and threadpool workers.

**Regression:** Before/withdrawn fix: 4 target failures and 4 passing controls. With the fix: all 8 cases pass.

## Review scope

Production change is **+21/-7 across 1 file**; tests are **+118/-0 across 1 file**. Most added lines are regression tests.

- Review the completion guards in [AsyncPQExecutor._worker](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/861ec201bb974e435ec3d28b7c420fceeeffef97/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/job_executor/pq_executor.py#L55) and [AsyncPQThreadPoolExecutor._worker](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/861ec201bb974e435ec3d28b7c420fceeeffef97/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/job_executor/pq_executor.py#L166). Both successful and exceptional completion must leave the worker alive after caller cancellation.
- Queue acknowledgement remains in finally; pending callers retain normal result/exception delivery. Other added lines document and type these worker paths.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Evidence and environment</summary>

Baseline: `1b7dff2cd83fc634326b5989eb71aa5f05b4f426`; CPU only.

- Eight parameterized cases cover both executor types and successful/exceptional job completion.
- Events establish that cancellation happens after the job starts; timeouts only bound waits. The following job verifies that the same single worker remains usable.
- Candidate: 8 passes. With the production fix removed and tests retained: 4 failures / 4 controls pass.
- Non-Rust pre-commit checks passed; Rust hooks were explicitly skipped.

Regression module: `tests/v1/storage_backend/test_pq_executor_cancellation.py`.

#4490 addresses shutdown ordering, which is outside this fix.

</details>

## Limitations

Queued/running jobs still execute after caller cancellation. This does not handle a job that itself raises CancelledError or guarantee prompt cleanup of abandoned results. No model-serving, GPU or performance validation was run.

- [x] This PR contains unit tests.

title: [Bugfix] Preserve the consecutive hit prefix in redis-py connectors
body:
**Bug:** If a middle key disappears during a nonblocking Redis batch read, a later key’s payload can be returned in the missing key’s position.

**Root cause:** RedisConnector and RedisClusterConnector remove missing entries instead of returning the consecutive hit prefix required by RemoteConnector.

**Fix:** Stop the returned prefix at the first miss/error and release successful objects fetched after that boundary.

**Regression:** Removing the production fix yields 6 failures and 2 passing controls; the fix passes all 8 regressions.

## Review scope

Production change is **+41/-4 across 1 file**; tests are **+337/-0 across 1 file**. Most added lines are regression tests.

- Check prefix ordering and exactly-once tail release in [_consecutive_prefix](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/f023cec2f8aec5c338de526d5c7dba7e6a3d7563/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/redis_connector.py#L31).
- Check that both [RedisConnector](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/f023cec2f8aec5c338de526d5c7dba7e6a3d7563/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/redis_connector.py#L461) and [RedisClusterConnector](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/f023cec2f8aec5c338de526d5c7dba7e6a3d7563/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/redis_connector.py#L843) collect ordered results with exceptions preserved, then use the same prefix helper.

## Validation

Original baseline: `1b7dff2cd83fc634326b5989eb71aa5f05b4f426`.

- Real connector, metadata decoding and CPU allocator paths; only redis-py construction/GET boundaries are replaced. Payloads are 8 bytes.

In the `92a40871` integration tree, the 8 prefix cases passed, and the prefix/Sentinel/existing Cluster combination passed 23 cases (15 unrelated cases deselected).

Scope is the redis-py connectors. #2173 concerned EIC; #5124 addresses RESPConnector/native completion.

</details>

title: [Bugfix] Recover LMC server connections after disconnects
body:
**Bug:** After an LMC server disconnect, later requests keep using the failed connection even when the server is available again. Fixes #3565.

**Root cause:** The connector neither replaces a broken socket nor safely discards a partially completed RPC before reuse.

**Fix:** Reconnect and replay with a bounded retry budget while holding the whole-RPC lock; clean up interrupted reads and reject incomplete server PUT bodies.

**Regression:** 10 real loopback TCP regressions pass. Withdrawing both client/server fixes reproduces 7 target failures.

## Review scope

Production change is **+162/-32 across 2 files**; tests are **+876/-0 across 1 file**. Most added lines are regression tests. Documentation adds +72/-0 across 2 files.

- Check retry/lock and cleanup invariants in [LMCServerConnector._run_with_reconnect](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/19b04bd4da08f409385b99203f44f139a79a13aa/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/lm_connector.py#L244) and [receive_all](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/19b04bd4da08f409385b99203f44f139a79a13aa/lmcache/v1/storage_backend/connector/lm_connector.py#L94). Each RPC has at most three attempts; failed receive allocations and sockets are released.
- Check the incomplete-body guard in [server handle_client](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/19b04bd4da08f409385b99203f44f139a79a13aa/lmcache/v1/server/__main__.py#L43): a disconnected PUT must not overwrite a successful retry.

## Validation

<details>
<summary>Evidence and environment</summary>

Baseline: `1b7dff2cd83fc634326b5989eb71aa5f05b4f426`; real loopback TCP, 16-byte CPU payloads.

- Candidate: 10 regression passes. With both production fixes removed: 7 target failures, 1 pass, 2 deselected.
- Adjacent metadata/interface checks: 15 passed, 3 unrelated cases deselected.
- Non-Rust pre-commit checks passed; Rust hooks were explicitly skipped.
- Strict Sphinx baseline and candidate produced the same 30 warnings and 1 error after path normalization, all outside the changed docs. The full documentation build is not clean.

Regression module: `tests/v1/storage_backend/test_lm_connector_reconnect.py`.

The earlier closed #3569 proposed bounded reconnect/replay; this repair also covers stream/allocation cleanup and incomplete server PUTs.

</details>

## Limitations

PUT still has no acknowledgement, durability or exactly-once guarantee. Initial connect and ordinary reads/writes retain their existing blocking behavior. No Kubernetes, model-serving, GPU or performance validation was run.

title: [MP][Ascend][KV format] Add NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS for vLLM-Ascend MLA/DSA plane tuples
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Refs #4061 

vLLM-Ascend emits per-layer plane tuples for MLA and DSA caches: DeepSeek-V2/V3 MLA registers each layer as `(latent, rope)` and V3.2 DSA as `(latent, rope, dsa)`. Every plane is a paged `[NB, BS, 1, width]` tensor with a single latent KV head and mutually unequal widths; previously these were misclassified or rejected by the vLLM detector, so LMCache could not attach to vLLM-Ascend MLA/DSA models.

This adds `EngineKVFormat.NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS` to detect and transfer them:

- New format value + format facts, pybind export, .pyi stub
- vLLM detector branch: single-head tuples of unequal widths (or arity 1/3) classify as plane tuples; equal-width pairs stay `(K, V)`
- New spec `NL_X_NP_X_NB_BS_ONE_HS_Spec`; NP stays symbolic like ONE/TWO
- Per-layer format discovery grouped by full shape/dtype structure (`get_shape_and_dtype`) so plane-tuple layers share one detection pass
- Block-stride resolution accepts the format
- Python-fallback D2H/H2D transfer carves planes by byte offset, including mixed-item-size (int8 latent + fp16 scale) packing

The transferred object stays one flat plane of the summed width (`kv_size == 1`, `is_mla`); only the paged source arrives as per-plane tuples.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

NPU path verified on 910B (roundtrip + detection tests).
