title: [Fix][Disk] Guard batched_async_load_bytes_from_disk against concurrent-eviction TOCTOU
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

#2420's traceback is a `KeyError` at `self.dict[key].cached_positions` after `read_file()`
silently drops `key` from `self.dict` on a `FileNotFoundError`. The reporter noted the same
pattern exists in `async_load_bytes` (now `batched_async_load_bytes_from_disk`). Open PR #4405
guards the sibling `load_bytes_from_disk`, but doesn't touch this function, so the async
prefetch path still raises the bare `KeyError` if a concurrent `remove(key, force=True)` races
its unlocked disk read.

Fix mirrors #4405 and the already-guarded `_load_chunk_into_memory`: recover the metadata under
`disk_lock` and drop the key as a miss (`ref_count_down()`, skip) instead of indexing straight
into `self.dict`.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

The race needs a second in-flight request removing the same key while this one is still
mid-read (e.g. `remove_after_retrieve` on a PD receiver, or an explicit cache clear), which I
didn't reproduce end to end through the full prefetch pipeline. The regression test reproduces
it directly at the function level with a threading barrier in `read_file`, on unfixed `dev` it
raises the exact `KeyError` from #2420; on this branch it returns cleanly.

**If applicable**:

- [x] this PR contains unit tests

Fixes #2420

title: [Perf][RawBlock] Batch io_uring put_many writes in bounded chunks
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

  With `io_engine="io_uring"`, `put_many` of N>1 keys previously issued one
  io_uring submit/wait per key, so the device wrote them one at a time.
  This routes that case to `_put_many_batch_io`, which groups eligible keys into
  bounded io_uring chunks and submits each chunk through one `_write_buffers` call
  (header+payload entries), so writes in that chunk can be in flight concurrently.

  Large calls are capped at 64 keys per chunk. The cap limits keys, not entries:
  on the regular io_uring path each key contributes two write entries (header +
  payload), so a chunk submits at most 128, while on the `io_uring_cmd` path those
  entries are split further by `max_data_transfer_size` and a chunk can submit
  more. The cap bounds RawBlockCore lock hold time and the memory a single batch
  holds.

  Commit and rollback are per chunk: if the device write for a chunk fails, every
  new key submitted in that chunk is rolled back and none are committed to the
  index. This is a chunk-level index commit boundary, not device-write atomicity
  -- bytes may already have reached the device. Pre-submit failures stay per key:
  already-indexed keys report success without rewriting, and oversized payloads or
  slot exhaustion fail only that key. The POSIX path is unchanged.

  For non-`uring_cmd` io_uring writes, padded O_DIRECT writes intentionally fall
  back to per-entry `write_uring`, because the current Rust `batched_write` API
  does not carry separate `payload_len` and `total_len` values. True batched
  padded O_DIRECT support is left for a follow-up Rust API change.

  **Special notes for your reviewers**:

  Contract is covered by fake-io_uring-device unit tests: single-submit-per-chunk
  behavior on batchable writes, bounded chunking, round-trip, already-indexed
  skip, same-batch duplicates, oversize isolation, chunk-level write-failure
  rollback, partial-submission rollback, failed-completion rollback, partial
  slot-exhaustion, `io_uring_cmd` multi-key batching with per-key placement IDs,
  and POSIX stays sequential.

  Real-NVMe speedup is not covered in CI because it requires a suitable
  kernel and a scratch raw-block device; validation was performed locally.
  On a local Samsung PM1753 32TB NVMe SSD, at the time of that measurement,
  _put_many_batch_io reduced put_many wall-clock latency by 49–66% at p50 and
  56–77% at p95 across the evaluated workloads.

  **If applicable**:

  - [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
  - [x] this PR contains unit tests

title: [Feature][MP] Negotiate chunk size from KV geometry
body:
## Summary

- add a `NEGOTIATE_CHUNK_SIZE` controller RPC so the vLLM MP connector can send the model-derived KV alignment before normal lookup/store/retrieve traffic starts
- keep the MP server's `--chunk-size` as the user-configured minimum chunk size; the server rounds it upward to the first value compatible with the vLLM geometry when needed
- update chunk-size-bound runtime state (`TokenHasher`, `SessionManager`, blend matcher, and MP continuous usage conversion) after negotiation, while preserving the existing fixed-size behavior when the configured size is already compatible

## Why

The MP server currently starts with a fixed `chunk_size` (default: `256`) before vLLM has loaded the model and resolved its KV-cache layout. That works for common layouts, but fails for newer hybrid / MLA / Mamba layouts where the LMCache chunk boundary must align with model-specific cache group spans.

Concrete examples:

- `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` can resolve to `group_tokens_per_block = [640, 0, 640, 640, 640, 640]`, so every cacheable chunk must be a multiple of `640`. A default server `--chunk-size 256` is too small and incompatible; this PR negotiates it upward to `640`.
- `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` can require a `400`-token boundary. Common guesses such as `256`, `512`, or `1024` are not reliable because only multiples of `400` are valid.
- Mixed layouts such as `[544, 64]` need the common multiple `1088`; a server launched with `--chunk-size 1024` should become `1088`, not fail simply because the operator could not know the model geometry before vLLM startup.

This avoids asking operators to know model-specific KV geometry at LMCache server launch time.

Fixes #5217

## Chunk-size semantics

This PR separates two concepts:

- `required_chunk_alignment`: a hard correctness constraint computed by vLLM from the resolved KV groups. The final LMCache chunk size must be a multiple of this value.
- `--chunk-size`: the LMCache server-side minimum chunk size. vLLM does not get to shrink it.

The server resolves:

```text
final_chunk_size = round_up(server_configured_chunk_size, required_chunk_alignment)
```

Examples:

```text
server --chunk-size 256,  vLLM alignment 32   -> final 256
server --chunk-size 256,  vLLM alignment 640  -> final 640
server --chunk-size 512,  vLLM alignment 400  -> final 800
server --chunk-size 1024, vLLM alignment 544  -> final 1088
```

So the vLLM side only supplies geometry; the server remains responsible for the minimum chunk-size policy.

## Why a new negotiation RPC instead of changing REGISTER_KV_CACHE?

The issue discussed either adding fields to `REGISTER_KV_CACHE` or using a separate pre-registration negotiation RPC. I chose the latter for the draft because of the current vLLM MP connector timing:

- the scheduler adapter needs the final `lmcache_tokens_per_chunk` during connector initialization, before it can safely round APC hits, compute `blocks_in_chunk`, and issue lookup/prefetch requests;
- worker-side `REGISTER_KV_CACHE` happens later, only after vLLM hands actual KV cache tensors to the worker role;
- there are multiple registration surfaces (`REGISTER_KV_CACHE`, `REGISTER_Q_CACHE`, and `REGISTER_KV_CACHE_ENGINE_DRIVEN_CONTEXT`), so putting chunk-size negotiation into only one register path would leave other paths inconsistent;
- the protocol docs already treat payload-shape changes as requiring a new request name, so adding optional fields to the existing enum would be a wire-compatibility risk.

A register-based design is still possible, but it would need a larger change: either add versioned registration request names and make scheduler chunk-size discovery wait for registration, or split the server's configured minimum from the final negotiated value and ensure all register paths finalize the same value. This draft keeps the negotiation explicit and early.

## Testing

- `uv run pytest -q tests/v1/multiprocess/test_chunk_size_negotiation.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_config.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_client.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_protocols.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_grpc_transport.py tests/v1/test_vllm_mp_adapter.py tests/test_usage_telemetry.py`
- `uv run ruff check lmcache/integration/vllm/lmcache_mp_connector.py lmcache/integration/vllm/vllm_multi_process_adapter.py lmcache/usage_telemetry/mp_continuous.py lmcache/v1/multiprocess/config.py lmcache/v1/multiprocess/engine_context.py lmcache/v1/multiprocess/modules/blend/module.py lmcache/v1/multiprocess/modules/management.py lmcache/v1/multiprocess/protocols/controller.py lmcache/v1/multiprocess/server.py lmcache/v1/multiprocess/transport/base.py lmcache/v1/multiprocess/transport/zmq_impl/client.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_chunk_size_negotiation.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_client.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_config.py tests/v1/multiprocess/test_grpc_transport.py tests/v1/test_vllm_mp_adapter.py tests/test_usage_telemetry.py`

title: [Feature][MP] Enable Hybrid Multi-Group KV Transfer (Engine-Driven Path) for Qwen3.5/Gemma-Style models on Intel GPU
body:
# Enable Hybrid Multi-Group KV Transfer (Engine-Driven Path) for Qwen3.5/Gemma-Style models on Intel GPU ## 1. Motivation & What Changed The engine-driven (XPU) transfer path originally assumed a single, uniform KV cache group for the whole model: one shared block size, one shared hidden dimension, one shared KV format. Hybrid models such as Qwen3.5 and Gemma, which mix multiple KV cache groups, could not run on XPU under this assumption. This change adds engine-driven multi-group support for Qwen3.5/Gemma-style hybrid models on XPU only (the CUDA IPC / lmcache-driven path is untouched): - The worker can register **N independently-shaped LMCache groups** (own layer count, block size, hidden dim, KV format per group) instead of requiring every group to share one layout. - Store/retrieve gather, transfer, and scatter each group using its own layout, concatenating wire data **group-major** . - Null-chunk skipping: chunks vLLM has already nulled out (recurrent state before it's live, or sliding-window/GDN chunks outside the current window) are no longer stored or read back as garbage -- a new per-group, per-chunk mask excludes them from the transfer. Non-hybrid (single-group) registrations keep working unchanged -- every new code path collapses to the old single-group behavior when no groups are registered. ## 2. Architecture Changes ### 2.1 Worker Side: One Layout -> Per-Group Plans Before: ```text EngineDrivenTransferContext register() -> one EngineDrivenContextMetadata (shared layout_desc, block_size) submit_store() -> prepare_store -> gather_paged_kv_to_cpu(all layers, one block size) -> commit_store submit_retrieve() -> prepare_retrieve -> scatter_cpu_to_paged_kv(all layers, one block size) -> commit_retrieve AsyncEngineDrivenTransferContext.submit_store() (pre-existing, #3808) -> prepare_store -> gather_paged_kv_to_cpu(all layers, one block size) runs in the background commit_executor -> staging buffers keyed by ONE (shape, dtype), since every chunk in a single-group store shares one shape -> commit_store ``` After: ```text EngineDrivenTransferContext register() -> _build_group_transfer_plans(engine_group_infos) -> self._group_plans: list[GroupTransferPlan] (per group: layer_indices, blocks_per_chunk, chunk_shape, engine_kv_format -- cached once, not recomputed per transfer) -> single-group fallback: one plan with group_info=None when engine_group_infos is empty iter_transfer_groups() <-- shared fan-out point -> yields (plan, group_kv_caches, group_block_ids) per group (or the single-group fallback plan when no groups were registered) submit_store() -> iter_transfer_groups() -> _has_maskable_group() -> null_chunk_mask_from_groups() (attach null_chunk_mask to the key when any group is recurrent or sliding-window) -> prepare_store (server reserves slots / returns chunk_indices) -> for plan, group_kv_caches, group_block_ids in transfer_groups: slice flat out_buffers/chunk_indices onto this group via _select_group_chunks(); skip if this group has nothing selected gather_paged_kv_to_cpu() using THAT group's plan (blocks_per_chunk, chunk_shape, cached engine_kv_format) -> concatenate gathered chunks group-major -> commit_store submit_retrieve() -> iter_transfer_groups() -> _has_maskable_group() -> null_chunk_mask_from_groups() -> prepare_retrieve (server returns flat, group-major src_buffers, already shortened by any null-masked chunks) -> for plan, group_kv_caches, group_block_ids in transfer_groups: drop this group's null-masked block IDs via _select_live_scatter_chunks() to line up with the server's already-shortened chunk list scatter_cpu_to_paged_kv() using THAT group's plan -> commit_retrieve AsyncEngineDrivenTransferContext.submit_store() (pre-existing class, retrofitted) -> same iter_transfer_groups() fan-out, but the per-group gather loop runs in the background commit_executor; staging buffers are bucketed by (shape, dtype) since groups can have different shapes ``` ### 2.2 Server Side: One Context -> Per-Group Contexts Before: ```text EngineDrivenTransferModule register_kv_cache_engine_driven_context() -> one EngineDrivenContextEntry.metadata (shared layout_desc) prepare_store() / commit_store() / prepare_retrieve() / commit_retrieve() -> operate on entry.metadata directly (single layout, single set of object keys, single TransferStrategy call) ``` After: ```text EngineDrivenTransferModule register_kv_cache_engine_driven_context() -> if engine_group_infos present: entry.metadata_by_group: list[EngineDrivenContextMetadata] (one per group, own layout_desc + block_size) + AttnWindowDesc registered via _make_attn_window_desc() (per-group sliding-window size, "attention"/"recurrent"/ "standalone" kind) else: entry.metadata_by_group stays empty -> single-group fallback prepare_store() / prepare_retrieve() -> contexts = entry.metadata_by_group or [entry.metadata] <-- decision point -> for group_id, context in enumerate(contexts): <-- fan-out point resolve this group's object keys (_resolve_per_group_obj_keys) apply null_chunk_mask exclusion (_apply_null_chunk_mask) delegate to TransferStrategy for this group accumulate with a running chunk_offset -> concatenate slots/chunk_indices (store) or slots/chunks (retrieve) group-major commit_store() <-- pickle/SHM split on cpu_data -> if cpu_data == b"" (SHM mode): flatten all groups' object keys (_flatten_obj_keys) one strategy.commit_store_chunks() call, chunks=[] (worker already wrote into reserved slots; this only releases the shared write locks for every group at once) else (pickle mode): pickle.loads(cpu_data) once -> flat, group-major chunk list for group_id, context in enumerate(contexts): <-- fan-out point slice this group's chunks out of the flat list via chunk_offset strategy.commit_store_chunks() for this group's slice result = AND of all groups' outcomes commit_retrieve() -> single strategy.commit_retrieve() call (SHM read locks for every group were accumulated under the same transfer key during prepare_retrieve, so one call releases them all; pickle mode has nothing to release) ``` `TransferStrategy` (`server_transfer.py`) gained `commit_store_chunks()` / `prepare_retrieve_chunks()` so a multi-group caller can pass already-decoded tensors instead of re-pickling per group, and `ShmTransferStrategy` now accumulates reservations from multiple `prepare_store`/`prepare_retrieve` calls (one per group) under the same transfer key, so a single `commit_store`/`commit_retrieve` releases every group's locks together. ## 3. title: [Feature][MP] Support GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
body:
For #4966. 

GLM-5.3-Flash is KDA + sparse MLA (DSA) and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is GDN + QSA. LMCache already serves these cache kinds. What is new is the selector: DSA and QSA pick history from compressed keys, packing 4 tokens into one selection key. While a group is still open, its raw keys sit in a tiny per-request ring buffer, KpoolTailSpec in GLM (4 tokens) and CircularBufferSpec in Qwen (a few tokens, compress ratio plus speculative lookahead). The ring is one block per request, overwritten in place by position, and marked prefix_cacheable = False by vLLM. LMCache treated it as a normal group, so the storable prefix was the min over groups and STORE never happened. The core of this PR is to detect these scratch groups by prefix_cacheable and skip them end to end.

Also some fixes for making model run
1. Sub-paged MLA re-view only handled rank-3 caches
2. The Mamba unified view rejected BLNHC
3.  With a single KV head under NHD, the head and token dims have equal strides; contiguity recovery could not order them and rejected Qwen's compressed key.


Validated on a  4× H200, TP=4, vLLM main `385dce36` with GSM8K.

- [x] this PR contains unit tests

title: [RawBlock] Support padded payloads in batched io_uring put_many
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Regular io_uring `RawBlockCore.put_many` batches writes through `batched_write`, but padded entries (`payload_len < total_len`) fall back to per-entry `write_uring` calls because `batched_write` has no separate payload length. This PR lets padded payloads use the same batched path.

- Add an optional `payload_lens` argument to `batched_write` after `placement_ids`. Omitting it keeps `payload_lens == total_lens`.
- Share padded write preparation between `write_uring` and `batched_write`: the source is read only within its bounds, and `[payload_len, total_len)` is always written as zeroes.
- Route all regular io_uring writes in `RawBlockCore.put_many` through `batched_write`.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Padded `RawBlockCore` payloads are still bounced in Rust because `byte_array` exposes only the payload bytes. The gain is fewer submissions, not zero-copy.
- `batched_write` used to copy `total_len` bytes from each source, which could read past a shorter buffer. It now reads at most `payload_len` bytes and raises `ValueError` for a buffer shorter than that.
- `io_uring_cmd` writes are unchanged.

title: [Fix][FS Native] Fix fs native object group key parsing
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes fs_native filesystem key parsing for ObjectKey values that include `object_group_id`.

The Python fs_native adapter serializes keys as:

- unsalted: `model@kv_rank@object_group_id@chunk_hash`
- salted: `model@kv_rank@object_group_id@chunk_hash@cache_salt`

The C++ `FSConnector` still parsed the older 3/4-field format, so salted fs_native stores failed before creating the expected file. This PR updates the C++ parser to accept the current 4/5-field format and preserve `object_group_id` in generated filenames, matching the Python fs_l2 filename layout.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Added a native-backed regression test that exercises `NativeConnectorL2Adapter + LMCacheFSClient` instead of only mocking the native connector. The new test verifies both unsalted and salted fs_native stores create filenames with `object_group_id`.

Tested with:

- `NO_GPU_EXT=1 python -m pip install -e . --no-build-isolation`
- `python -m pytest -xvs tests/v1/distributed/test_fs_native_connector_keys.py`
- `python -m pytest -xvs tests/v1/distributed/test_native_connector_l2_adapter.py::TestObjectKeySerialization tests/v1/distributed/test_fs_l2_adapter_keys.py`
- `python -m ruff check --no-cache tests/v1/distributed/test_fs_native_connector_keys.py`

title: [Feature] Add raw-block I/O attempt metrics and safe failure cleanup
body:
## Summary
Refs #5016.

- Expose cumulative per-device I/O metrics through `report_status()` → `core.device_io`, using sharded counters and worker-local accumulation.
- Count backend attempts and requested submitted bytes, including retries; outstanding requests include queued work.
- Fix partial-submit tracking and fatal-error admission. Retain accepted I/O buffers until terminal completions; shutdown may wait indefinitely if requests cannot complete or be canceled.

## Validation
- Rust: 15 tests passed; metrics and admission tests retained without fault-injection hooks.
- Python: 114 passed, 1 skipped (raw-block device, core, key codec, and adapters).
- Release build and pre-commit checks passed.
- Updated documentation page builds without warnings; the full-site strict build still reports 31 pre-existing diagnostics.

title: Add optional force flag to clear RPC
body:
## Summary
- add an optional `force: bool = False` parameter to the shared clear RPC contract
- send the force flag through the ZMQ request payload and gRPC `ClearRequest` proto

title: Fix: periodic thread restart after failure
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Reset `PeriodicThread`'s running state when its run loop exits.

When `_execute()` raised `IrrecoverableException`, the run loop stopped without
clearing `_running`. Although `is_running` correctly reported that the worker was no
longer alive, a subsequent `start()` checked the stale flag, treated the thread as
still running, and refused to restart it.

The run loop now clears `_running` whenever it exits. The regression test exercises
the public API by terminating the first worker with an irrecoverable exception and
verifying that a second `start()` creates and runs a new worker.

body:

LMCache MP stores and retrieves KV correctly, but its vLLM connector does not currently publish completed MP stores through vLLM's KV-event path.

title: [Platform][RBLN] MLA (NL_X_NB_BS_HS) block transfer support
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adds MLA KV-cache support to the RBLN block-transfer path. vLLM-RBLN's MLA attention backend allocates each layer as `[NB, BS, HS]` (a single latent plane, no K/V split and no head axis), which the vLLM detector classifies as `EngineKVFormat.NL_X_NB_BS_HS`. `RblnDeviceOps` previously rejected everything but the HND attention layout, so MLA models could not use KV offloading on RBLN.

- `RblnDeviceOps.multi_layer_block_kv_transfer` now accepts the MLA format alongside HND, classifying it with `lmcache_native.is_mla()` and dispatching to an MLA-specific op sequence; the chunk/block bookkeeping stays shared. MLA layouts other than `NL_X_NB_BS_HS` are rejected at the format check with a format error.
- The MLA gather/scatter (`gather_blocks_to_chunk_mla` / `scatter_chunk_to_blocks_mla`) is built functionally (`index_select` + `stack`, `index_copy_`) so it stays on device-native v2v kernels and crosses the device boundary with one DMA per chunk. The shared torch path stages through `torch.empty(device=...)`, which on RBLN is a lazy SHM tensor that drops the ops onto the CPU-fallback path.
- `validate_mla_layers` pins the 3-D rank at the transfer boundary so a layout drift fails loudly instead of mis-addressing bytes.
- The existing HND kernels are renamed `gather_blocks_to_chunk_hnd` / `scatter_chunk_to_blocks_hnd` to mirror the `_mla` pair.

Chunks keep LMCache's canonical token-major wire layout (`[L, T, HS]` for MLA), so they remain byte-compatible with chunks produced on other devices. The design rationale is documented in `docs/design/v1/platform/rbln/README.md`.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Both layouts require the engine's KV caches to be real device tensors (`VLLM_RBLN_USE_DEVICE_TENSOR=1`); with compile-mode allocation the per-layer tensors are `meta` and any transfer dies at the first host copy.

title: fix(test): replace fixed sleeps with condition waits in distributed storage manager tests
body:
close #5135 

tests/v1/distributed/test_distributed_storage_manager.py is flaky. ref: https://buildkite.com/lmcache/unit-tests-xpu/builds/1485/list?sid=01a0a75f-81ff-4c1a-8a3f-2264d5d758a8&tab=output
https://buildkite.com/lmcache/unit-tests-xpu/builds/1457/list?sid=01a0a06a-7e9f-45ba-b884-c44a9bb6dcce&tab=output

After writing keys and waiting for them to become visible in L2, the test calls the non-force sm.delete_l1_keys([all_keys[1]]) to remove one key from L1. However, L2 visibility does not imply that the background StoreController has released its L1 read locks yet. While the read lock is still held, the non-force delete refuses the key and returns (deleted=0, skipped=1).

The same race also affects other tests in this file that do time.sleep(0.05); sm.clear() after waiting for L2 — the fixed 50 ms sleep is not a synchronization point, so sm.clear() can observe a non-empty / locked L1 as well.

L2 visibility can precede StoreController releasing its L1 read locks, so a fixed 0.05s sleep before clear/delete is racy. Add clear_l1_and_wait() that retries sm.clear() via wait_for_condition and checks the public report_status() API, and retry the non-force L1 delete in test_sparse_skip_l2_locks_only_l1.

title: [Fix][MP] More robust imported and exported IPC Event Lifetimes
body:
Refs #4419, #4640.

**Both lifetimes are released on facts, not inference: the transfer stream itself drops an imported worker event once it has consumed the wait (a host callback queued right after it), and the worker itself releases an exported completion event once it is done querying it (`RELEASE_EVENT`).**

Before:

```
WORKER                            SERVER

ev_w ─────────────────────────→ import ev_w
                                queue wait(ev_w)
                                copy
                                create ev_s
                                record ev_s
ev_s handle ←────────────────── export ev_s
                                |
                                handler returns
                                |
                        ev_w dies TOO EARLY
                        ev_s dies TOO EARLY
```

After:

```
WORKER                            SERVER / ContextEntry

ev_w ─────────────────────────→ ev_w' = import(ev_w)
                                ipc_events.track_imported(ev_w')
                                queue wait(ev_w')
                                queue host callback: drop ev_w'   <- fires only after the wait
                                copy
                                E17 = completion_event_pool.pop()
                                record E17
handle(E17) ←──────────────── export; ipc_events.track_exported(handle, E17)
                                |
                                handler returns: nothing dies
...
import(handle), query() == True
RELEASE_EVENT(handle) ────────→ E17 back to completion_event_pool
```

- **Exported events**: per-context pool (`completion_event_pool`, pre-warmed with 256, grows on demand); an event is held until the worker's `RELEASE_EVENT`, which `DeviceMessagingFuture` sends once for every client, then returns to the pool.
- **Imported events**: held in the shared `IPCEventRegistry` until the host callback queued on the transfer stream right after the wait fires.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core multiprocess GPU synchronization and wire protocol (`RELEASE_EVENT`); incorrect lifetimes or missed releases could cause racey KV reads/writes or resource leaks under concurrency.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes cross-process KV transfer ordering bugs where **exported completion events** and **imported worker events** could be freed too early, leading to silent cache corruption under load (LMCache#4422).
> 
> The server now keeps **exported** completion events alive until the worker sends a new **`RELEASE_EVENT`** RPC after `DeviceMessagingFuture` finishes on the device side. Each registered context uses a **pooled, long-lived completion event** (pre-warmed, grows on demand) that is **recorded and re-exported per transfer** instead of creating a fresh event every STORE/RETRIEVE/STORE_Q.
> 
> **Imported** worker events are held in a shared **`IPCEventRegistry`** until a **stream-ordered host callback** runs immediately after the transfer stream’s `wait_event`, proving the wait was consumed. Unregister/reap clears unreleased exports via `forget_pool`; **`report_status`** exposes pool and outstanding import/export counts.
> 
> Transport clients attach **`release_hook`** on messaging futures (ZMQ and gRPC) so release is automatic. Design docs describe the lifetime contract, including snapshot semantics for timeline-semaphore exports.
>

title: Read allocator sizes from a single locked snapshot in memcheck/usage reporting
body:
## Summary

Closes #3768.

`TensorMemoryAllocator.memcheck()` read free size, allocated size, and heap size through **separate** `AddressManager` calls:

```python
total_free_size = self.address_manager.get_free_size()
if (total_free_size + self.address_manager.total_allocated_size
        != self.address_manager.get_heap_size()):
    logger.error("Memory allocator size is inconsistent")
```

With lazy allocation, `sbrk()` can grow the address space **between** those reads, so the check compares a stale free size against a newer heap size and incorrectly logs `Memory allocator size is inconsistent` / returns `False` on a perfectly valid allocator. The same split-read pattern affected L1 memory-usage reporting, which derived `used`/`total` from separate address-manager reads.

## Fix

Add `AddressManager.get_size_snapshot()`, which captures `(free, allocated, heap)` atomically under the allocator's existing `_lock` and returns an `AddressSizeSnapshot`. All three values then describe one coherent state, so `free + allocated == heap` always holds for a consistent allocator regardless of concurrent `sbrk()` growth.

Routed through the snapshot:
- `TensorMemoryAllocator.memcheck`
- `gds_l1_memory_manager`: `memcheck` + `get_memory_usage`
- `l1_memory_manager`: `get_memory_usage`

All four sites operate on an `AddressManager` (verified: `TensorMemoryAllocator.address_manager`, GDS L1's `_address_manager`, and both branches of L1's `get_address_manager` — `pin_allocator.address_manager` and `LazyMemoryAllocator.get_address_manager()` — are `AddressManager` instances).

## Testing

Adds `TestAddressSizeSnapshot` to `tests/v1/test_address_manager.py`:
- snapshot fields match the individual accessors on a quiescent allocator;
- `free + allocated == heap` holds across allocate / free / sbrk;
- the invariant never breaks while a background thread grows the space via `sbrk()` (4 observer threads × 20k snapshots).

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `py_compile` pass on all changed files. (The allocator module imports `torch`, so the suite runs in CI; I additionally validated the snapshot arithmetic and concurrency guarantee with a standalone replica of the size bookkeeping.)

title: [Bugfix] Clean up aborted async lookups without future traffic
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #5006.

Async lookup cancellation previously only added the lookup ID to a Scheduler-side set. Cleanup messages were sent by a later `lookup_cache()` call after completion, so an idle or asymmetrically routed instance could retain the completed event and its prefetched memory indefinitely.

This change sends cleanup intent immediately from `cancel_lookup()`. Each worker tracks active lookups and deferred cleanup requests, including the window before EventManager registration. Result post-processing marks the lookup DONE only after it has finished, then triggers deferred cleanup locally. Cleanup after completion remains immediate, duplicate cleanup is ignored after the event is consumed, and no-hit lookups discard their tombstones.

The client response thread now drops completed responses for canceled lookups directly, so Scheduler-side state also no longer needs a future unrelated lookup to drain it.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

The completion transition intentionally occurs after prefetch result processing but before the response is sent. A second idempotent done callback covers exceptional result processing, allowing an aborted failed future to be removed as well.

Local validation was limited to small mock/state-machine tests; no model, GPU cache, or large allocator test was run. GitHub CI should run the broader suite.

 Following the discussion in https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/5058

title: [Fix][MP] honor kv_role when storing KV cache
body:
<!--  Thanks for your contribution to LMCache!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'Fixes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'Refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
  Fixes LMCache/LMCache#5143.

  LMCacheMPConnector previously submitted STORE operations even when configured as kv_consumer. This change prevents consumers from generating STORE metadata or lazy-offload candidates while preserving lookup, retrieval, token/block accounting, and request cleanup.

  Storage remains enabled for kv_producer and kv_both. The capability comes from the connector’s own configuration, so an outer MultiConnector configured as kv_consumer still permits a nested MP connector configured as kv_both to store.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

  Consumer completion no longer delays block release for saves. get_finished() continues polling retrievals but excludes consumer request IDs from store-completion processing. This prevents the adapter from reporting completed saves for already-released requests, which triggers a vLLM scheduler assertion.

  - GPU checks used Qwen3-8B, BF16, TP=1, CPU L1, 256-token MP chunks, and a 512-token prefill budget.
  - Cold and lazy consumers completed long requests with zero STORE submissions.  Restarted consumers retrieved 1,280 external tokens without writeback.
  - Shared-MP P/D: both/both baseline passed. With producer/consumer roles, prefill submitted four stores, decode submitted zero stores and two retrievals; completion telemetry and streaming both worked.
  - Native NIXL P/D: nested kv_both retained MP stores on both engines. After engine restart, prefill retrieved 1,024 tokens from its retained MP server. Changing only decode’s nested MP role to kv_consumer preserved NIXL handoff while eliminating decode MP stores.

GPU validation preceded the final test revisions; runtime behavior was unchanged by those revisions.

title: [Fix][RawBlock] Fix TOCTOU accounting bug in delete() by merging was_indexed into delete_many
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

`RawBlockL2Adapter.delete()` had a TOCTOU race between reading metadata and deleting:

```python
# old — two separate operations, not atomic
metas = self._core.get_metadata_many(encoded_keys)    # step 1
deleted_bitmap = self._core.delete_many(encoded_keys) # step 2
```

Between step 1 and step 2, an inflight key could be committed to `_index`. When that happened, `meta` was `None` (key not yet indexed at step 1), so `deleted_sizes` got `0` instead of `slot_bytes`. `_notify_keys_deleted` then under-reported the freed size, leaving `total_bytes_used` permanently inflated by one slot.

The fix merges the "was it indexed?" question into `delete_many` itself. `RawBlockCore.delete_many` now returns `list[RawBlockDeleteResult]` — a frozen dataclass with `deleted` and `was_indexed` — both fields captured atomically under `_lock`. The adapter reads `result.was_indexed` instead of calling `get_metadata_many` separately.

## Special notes for your reviewers

- `RustRawBlockBackend.remove()` also calls `delete_many`; it only needs `.deleted`, updated on the same line.
- `was_indexed` is `True` iff `removed_entry is not None` — i.e., the key was in `_index` (not merely `_inflight`) when the lock was held during deletion. Inflight-only deletes cancel the write but never charged `slot_bytes` to usage in the first place, so size 0 is correct.

## Tests

```
pytest tests/v1/distributed/test_raw_block_l2_adapter.py \
  -k "test_raw_block_l2_adapter_delete_indexed_key_deducts_slot_bytes or test_raw_block_l2_adapter_delete_inflight_key_keeps_usage_at_zero" \
  -v
```

Two new tests:
- `test_raw_block_l2_adapter_delete_indexed_key_deducts_slot_bytes` — store then delete, verify usage returns to 0 (was_indexed=True path).
- `test_raw_block_l2_adapter_delete_inflight_key_keeps_usage_at_zero` — races `delete()` against a write paused at `_write_one` to reproduce the TOCTOU window and verify usage stays at 0 (was_indexed=False path).

- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works

title: Fix: Reject unknown dtypes in standalone KV shape specs
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The standalone KV-cache shape parser previously defaulted unknown dtypes to `float16`. As a result, typos or unsupported dtype values could silently initialize the cache with an unintended dtype.

This PR:

- explicitly rejects unknown dtypes and reports the supported values
- aligns the standalone parser behavior with the shared KV shape parser
- corrects the parser docstring
- adds a regression test for unsupported dtypes

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

title: [MP] feat(nixl_store_dynamic): add shard_dirs option for 2-level subdir layout
body:
### Summary
Adds an **opt-in** `shard_dirs` backend param (default `false`) to the MP dynamic NIXL L2 adapter (`nixl_store_dynamic`). When enabled, it lays out per-key files in a 2-level hash-prefix subdirectory tree (`file_path/<hex[:2]>/<hex[2:4]>/<name>`, where `hex` is `chunk_hash.hex()`) instead of one flat directory.

Default is unchanged behavior — nothing moves unless you turn it on.

### Current layout (today, `shard_dirs=false`)
Every per-key file lives directly under `file_path`, in one flat directory:
```
/mnt/kvcache/model--Name_00000000_0_834ebc79....bin
/mnt/kvcache/model--Name_00000000_0_1734d4a0....bin
/mnt/kvcache/...                              ← grows to a large number of files in ONE dir
```
The dynamic adapter creates files on demand and holds a large, LRU-bounded steady-state set (and persists them across restarts), so this directory can accumulate a very large number of files in one place.

### New layout (opt-in, `shard_dirs=true`)
The subdir is the first four hex chars of the chunk hash — the same value already in the filename — split into two levels:
```
/mnt/kvcache/83/4e/model--Name_00000000_0_834ebc79....bin
/mnt/kvcache/17/34/model--Name_00000000_0_1734d4a0....bin
                └── <hex[:2]>/<hex[2:4]>/
```
So the subdir matches the leading hex of the file's own name (`834e…` → `83/4e/`).
Spreading files across subdirectories keeps each directory small and scales well on a parallel filesystem (e.g. Lustre), with a uniform 256×256 fanout.

### Design notes
This is the same 2-level hash-prefix idea the GDS backend uses, applied to the MP dynamic NIXL adapter (the NIXL store itself has always been flat). It keys on `chunk_hash.hex()` (GDS renders the hash as a decimal string; hex here is uniform and matches the filename's hash prefix).

Scope: **dynamic adapter only.** The static `nixl_store` pool is bounded by `pool_size` and the OS open-file-descriptor limit (it pre-opens every slot file), so it can't reach the file counts where directory layout matters.

### Compatibility
`shard_dirs` is a **deploy-time choice** — the layout is a pure function of the config, so there is no runtime fallback or per-read lookup:
- **`shard_dirs=false` (default):** byte-for-byte the current flat behavior.
- **`shard_dirs=true`:** all files (store and read) use the subdir layout.

Enable it on a fresh cache directory. Converting an existing flat cache is out of scope for this PR — it would be a one-off offline migration script, only if ever needed.

### Tests
- `_object_key_to_relpath`: hex hash-prefix levels, subdir matches the filename hash prefix,
  spread across all 256 top-level subdirs, two-level structure.
- Integration: a store lands in the subdir (not flat) and loads back with data intact.
- Existing tests unchanged (default flat). **35 passed.**

title: Add batched_async_contains to NixlStaticStorageBackend
body:
### What
Implement `batched_async_contains` for `NixlStaticStorageBackend`, following the existing implementations in `LocalDiskBackend`, `LocalCPUBackend`, and `NixlDynamicStorageBackend` (#2966). Uses a fail-fast managed-thread loop over `self.contains`. 
  
### Why
`LocalDiskBackend`, `LocalCPUBackend`, the audit/p2p backends, and `NixlDynamicStorageBackend` (#2966) all implement `batched_async_contains`, so they support async loading. `NixlStaticStorageBackend` does not — it falls through to `AbstractStorageBackend.batched_async_contains`, which raises `NotImplementedError`. So with `LMCACHE_ENABLE_ASYNC_LOADING=True` and a NIXL static backend, every lookup waits the full `LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS` and then recomputes. This brings the static backend to parity with the others.

(Intentionally a per-backend override rather than a base default — async loading should remain an explicit opt-in per backend, since not every backend's `contains` is appropriate to drive from the async path.)
  
### How
Same fail-fast batched approach as the dynamic backend (`_CONTAINS_BATCH_SIZE` batches over `self.contains`, stopping at the first miss). Adds regression tests covering: empty keys, all present, stop-at-first-miss, and pin-on-hit.

### Performance
Beyond enabling the feature (without this, async loading on a static NIXL backend isn't usable — it hangs on the lookup timeout and recomputes), it gives async loading's intended benefit of overlapping retrieval with compute.

In our testing (concurrency=8, 30K-token prompts, warm reads, measured via the in-process NIXL POSIX path), enabling async loading on the static NIXL backend reduced TTFT by approximately 20–30% and increased sustained read bandwidth by roughly 35–70% compared to async loading disabled. As expected, the benefit only appears under concurrent workloads, where async loading can overlap cache lookups with GPU compute and hide retrieval latency. At concurrency=1 there is no measurable improvement, because there is no opportunity to overlap work.

title: [MP][Maru] Maru CXL L1 backend for MP mode
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**: This PR adds [Maru](https://github.com/xcena-dev/maru), a CXL shared-memory KV cache engine, as a **shared L1 tier** for MP mode — the shared-L1 counterpart to the in-process Maru backend from #2705. Today each MP server has a private, node-local L1 (pinned DRAM / Device-DAX / GDS). With Maru, MP servers on separate nodes `mmap` one CXL pool and read each other's entries zero-copy: a node that never stored a key still hits it if a peer did, with no network transfer. Control stays entirely with LMCache. Maru is a sibling L1 manager (`MaruL1Manager`) behind a new structural `L1ManagerInterface` Protocol; the stock controllers, L1↔L2 tiering, eviction, and L2 adapters run unchanged on top. The L1 core (`l1_manager.py`, `l1_memory_manager.py`, `internal_api.py`) is byte-identical to `dev`; the remaining edits are additive wiring only. Design doc: `docs/design/v1/distributed/maru_l1.md` · Maru: [docs](https://xcena-dev.github.io/maru/) / [github](https://github.com/xcena-dev/maru) **Benchmark**:
setup - Hardware: 1× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96 GB), Intel Xeon 6730P (Granite Rapids), 1 TB DRAM; CXL pool via Device-DAX (`/dev/dax9.0`, 500 GB), served by `maru-server` + maru-resource-manager - Versions: vLLM 0.24.0 · LMCache v0.1.dev1942 · Maru 0.1.0 · model `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` (bf16 KV) - Workload: `lmcache bench engine`, `long-doc-qa` — one exported config replayed unchanged against all three setups: 40 GB KV volume → 29 documents × 10k tokens (`tokens_per_gb_kvcache=7281`), 1 query/doc, `tile` order, 4 in-flight, 128 output tokens (`ignore_eos`), seed 42 - vLLM identical in all runs: `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.5` (GPU KV ≈ 30 GiB ≈ 220k tokens < 290k-token workload, so the GPU cache alone cannot hold the working set), default prefix caching, chunk size 256 - LMCache server (MP mode, `lmcache_driven`): **B** `--l1-size-gb 60` (DRAM L1, default lazy allocator) · **B′** same + `--no-l1-use-lazy` (preallocated `MixedMemoryAllocator`) · **C** `--maru-server-url maru://localhost:5555 --maru-pool-size-gb 60 --l1-size-gb 0` (Maru CXL L1); same 60 GB capacity, no eviction in any run - All cached runs had identical cache behavior — warm-up pass all-miss, measured pass **100% hit** (289,536 / 289,536 lookup tokens, from Prometheus counters) — so the deltas between B/B′/C isolate the L1 medium and allocator, not hit-rate differences
| Metric | A: vLLM alone | B: MP + DRAM L1 (lazy alloc, default) | B′: MP + DRAM L1 (mixed alloc) | C: MP + Maru L1 | |---|---|---|---|---| | Mean TTFT (ms) | 1404.0 | 215.7 (**−84.6%**) | 178.3 (**−87.3%**) | 184.6 (**−86.9%**) | | P50 TTFT (ms) | 1244.7 | 206.5 | 175.6 | 181.3 | | P90 TTFT (ms) | 2022.2 | 234.0 | 197.7 | 204.8 | | P99 TTFT (ms) | 2032.7 | 376.2 | 263.2 | 283.0 | | Benchmark duration (s) | 30.13 | 17.73 | 16.69 | 16.58 | | Input throughput (tok/s) | 9,639 | 16,380 | 17,395 | 17,516 | | Output throughput (tok/s) | 123.2 | 209.4 | 222.4 | 223.9 | | Mean decode speed (tok/s) | 53.1 | 66.3 | 66.7 | 66.6 | | Mean request latency (ms) | 3,905 | 2,150 | 2,101 | 2,109 | All runs: 29/29 requests successful, 290,396 input tokens. B′ = B with `--no-l1-use-lazy` (preallocated pinned-DRAM `MixedMemoryAllocator` instead of the default `LazyMemoryAllocator`). - Maru CXL L1 vs DRAM L1: with identical 100% hit rates Grafana (LMCache MP dashboard) during the runs — L1 usage filling over the warm-up pass and 100%-hit read phase: | DRAM L1 (run B) | Maru L1 (run C) | |---|---| | | | **Special notes for your reviewers**: - **Control / directory split.** LMCache decides everything (store / evict / promote / pin); the passive `MaruServer` is only a shared directory (key → region/offset) plus a cross-node `pin_count`. Page reclamation is driven by LMCache eviction, so the allocator's `free` is a no-op. - **Why a sibling, not an allocator swap.** A private tier keeps membership and locks in a local dict; a shared tier needs them authoritative in the shared directory (cross-node reads and pins). `MaruMemoryAllocator` supplies the CXL medium, `MaruL1Manager` the shared control. (The MP Coordinator is unrelated: it plans fleet-wide L2 eviction on logical keys, not L1 physical-page state.) A later `L1StateBackend` seam to shrink the sibling is possible follow-up, out of scope here. - **Startup guards** reject unsupported combos up front: gds/devdax, `skip_l1` store policy, registered/RDMA-type L2 (copy-type only), p2p, and engine_driven/auto transfer mode. **If applicable**: - [x] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added (`docs/source/mp/configuration.rst` + design doc) - [x] this PR contains unit tests

title: docs: codify the log format-specifier convention in coding standards
body:
## Summary

Closes #3785 (Direction A — the lightweight option proposed in the issue).

The issue notes that converting f-string log calls to `%`-format isn't a mechanical find-and-replace because the right specifier depends on the variable's type — and some names (`instance_id`) are `str` in most modules but `int` (GPU index) in a few multiprocess modules. It asks whether "`%d` for `int`, `%s` for everything else" is the right convention and offers to document it.

This PR documents exactly that, in `docs/coding_standards.md` §7.4 (Logging):

- Prefer lazy `%`-formatting over f-strings in log calls.
- Choose the specifier from the variable's **type annotation**, not neighboring calls: `%d` for `int`, `%s` for everything else (`str`/`bool`/objects/exceptions), `%f`/`%.2f` for floats.
- Calls out the `instance_id` str-vs-int ambiguity and the bool `%d`→`1`/`0` vs `%s`→`True`/`False` gotcha.

This gives the f-string→%-format conversions (e.g. #3794, my #3797) a single convention to follow.

## Testing

Docs-only change. `codespell --toml pyproject.toml docs/coding_standards.md` passes.

If maintainers prefer Direction B (unifying `instance_id`'s type) instead, happy to close this — but the convention is useful either way.

title: lint: enforce G004 (lazy %-format logging) with temporary ignores for un-migrated code (#5118)
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Refs #5118
Refs #3372

Enables ruff's `G004` ("logging statement uses f-string") and adds temporary
`per-file-ignores` for the files that have not been migrated to lazy `%`-format
logging yet — the first step requested by @maobaolong in #5118.

`logging` renders a record lazily as `msg % args`, so an f-string pays for its
formatting even when the level is disabled. Today nothing prevents a new
`logger.info(f"...")` from landing in a file that was already migrated, which is
why this keeps generating one-file good-first-issue PRs: 15+ such PRs have been
merged since March 2026 (#5014, #5094, #4970, #4785, #4727, #4650, #4479, #4357,
#4290, #4142, #4124, #4102, #3977, #3975, #3973) and #4937, #4506, #5106, #5110,
#5112 are still open.

### Why the ignore list is mostly per file

Ruff matches `per-file-ignores` patterns with `*` **crossing directory
separators**, so `"lmcache/*.py" = ["G004"]` silently ignores the whole package
subtree. A naive per-directory list (`lmcache/*.py`, `lmcache/v1/*.py`,
`lmcache/v1/storage_backend/*.py`, ...) would additionally ignore **771
already-migrated files**, leaving only 494 of 1337 lintable files protected —
including `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/` and `lmcache/v1/distributed/`, the two
directories that already enforce SLF.

So the list is derived from the actual violations:

* `"<dir>/**" = ["G004"]` only where *every* file below that directory violates
  the rule — 4 entries: `benchmarks/storage_backend_io`, `examples/disagg_prefill`,
  `examples/disagg_prefill_mp`, `examples/token_dropping/rkv_variants`;
* an explicit file entry otherwise — 66 entries.

Result: exactly the 72 violating files are ignored and no clean file is (checked
programmatically), while the rule guards the other 1265 files. Entries can be
deleted one by one as migration continues; each one is either a single file or a
directory that is entirely un-migrated.

Notebooks are covered too — `examples/token_dropping/*.ipynb` and
`examples/token_dropping/rkv_variants/**` account for 41 of the 223 violations.

### Verification

* `ruff check .` → `All checks passed!`, `ruff check --statistics .` → no findings.
* Enforcement sentinel (three temporary files containing `logger.info(f"...")`,
  deleted again afterwards): `lmcache/v1/multiprocess/<file>`,
  `lmcache/v1/storage_backend/plugins/<file>` (a subdirectory of an un-migrated
  directory) and `lmcache/v1/distributed/<file>` were all reported as `G004`,
  while the ignored files stayed quiet.
* Ignore-set audit: the 70 entries cover all 72 violating files and ignore zero
  clean files.
* `SKIP=rust-fmt,rust-clippy pre-commit run --all-files` → all hooks pass
  (`cargo` is not installed in my environment).

**Special notes for your reviewers**:
- This PR only changes `pyproject.toml`; no runtime code is touched.
- `G201` (24 sites) and `G002` (1 site) are deliberately not enabled: they change
  *what* is logged rather than *when* it is formatted, so they deserve a separate
  decision (noted in #5118).
- The follow-up — delete one ignore entry per migrated file/directory — is a good
  fit for new contributors, as you suggested.

**If applicable**:
- [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [ ] this PR contains unit tests

Daily automated docs-drift check between LMCache multi-process (MP) mode documentation and the current code on `dev`. Today's changes on `dev` include #4953 (`feat(multiprocess): add gRPC request transport and run grpc & zmq in test`), which landed the gRPC runtime and the new `--grpc-server-workers` flag. title: [fix] lookup: record sub-chunk lookups on the session
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

A request whose prompt is shorter than one chunk succeeds, but logs a warning on
every single request:

```
Session <id> has no lookup ipc key, skipping touch
```

**Reproduction.** Chunk size 1024, `gemma-4-31B-it`, MP server, sequential then
4-way concurrent:

| Requests | Prompt tokens | HTTP | Matching warnings |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| short: initial, repeated, 4 concurrent | 31 | 6/6 200 | 6 |
| long: initial, repeated, 4 concurrent | 3462 | 6/6 200 | 0 |

The very first sequential short request reproduces it, so concurrency, restart
and warm prefix-cache state are not prerequisites. An ordinary cache miss is not
sufficient either: the first long request also reported `found_count=0` and did
not warn.

**Root cause** (verified on `dev` at 5001a52c):

1. `compute_chunk_hashes` hashes complete chunks only, so a 31-token prompt at
   chunk size 1024 returns `[]`.
2. `lookup()` therefore takes the `empty_chunk_hashes` early exit and returns
   *before* `session.begin_lookup()`, so no session records the lookup key.
3. `query_prefetch_status()` nevertheless calls
   `session_manager.get_or_create(job.request_id)` to record the zero-hit
   result -- materializing a session whose `lookup_ipc_key` defaults to `None`.
4. Such a request stores no complete chunk either, so the fallback in
   `MPCacheServerContext.resolve_object_keys` never supplies the key.
5. `end_session()` finds the missing key and warns.

So `empty_chunk_hashes` is the one early exit that is both a *success* path and
a path that skips `begin_lookup()`. `no_group_layout_descs` returns after it and
is already well-formed; `no_gpu_context` is a genuine error path that has
already logged `logger.error`.

**The fix.** Record the lookup on the session in that branch exactly as the
normal path does. The session is then well-formed, and `end_session` resolves an
empty key set from it quietly -- while still touching the chunk if generation
later crosses a chunk boundary and stores. `end_session` additionally returns
before dispatching an empty key list through the L1 touch listeners and the
`L1_KEYS_ACCESSED` event.

Impact is log noise proportional to short-request volume -- these requests
succeed, and there is no missed L1 touch, because there is no cacheable chunk to
touch. But the noise masks the same warning when it does indicate a real session
lifecycle problem.

Refs #3020 (introduced the lookup key and the unified end-session touch), and
#4094 for the short-prompt / whole-chunk-storage behavior.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

The warning itself is deliberately unchanged -- no suppression, no level change.
It still fires for a missing session, and for a session that has cacheable
chunks but never recorded a lookup; both are pinned as regression guards in
`tests/v1/multiprocess/test_short_prompt_session.py`, since a fix of this shape
is only correct if it stays targeted.

Two things worth knowing while reviewing:

- `ipc_key_to_object_keys` reads only model/world/worker/salt from the key,
  never `token_ids`. Storing the lookup key therefore resolves the same touch
  set the existing `resolve_object_keys` fallback would have produced for a
  prompt that grows past a chunk boundary during generation. That case is a
  regression guard here, not a behavior change.
- `no_gpu_context` still ends with the same warning, because the polling
  `get_or_create` leaves it a keyless session too. That is left alone on
  purpose: there the session really is incompletely initialized, and the path
  has already logged an error. A test pins that it stays loud.

Not addressed here, and worth a separate look: that same `get_or_create` during
polling can resurrect a session after `end_session` removed it, leaving an entry
until the TTL sweep. It is a distinct race with a distinct fix.

Tested with `pytest tests/v1/multiprocess/`. Note that this directory is
excluded from the default suite command in `AGENTS.md`, so it needs running
explicitly. The 14 new tests fail on 5001a52c and pass with the change.

title: [Model Support][MP] Add safe prompt-only caching for R-SWA
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes #5001.

R-SWA keeps the prompt KV around, but releases decode blocks once they leave
the active window. LMCacheMP currently treats that block table as an
append-only prefix. It can end up saving a released slot under a valid token
key, which makes a later lookup look like a good cache hit when it isn't.

This patch caches only the initial prompt for R-SWA. Lookup, store, retrieve,
and lock cleanup use the same boundary. Decode tokens stay available for
bookkeeping, but don't go into the cache. Resumable requests bypass LMCache,
since later turns can extend the reference region. The new policy also gets
its own model namespace so it can't read unsafe entries left by an older client.

The support is in LMCache's external MP connector; the in-process connector
rejects R-SWA at startup. The Unlimited-OCR recipe keeps vLLM prefix caching
off and the multimodal processor cache on. Turning both off can produce
renderer-local image IDs that repeat across restarts, so this R-SWA path
rejects that combination too.

After #4847, request lifecycle events use the new lazy-offload manager. A
cache-bypass request never takes over an older request's deferred session
under a reused ID. The manager still waits for all worker receipts before
unpinning submitted blocks or releasing a cached request's session.

Unlimited-OCR itself uses **immediate offload**, not lazy offload. Both
upstream lazy-offload policies require vLLM prefix caching, which the model
disables. The recipe now sets `lmcache.mp.lazy_offload=false` explicitly;
the upstream startup guard is unchanged.

**Validation**:

- The CPU reproduction uses vLLM's real `RSWAManager`: with a 256-token prompt
  and decode to 512 tokens, it releases blocks the old tracker would still save.
- 264 related tests pass after syncing with `dev` at `3a09d3b9`, covering
  prompt boundaries, mixed KV groups,
  preemption, lazy offload, early aborts, completion handshakes, multimodal keys,
  and existing DCP/layout behavior. This includes the upstream nonblocking
  lookup and pending-push checks, plus coverage for per-request offload limits
  and lookup timing. A write budget can shorten prompt stores but cannot
  admit decode KV or suppress reads of already-cached prompt KV. Bypassed
  requests do not start a lookup timer or emit lookup samples.
  The deleted pending-store tests were replaced with 28 cases using real
  vLLM requests/block pools and both new manager policies: coalescing,
  preemption, reused IDs, failed/late worker receipts, pin release, and APC-off
  startup rejection. These CPU lifecycle tests do not claim Unlimited-OCR
  supports lazy offload.
- Repeated GPU validation on September 17 after this sync, using
  `baidu/Unlimited-OCR`, vLLM `4fc943b8676e`, BF16, and one A100. A 279-token
  single-image prompt writes one 256-token chunk; its warm request retrieves
  that chunk without another store. A separate 512-token prompt writes and
  retrieves two chunks. Its warm request recomputes the last prompt token
  (`num_cached_tokens=511`) and completes generation. All four runs generate
  320 tokens, crossing another chunk boundary without storing decode KV.
  These are cache-transport and long-decode smoke tests, not OCR-accuracy or
  bitwise-equivalence results: cold/warm output tokens differed. LMCache used
  its Torch transfer fallback in this environment, not compiled `cuda_ops`.
- Pre-commit passes on the changed files, with the unchanged Rust hooks skipped.
- The changed Sphinx pages render without new diagnostics. The full `-W` build
  still fails on 31 existing warnings/errors elsewhere in the docs; the
  diagnostics match a clean `3a09d3b9` build after normalizing checkout paths.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Use `kv_connector_module_path="lmcache.integration.vllm.lmcache_mp_connector"`.
vLLM's vendored MP connector and `use_native=true` aren't covered. I tested
single-image requests; CacheBlend, compression, and multi-image requests still
need separate validation. No lazy-offload GPU support is claimed for
Unlimited-OCR; the new manager tests exercise its CPU lifecycle contract only.

title: fix(l2_adapters): don't crash CLI when an adapter import raises non-ImportError (#4204)
body:
## Summary

`lmcache server` — even `lmcache server --help` — crashes on startup when an installed optional adapter dependency is incompatible with the environment, before any server logic runs. This affects users who never use the offending adapter, because adapter enumeration is mandatory at CLI construction time.

Fixes #4204.

## Root cause

`load_all_adapters()` force-imports every pending L2 adapter module so the CLI help can list all registered type names. It only caught `ImportError`:

```python
try:
    importlib.import_module(mod_path)
except ImportError:
    logger.debug("Skipping module %s during bulk load", mod_path)
```

A *missing* third-party dep raises `ImportError` and is skipped correctly. But an *installed but incompatible* one can raise something else during import — e.g. an incompatible `google-cloud-bigtable` / `protobuf` pairing raises `TypeError` while building the generated proto descriptors. That escaped the handler and took the whole CLI down:

```
File ".../lmcache/v1/distributed/config.py", line 524, in add_storage_manager_args
    add_l2_adapters_args(parser)
  ...
TypeError: ...
```

## Fix

Bulk enumeration is best-effort (it only backs the CLI help string), so any module that fails to import for any reason should be skipped and logged at debug rather than allowed to crash the CLI. Broadened the handler to `except Exception` and included the error in the debug log for diagnosability. The narrower per-adapter path (`ensure_adapter_loaded`) is untouched, so a real requested adapter still surfaces its import error.

## Testing

`lmcache server --help` no longer aborts when the bigtable adapter's protobuf conflict raises `TypeError`; the adapter is skipped and the remaining adapters/help render normally.

title: feat: add vllm DP support
body:
<!--  Thanks for your contribution to LMCache!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'Fixes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'Refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Under DP, vLLM's gpu_worker shifts each worker's local device by `dp_local_rank * tp_size * pp_size` so DP replica k binds to GPUs [k*W, (k+1)*W). LMCache however used parallel_config.rank directly as local_worker_id and then called torch.cuda.set_device, which left LMCache on cuda:0 while the DP>0 worker was on cuda:1+. The mismatched device for CUDA events/streams produced:

  RuntimeError: Event device index does not match recording stream's
  device index

Mirror vLLM's adjustment by adding compute_dp_device_offset(), gated on the same conditions vLLM uses (single-node-per-DP, non-Ray / non-external_launcher executor backend). For ray / external_launcher the runtime already isolates each worker to a single visible device, so no offset is applied. Both call sites (create_lmcache_metadata, calculate_local_rank_and_world_size) now share this helper.

Add unit tests covering DP enabled/disabled, TP-only, TP+PP, Ray, external_launcher, Ray DP backend, multi-node DP, and missing optional attributes on older vLLM versions.

Verified end-to-end with vLLM data parallelism (DP); works as expected.

title: [MACA] Add Buildkite CI pipeline for MetaX MACA hardware
body:
Adds a classic (non-K8s) Buildkite pipeline for the `metax-maca` queue, matching the bare-metal pattern the main `pipeline.yml` itself already uses on its own queue rather than the `k3_tests/` K8s-based pattern used by AMD/XPU/MUSA: this queue is a single dedicated host with one GPU, so we are not using K3s for this queue.

## What's included

- `common-setup.sh`: shared venv/install/env setup for both lanes below.  Reuses one fixed venv (recreated each run) rather than a per-build-id venv,  since this is a persistent host with limited disk, not an ephemeral pod.  Includes a disk-space guard, `uv` cache pruning, `MACA_MPS_MODE=1` (fixes a  cross-process CUDA event ordering timeout), and a `no_proxy` exemption for
  localhost (the host's proxy otherwise intercepts tests that spin up a real  local HTTP server, causing spurious 503s).
- `run-smoke-tests.sh`: fast subset for PR feedback.
- `run-unit-tests.sh`: full suite on push to `dev`, matching the scope of the  main CUDA "Unit Tests" step. Both scripts delete the whole workspace after  running, matching that step's own convention.
- `pipeline.yml` / `buildkite-pipeline.yml` / `BK_WEB_SETUP.md`: pipeline  definition and web UI setup doc, following the AMD/XPU/MUSA/sglang  convention (including "Skip queued / cancel running branch builds").

## Test scope

A handful of cases are excluded, each documented inline in `run-unit-tests.sh` with the evidence behind it:

- Two confirmed structural gaps: MACA's Triton backend lacks one FP8  conversion; two files under `tests/v1/platform/` depend on NVIDIA-only  `cuda.bindings` for raw CUDA IPC (the same category ROCm is already  excluded from upstream).
- A confirmed environmental flake (single-GPU host timing, not reproducible  in isolation).
- A small, deliberately-parked cluster of MP-server-round-trip timeouts  (mostly under `tests/v1/multiprocess/`) .

## Verification

Both scripts run end-to-end via their real Buildkite invocation path on MetaX C500 hardware:

- Smoke: 1242 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped (~1 min).
- Full suite (`--maxfail=1`, the real production config): 6359 passed,  0 failed, 281 skipped, 5 deselected, ~21 min.

## Still needed before this queue is fully live

- A real Buildkite agent token -- needs to be issued by an LMCache org  admin.

title: [MP][Coordinator] Let an operator leave a built-in controller unbuilt
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Adds `extra_config["disabled_controllers"]`, a list of controller class names to leave unbuilt — the other half of `controller_packages` from #4760.


```bash
lmcache coordinator --extra-config '{
  "controller_packages": ["acme_controllers"],
  "disabled_controllers": ["FleetEvictionController"]
}'
```

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- **A disable name that matches nothing raises at startup**, matching how `controller_packages` treats a package that does not import: an operator believing they disabled something they did not is worse than a boot failure that says so, because a typo would silently leave the built-in controller running against its replacement.
- **Why a name list rather than `--disable-eviction-controller`.** A flag per controller does not generalize, and this is symmetric with `controller_packages` — same shape, same validation, same file. The cost is that it is stringly-typed, which the startup-time check for unknown names is meant to cover.
- **The route move is behavior-preserving** when the controller is built: same paths, same schemas, same responses. It is a separate commit and can be split into its own PR if you would rather review it apart from the switch — though the switch is not much use without it, since a disabled controller would otherwise leave routes that shadow its replacement's.
- **Durable state survives the swap.** Sections are named by the component, not by its owner, so a replacement controller inherits the pins and quotas the built-in one held — provided only one of them is built, which is exactly what this PR makes possible.

Tested: `tests/v1/mp_coordinator` 429 passed, `tests/v1/multiprocess` 718 passed / 1 skipped.

title: [Deprecation] Complete in-process KV-cache deprecation and MP migration guidance
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The legacy documentation already marks in-process mode deprecated, but runtime startup provides no migration notice and some onboarding instructions still promote or incorrectly select that mode. 
This PR makes the existing soft deprecation consistent while retaining working legacy deployments.

- Log one actionable WARNING per operating-system process when the legacy KV engine or vLLM connector is constructed. Both entry points share a PID-aware guard, covering scheduler-only vLLM startup and allowing forked children to emit their own warning. Imports and shared configuration/metadata remain silent.
- Make MP the primary quickstart path where the integration and required features are supported. Preserve vLLM connector-version requirements, correct SGLang mode-selection guidance, use separate MP/legacy configuration files, and qualify TensorRT-LLM connector-preset requirements.
- Add `legacy/migration_to_mp` with configuration mappings, server pool sizing, cache-format precautions, store/retrieval verification, feature gaps, and rollback instructions that preserve existing configuration and cache data.
- Label legacy tutorial/example sections explicitly without deprecating shared tools or their MP functionality. Clarify that the separate encoder-cache engine is outside this KV-cache deprecation.
- Add regression coverage for legacy startup and deduplication, scheduler-only warnings, isolated fork behavior, silent shared imports, and actual MP server startup over ZMQ and gRPC. Negative checks include a logging positive control so disabled capture cannot produce a false pass.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

Production changes are limited to `lmcache/deprecation.py` and calls from `LMCacheEngine.__init__` and `LMCacheConnectorV1Impl.__init__`. Legacy SGLang and TensorRT-LLM engine construction reaches the same engine boundary. The warning uses the existing logger and is independent of the startup banner.

No existing files are deleted or renamed. Legacy APIs, configuration defaults, request handling, and shutdown behavior remain intact. MP implementations, shared config/metadata types, dedicated MP documentation/examples, and `AGENTS.md` are unchanged. There is no automatic mode switch, server launch, configuration translation, removal date, or new maintenance guarantee.

Migration does not imply feature parity: the guide records MP CacheGen and encoder-cache gaps, unverified hidden-state parity, platform-specific SGLang restrictions, and version-dependent TensorRT-LLM support. CacheBlend has an MP implementation with different configuration.

title: feat(operator): add runtimeClassName override to LMCacheEngine
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it
The operator forces `runtimeClassName: nvidia` on the engine pods whenever `gpuVendor` is `nvidia` (the default). That `nvidia` RuntimeClass object is created by the **NVIDIA GPU Operator** , so on NVIDIA clusters that serve GPUs **without the GPU Operator** (device plugin on containerd's default runtime), the object doesn't exist and every engine pod is **admission-rejected**, leaving the DaemonSet stuck at 0.

This PR adds an optional `spec.runtimeClassName` override: an empty string clears it so pods run on the **default container runtime**, while `gpuVendor` stays `nvidia` (keeps `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all`, etc.). Unset = today's behavior, unchanged.

**New Behavior:**

| `runtimeClassName` set to | Result |
|---|---|
| *(unset / nil)* | vendor default — `nvidia` ⇒ `"nvidia"` class, `amd` ⇒ none (unchanged) |
| `""` (empty) | no runtimeClassName → default runtime (the Nebius fix) |
| `"foo"` | uses `foo` verbatim (works with any vendor) |

## Failure Example
On a Nebius 8xB200 cluster (containerd `default_runtime_name` is already `nvidia`, GPUs via the device plugin, **no GPU Operator**), the engine DaemonSet can't create any pods:

```nginx
Warning  FailedCreate  daemonset/tensormesh-engine
Error creating: pods "tensormesh-engine-" is forbidden: pod rejected: RuntimeClass "nvidia" not found

# daemonset.apps/tensormesh-engine   DESIRED 2   CURRENT 0   READY 0
# lmcacheengine ... phase: Pending   (ConfigValid=True, but 0/2 instances ready)
```

## Special notes for your reviewers
Add an optional override field and apply it after the vendor-derived default (nil = derive, "" = clear, "x" = use x). No behavior change unless the field is set.
```GO
operator/api/v1alpha1/lmcacheengine_types.go  (new field on LMCacheEngineSpec)

+	RuntimeClassName *string `json:"runtimeClassName,omitempty"`

operator/internal/resources/daemonset.go  (buildDaemonSetCore)

#### BEFORE
	gpuVendor := derefString(spec.GPUVendor, lmcachev1alpha1.GPUVendorNvidia)
	var runtimeClassName *string
	if gpuVendor == lmcachev1alpha1.GPUVendorNvidia {
		rc := nvidiaRuntimeClass          // always "nvidia" — no way to opt out
		runtimeClassName = &rc
	}

#### AFTER  (+ explicit override)
	if gpuVendor == lmcachev1alpha1.GPUVendorNvidia {
		rc := nvidiaRuntimeClass
		runtimeClassName = &rc
	}
+	// explicit override wins; "" clears it -> default container runtime.
+	if spec.RuntimeClassName != nil {
+		if *spec.RuntimeClassName == "" {
+			runtimeClassName = nil
+		} else {
+			rc := *spec.RuntimeClassName
+			runtimeClassName = &rc
+		}
+	}
````

title: [Feature][RawBlock] Enable fixed-buffer I/O for MP L1 memory
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Partially addresses #4100 by enabling fixed-buffer I/O for stable MP L1 ranges. Incremental registration as lazy memory grows and splitting I/O across registered-region boundaries remain follow-up work.

The multiprocessing raw-block adapter previously always used ordinary io_uring buffers because it had no safe description of which L1 memory range could remain registered. Registering the final arena capacity directly is unsafe when only a lazy prefix is stable and is inappropriate for POSIX shared memory.

- Extends the L1 memory descriptor with an optional stable registration size.
- Exposes the full anonymous mixed-memory arena, no range for POSIX shared memory, and a bounded snapshot of the current lazy-memory prefix.
- Registers eligible L1 memory when io_uring and zero-copy are enabled, splitting ranges into regions no larger than 1 GiB.
- Falls back to ordinary io_uring when no stable range exists or kernel registration fails.
- Resolves interior buffer views to their registered region and uses fixed read/write SQEs only when the complete request fits within one region.
- Validates registered ranges and serializes registration with device shutdown.
- Adds descriptor, adapter, core, Rust range-resolution, and device integration coverage.

**Special notes for your reviewers**:

- Requests crossing registered-region boundaries intentionally use ordinary io_uring SQEs.
- Fixed-buffer registration is one-shot and best-effort; failure does not make the adapter unhealthy.

**If applicable**:

- [ ] this PR contains user facing changes - docs added
- [x] this PR contains unit tests

### Load performance

A/B testing with `lmcache bench l2`, using a wrapper to supply the production lazy L1 allocator: **20 GiB default initial size, 100 GiB final capacity**. The benchmark’s timed loops and production I/O implementation were unchanged.

Results are median load throughput across five A/B pairs per payload. Each trial’s throughput is measured payload bytes divided by total measured I/O time.

| Payload | Ordinary io_uring (MiB/s) | Fixed buffers (MiB/s) | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 KiB | 4725.8 | 5028.4 | +6.4% |
| 512 KiB | 5750.4 | 8676.5 | +50.9% |
| 1 MiB | 6999.9 | 8485.3 | +21.2% |
| 2 MiB | 6663.0 | 9260.4 | +39.0% |
| 4 MiB | 6186.2 | 9555.5 | +54.5% |
| 8 MiB | 7077.2 | 9317.5 | +31.7% |
| 16 MiB | 7682.4 | 9108.9 | +18.6% |
| 32 MiB | 8085.9 | 9146.9 | +13.1% |

Fixed buffers primarily benefited **loads** in this benchmark. Store throughput improved only **0.4–2.8% at 512 KiB–8 MiB**, was essentially unchanged at **16–32 MiB**, and regressed **4.5% at 256 KiB**.

**Setup and validation**

- Raw-block backend with `O_DIRECT`, regular io_uring, and `enable_zero_copy=true` in both modes.
- 32 keys per submission, eight in-flight submissions, eight load workers, and io_uring queue depth 256.
- Fixed mode used the L1 descriptor’s startup registration snapshot. Ordinary mode changed only `stable_registration_size` to `None`. Registration was verified as **20 GiB versus zero** in every run.
- Both modes completed lazy growth and CUDA registration of the full 100 GiB before warmup. Initialization, registration, growth, and buffer initialization/reset were outside I/O timing.
- Each trial ran in a fresh process. Mode and payload order alternated between pairs. All 80 trials passed data verification and completion checks; fixed-buffer loads were faster in all 40 paired comparisons.

**Scope:** Backing memory was allocated once per trial and reused across rounds. The largest combined store/load allocation was 16 GiB, entirely within the initial 20 GiB registered prefix. These results demonstrate steady-state load benefits with already-populated, CUDA-registered memory; they do not measure allocation churn, I/O outside the registered prefix, or end-to-end MP server performance.
